title: Rewrite tools/extract.py on poppler; re-extract all three docs
description:
poppler-utils replaces xberg in requirements.txt.

KEEP (load-bearing): sorted output, canonical JSON, atomic writes, clean_output of stale files before writing, and the rule that Python never reads data/sources.yaml (two parties recording the sha256 independently is a real check).

DROP (xberg shape): xberg_version, config, config_sha256, table_count, pages_with_tables, NORMALIZER_VERSION.

NEW ANSWER NEEDED: poppler has no structured error channel. It writes 'Syntax Warning: Bad annotation destination' to stderr and exits 0. Record the poppler version and captured stderr per document; do not claim manifest.errors works as before.

PUBLISH PAGE TEXT AS .txt NOT .md: GitHub renders .md in the blob view and collapses the runs of spaces that ARE the grid, which would silently break the provenance deep links fisc-gxa.5 depends on. Carry the rename through corpus.go:217, export/page.go:311, site/app.js:282, export_test.go:197, and the now-false comments at corpus.go:219 and rule.go:30.
close_reason: extract.py rewritten on poppler 24.02.0, stdlib only. All 786 pages re-extracted; byte-identical across runs, locales, and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH/PYTHONHASHSEED. Determinism verified by a third party on an independent re-run. schema_version bumped to 2 on both sides after review found that leaving it at 1 made a broken reader SILENT: Open() succeeded, then Page(n) returned ErrNotFound, which corpus.go documents as the normal 'no such page' case. Bumping it surfaced a real latent bug -- corpus.SchemaVersion was validating both the manifest and each table JSON, two independent contracts sharing one constant. poppler has no structured error channel; stderr is captured per invocation and the docstring says plainly that an empty errors list is not a promise every page came out whole.

title: Column-position guard in the resolver
description:
With geometry available, a value must fall within its column's x-range, derived from the header line. This is the actual payoff of the extractor switch: adopting a layout-preserving extractor and then reading it with a whitespace tokenizer (tokens(), resolve.go:744, which records byte offset only and no column position) throws away the reason for switching.

Without this guard the sparse pages produce plausible wrong values rather than errors.
acceptance_criteria: a row whose 2nd column is blank and 3rd carries a figure resolves the figure to column 3 or fails closed -- never silently to column 2; CIP p40 PB200654 fails closed naming the row
notes:
2026-08-18 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AMENDED. The original read, verbatim:

  "a row whose 2nd column is blank and 3rd carries a figure resolves the figure
  to column 3 or fails closed -- never silently to column 2; CIP p40 PB200654
  reads correctly"

The last clause is unmeetable and this bead's own notes already said why: six of
PB200654's eight cells print a "-" that is in NO substrate, because they are
drawn as non-text. No column guard recovers a mark the PDF never wrote. Closing
on "reads correctly" would have published a false claim, so the clause moved to
fisc-8ln (whose AC lost its "or fails closed" escape in the same edit, or the
obligation would have belonged to no open bead).

The first clause is met in its fails-closed branch, which is the only branch this
lane can demonstrate: geometry is a pure CROSS-CHECK here and never selects which
tokens a row consumes, so a blank cell yields a refusal rather than a correctly
placed figure. "Resolves the figure to column 3" needs band-driven selection,
which is filed with the sparse relaxation.

WHAT LANDED, in six commits: internal/geom (leaf, stdlib only); corpus.Doc.Geometry;
the doc interface at three methods; the verbatim-copy fixture tables generalised
to {document, artifact} over both substrates; column_headers on Part with per-part,
per-page and cross-file validation; the guard itself in internal/mapping/geometry.go;
and column_headers on all ten published spine parts.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE DESIGN ON THIS BEAD, each with its evidence:

(1) The count guard was NOT relaxed. The design said geometry "NECESSARILY
relaxes" positionalValues' exact len(toks) == ExpectedValues. That is true of
SPARSE pages and no mapped part is sparse: p66's data lines carry four value
words each and p67's carry eight, on all 24 of them, dashes included. Relaxing
would have traded the guard that caught fisc-c00 for a replacement exercised only
by the dense pages that never needed it.

(2) The gutter is the FIRST COLUMN HEADER'S x0, not the midpoint to the label
header. The design's own counterexamples refute the design: CIP p40's wrap word
"and" ends at 228.6 and CIP p29's "REVITILIZATION" at 234.85, both RIGHT of the
midpoints (213.16 and 218.67), so both would have filed into band 0. First-header-x0
(238.87 and 245.10) excludes them and keeps every real value, including the bare
leading "$" glyphs. Clearances are thin on CIP and are recorded in the code:
9.46pt left and 3.81pt right on p40.

(3) No column_headers_ordinal. The full ordered header sequence occurs exactly
once page-wide on 66, 67, 127, 128-140, 167, 168, 169, 170, CIP 40 and CIP 29 --
with zero unconsumed words right of the first match on every one. Shipping five
validation branches and a selection branch that no fixture can reach, inside the
guard everything else is about to trust, was the worse trade. Ambiguity is a
refusal naming the candidate lines. Filed for when a page forces it.

(4) No geom.ErrNoGeometry sentinel. corpus.ErrNotFound already means "the
manifest does not list this artifact", and a second sentinel would have put the
artifact reader's vocabulary in the leaf that exists so mapping need not import it.

(5) Substrate agreement is BYTE equality, not the design's "normalized text".
Normalizing would paper over a genuine disagreement, and the point of a second
witness is that it is allowed to disagree.

MEASUREMENTS THE DESIGN GOT WRONG, corrected here:

- Filing by header overlap misfiles 19-30 "on the mapped pages" -- it misfiles
  ZERO on pp.66/67. Over the eight measured pages the two rules disagree on 24
  tokens: 19 zero dashes (p127, p167, p168, p169, CIP p40), 2 bare "$" glyphs and
  3 footer tokens. The doc comment and TestOverlapFilingLosesZeroDashes carry the
  corrected figure.
- The line-grouping 1:1 with -layout is NOT a corpus property. It fails on 124 of
  786 pages, and 99 more fail token agreement. No page in current or near-term
  scope fails either, and the guard refuses the rest rather than reading them
  approximately. Do not write a corpus-wide assertion of it; it is false.
- p67 has 33 non-blank lines but 24 DATA lines.

fisc-j5p's hypothesis was disproved and is recorded on that bead.
close_reason:
The column guard is live over the published citywide spine, and all 240 facts and
facts/facts.jsonl are byte-identical with it on -- what changed is what is
checked, not what is published.

Six commits: internal/geom (leaf, stdlib only, the -bbox reader and the band
model); corpus.Doc.Geometry; the mapping doc interface at three methods, with the
argument for a required method over a type assertion written down; both
verbatim-copy fixture tests generalised to {document, artifact} tables over both
substrates; column_headers on Part with per-part, per-page and cross-file
validation; the guard in internal/mapping/geometry.go; column_headers on all ten
published spine parts; and the CIP p29/p40 tests.

Evidence: spineFacts 240 and spineTiedColumns 24 with the guard on, every balance
identity and headline figure unmoved, facts.jsonl and sankey.golden.json
byte-identical, fisc verify 19 passed 0 failed.

The guard is not inert, and that is asserted rather than hoped: a rule that names
only the last three of p66's four printed headers is refused naming the row, the
token, its x-position and the column the page actually prints it in; a header pair
in the wrong order is refused as an order claim; a part one column short of the
page is refused because the header line carries a header no column claims; and a
one-column part whose two rows were fused onto one printed line is caught by the
line count, which is the case no other check can see.

AC amended and the original preserved in the notes above, along with the five
deviations from the design and the three measurements on this bead that turned
out to be wrong. Follow-ups filed: fisc-gmx (substrate disagreement, 223 of 786
pages), band-driven selection with the sparse count relaxation, StatedTotals'
substrate inconsistency, column_headers_ordinal, and the two-grid page.

title: Emit both -layout text and -bbox geometry
description:
pdftotext -layout alone CANNOT distinguish an empty cell from an absent one: on a sparse wide grid a blank cell yields no token at all. CIP p40 row PB200654 prints two figures with six blanks between and -layout gives exactly two tokens. labelledValues takes toks[:ncols] (resolve.go:378), so a figure silently lands in the wrong column -- a plausible wrong value, which is what this project fails closed on, and it makes 'absent is not zero' unenforceable. xberg's tables/*.json grid was the only artifact carrying that geometry, and pp.131-140 / pp.167-170 (the Stage 2 targets) are the sparse ones.

-bbox is also the only way to keep one existing claim reproducible: the mapping file justifies its corrected omitted_rows: [] on p67 with 'pdftotext -bbox puts ten revenue rows here at the same ten y-positions' -- the fisc-c00 evidence.

Emit pages/pNNNN.txt (-layout) plus geometry/pNNNN.json (word boxes from -bbox). Strictly more useful than xberg's tables; replaces them rather than sitting beside them.
acceptance_criteria: geometry/pNNNN.json carries per-word text + bbox for every page of all three docs; a sparse-grid page (CIP p40) can be read column-correctly using it
notes: 2026-08-18 CORRECTION, from peer review of the landing plan. This bead's premise that pp.131-140 and pp.167-170 'are the sparse ones' is measurably FALSE. All 18 pages in that scope were checked against the emitted -bbox geometry: every data row carries exactly 4 value tokens, with '-' printed in every zero cell. They are uniformly dense. The -bbox substrate and the column guard built on it (fisc-yqv.2) are therefore not justified by any page currently in scope -- the poppler migration itself (fisc-yqv.3) IS, and demonstrably worked (p130 recovered 13 rows xberg lost). Recording the distinction so the guard's cost is not retro-justified by the extractor's success.
close_reason: Emits pages/pNNNN.txt (-layout) + geometry/pNNNN.json (-bbox word boxes), replacing tables/. Geometry verified sufficient for column identity: CIP p40 PB202617's lone 500,000 at x=391.1 sits under FY 2026-27 (369.9-418.9), where a whitespace read would have filed it under FY 2024-25. Word encoding flattened to [x0,y0,x1,y1,text] after review: 18.7 -> 8.2 MiB, 41.3 bytes/word. Geometry does NOT recover a value absent from the text layer -- see fisc-8ln.

title: [epic] E0 Extraction replacement: pdftotext replaces xberg
description:
The committed xberg artifacts have silently lost data rows on exactly the pages the POC needs: PDF p167 prints a ~40-line department x object grid and pages/p0167.md retains 7; p130 prints 13 Miscellaneous Revenue detail rows and p0130.md retains 0. This is the fisc-c00 failure class, and Part.OmittedRows' doc comment forbids absorbing it in a rule -- if rows go missing between the PDF and the artifact, fix extraction.

A scratch migration replacing all 786 pages with pdftotext -layout output confirmed: all 240 spine facts reproduce with identical amount_cents AND identical ids, sankey.json matches the golden except its build stamp, all 24 columns still tie, every headline control total re-derives, output is byte-identical across runs and locales. Of 583 grouped-value tokens xberg produced that -layout does not, every one is an xberg corruption (dash-glued negatives, split digits, a lost decimal).

Ends with all three docs re-extracted, the spine re-anchored, and the money proven identical cell by cell.
close_reason: E0 complete, 6/6. pdftotext -layout plus -bbox geometry replaced xberg across all three documents; the spine was re-anchored (7 edits across 5 of 10 parts); the table substrate and markdown residue are gone. Verified in peer review of the landing plan that the rewrite did what it was for: p130's 13 Miscellaneous Revenue rows, of which xberg retained 0, are all present in the poppler artifact. One correction recorded on fisc-yqv.1: its premise that pp.131-140 and 167-170 'are the sparse ones' is measurably false -- all 18 pages carry exactly 4 value tokens per row.

title: StatedTotals cannot read a totals row glued to the next data row
description:
Budget Book p67's expenditure totals cannot be read. The extracted page puts the TOTAL EXPENDITURES row and the TRANSFER OUT row on ONE physical line:

  ... 1,070,500 1,115,510 $1,061,355 $969,934 $6,984,597 $6,969,898 $19,267,561 $11,808,000 $25,077,367 $26,544,515 28,584,740 36,047,736 - - 1,137,050 900,550 40,000 612,000

StatedTotals anchors a label-less part on stop_at ('$') and asks amountRun for the first MAXIMAL run of exactly len(columns) parsable amounts within that line. Sixteen amounts follow the anchor -- the 8 totals plus the 8 transfer-out figures -- so the maximal run is 16, never 8, and the read fails with ErrNotFound.

That is indistinguishable from 'the totals row moved', which is a genuine hard failure, so it cannot be waved through. p67's revenue totals (line 15) and total-sources (line 17) each have exactly 8 amounts after their anchor, which is why only this one part fails.

The document already distinguishes the two rows typographically: totals rows are $-prefixed and data rows are bare. internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml relies on that convention already ('the totals row is the first line whose figures are prefixed with $ -- every data row above it is bare'). The resolver does not use it.
design:
In amountRun, when a maximal run is not the wanted length AND the run begins with a $-prefixed token, also consider that run's $-prefixed PREFIX. Return it if it is exactly the wanted length.

Deliberately additive: the existing maximal-run result is computed first and preferred, so a line the resolver reads today reads identically. The new branch can only turn a failure into a success. That rules out a regression on the pages where totals are only partially $-marked, which fail closed as before.
acceptance_criteria: p67's spine-expenditures part ties its 8 column totals; p66's labelled totals and p67's revenue totals are unchanged; a line whose $-prefixed prefix is the wrong width still fails.
close_reason: Fixed: amountRun considers a run's $-prefixed prefix when the maximal run is the wrong width. Deliberately additive -- the maximal run is computed and preferred first, so every line that read before reads identically and the new branch can only turn a failure into a success. p67 spine-expenditures now ties its 8 columns; the spine ties 24 of 24. Regression test TestCurrencyMarkedTotalsRunSurvivesAGluedDataRow covers the glued line, a wrong-width $-prefix, and an unchanged bare run.

title: Extraction dropped a data row: xberg strip_repeating_text eats identical rows
description:
Budget Book PDF p67 prints TEN revenue rows; data/extracted/.../pages/p0067.md carried only NINE (72 tokens where 10 rows x 8 columns = 80). Verified with 'pdftotext -bbox -f 67 -l 67': p67's revenue rows sit at y = 194, 210, 226, 241, 257, 273, 289, 304, 320, 336 -- the SAME ten y-positions as p66's ten labelled rows. The document omits nothing.

Rows 8-10 (Sales Taxes, Fines & Forfeitures, Licenses & Permits) are three consecutive all-dash lines. xberg's content_filter.strip_repeating_text defaults to true; it is a header/footer dedup heuristic and it treated the third identical DATA row as repeating boilerplate. Setting content_filter.strip_repeating_text=false restores all three (80 tokens, verified).

This matters far beyond one row. The project had recorded the loss as a property of the DOCUMENT -- docs/m0-spike.md finding #4, the omitted_rows comment in internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml, the OmittedRows doc comment in internal/mapping/rule.go, and fisc-mq4.7's own description all say p67 'omits' an all-zero row. It does not. Declaring it via Part.OmittedRows ('rows absent from THIS part') would launder a pipeline defect into a permanent published assertion about the City's budget, and row_label is inside fact.MakeID, so the affected facts would carry a coin-flip label.

The resolver's positional count guard (internal/mapping/resolve.go positionalValues) was CORRECTLY firing. It is the only reason this was caught.
design: Add content_filter: {strip_repeating_text: false} to CONFIG in tools/extract.py and bump EXTRACTOR_VERSION. CONFIG is hashed into manifest.config_sha256, so the change is attributable. Review the full-corpus artifact diff before committing: strip_repeating_text is a global heuristic and any other page it was silently editing will also change. include_headers/include_footers stay false and are separate knobs.
acceptance_criteria: p0067.md revenue block tokenizes to 80 between the 4th 'FY 2026-27' and the first '$'; omitted_rows disappears from the spine rule entirely; the four places that record the false premise are corrected; artifact diff outside the affected pages is reviewed and explained.
close_reason: Fixed in 6806ec7: content_filter.strip_repeating_text=False, EXTRACTOR_VERSION=2, corpus regenerated. p67 revenue block is 80 tokens (10 rows x 8). Zero numeric tokens lost corpus-wide; 326 pages gained restored content. Four records of the false premise corrected (m0-spike.md, testdata/spine.yaml, rule.go OmittedRows doc, testdata/README.md) plus this bead's parent fisc-mq4.7. Regression guard: TestExtractionDropOutIsNotAnOmission.

title: Rebuild-and-diff facts.jsonl in CI
description: CI runs 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)' and byte-compares the result against the committed facts.jsonl. Without this, a hand-edited facts.jsonl passes CI and the deployed site is built from different numbers than the audit trail -- the one thing a provenance gate must prevent. Pure Go, so it costs nothing and preserves the no-LFS-in-CI property.
notes: 2026-08-17 IMPLEMENTATION DEVIATION, deliberate: the description says 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)', which the tool refuses by design -- --output is resolved against the repository root and validateRepoPath (pkg/cmd/build/build.go:130) rejects absolute paths. The CI job builds to bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl instead (bin/ is gitignored and make clean already owns it, so the rebuild leaves the tree exactly as checked out) and compares with cmp, not 'git diff --exit-code'. cmp because git diff compares through the .gitattributes 'text eol=lf' clean filter rather than the bytes, and because the git diff form would leave the committed fact store overwritten in the workspace on failure. Recorded so the next reader does not 'fix' it back toward the description.
close_reason: The facts job rebuilds to bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl and byte-compares with cmp against the committed facts/facts.jsonl. Deviation from the description's literal 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)' recorded in the notes -- the tool refuses absolute output paths by design.

title: Structural checks: drift, cell relocation, dropped column
description:
- artifact drift: any data/extracted file whose sha256 differs from its manifest entry; any manifest whose source_sha256 differs from the registry; any manifest whose xberg_version differs from the pin
- registry drift (--full only): recomputed PDF sha256 vs sources.yaml
- CELL RELOCATION: independently re-resolve each fact by row_path + column_path and assert the resolved position equals the recorded one. This REPLACES a check that was tautological in an earlier draft -- hashing content and then asserting the content matched can never fail independently. A mismatch means the table shifted, which is precisely the event nothing else detects.
- dropped-column detection: if a page's text has a longer numeric run on a mapped row's label line than the table has columns, fail with 'possible dropped column' (ACFR p34 loses a column silently)

Default verify needs NO PDFs and NO Python; --full adds registry drift and runs monthly with lfs: true.
notes:
ALSO: cross-language normalizer agreement. internal/amount.Normalize must produce the same output as normalize_cell in tools/extract.py, because the committed artifacts hash normalized text with the Python one and a Go reader that normalized differently would compute different hashes for identical content.

One divergence is known and deliberate: extract.py applies Unicode NFKC, Go does not (that would mean a golang.org/x/text dependency, byob-release.10, for a transform that changes nothing in this corpus -- all 382 committed tables hash identically either way). This check is what catches it if that stops being true. The Go doc comment on Normalize cites this bead.
2026-08-17 THE CROSS-LANGUAGE NORMALIZE CHECK IS MOOT. This bead's note asks for 'cross-language normalizer agreement: internal/amount.Normalize must produce the same output as normalize_cell in tools/extract.py, because the committed artifacts hash normalized text with the Python one.' That premise died with the poppler migration (fisc-yqv.3): normalize_cell no longer exists, and tools/extract.py now writes raw 'pdftotext -layout' bytes plus -bbox geometry with NO cell normalization anywhere. The manifest hashes those raw bytes, so there is no Python normalizer for Go to agree with and nothing for the check to compare. Same staleness class as fisc-9lp.

The underlying worry is still real but has moved: amount.Normalize is now the ONLY normalizer in the pipeline, applied on the Go side at parse time, so a change to it changes what parses without changing any artifact hash. That is a unit-test concern (internal/amount already has TestNormalizeUnifiesDashes) rather than a cross-language one. The deliberate NFKC divergence the note mentions no longer exists either, because the Python side does no NFKC.

Dropped from the A4 lane rather than built. Also dropped: 'any manifest whose xberg_version differs from the pin' -- the field is extractor_version (currently 3) plus poppler_version ('24.02.0'), and both are checked.
2026-08-17 LANE A4 LANDED (uncommitted in the main tree; not closed -- the remainder is fisc-1wr.5.1). Four tier-0 structural checks in internal/check/structural.go, first in All()'s order:

artifacts-match-manifest -- hashes all 1572 files under data/extracted/ against the sha256 and bytes their manifest records, BOTH directions: changed bytes, a listed file that is gone, and a present file the manifest does not list. manifest.json is excluded (it cannot hash itself) and that is documented.
manifest-matches-source-registry -- each manifest's source_sha256/source_bytes/source_file against data/sources.yaml, plus the two document-id sets being the same set (a source with no extraction, an extraction with no source). No PDF: two independently written claims.
extraction-toolchain-pinned -- extractor_version and poppler_version against corpus.PinnedExtractorVersion (3) and PinnedPopplerVersion ('24.02.0'). Mutual agreement between the three docs is NOT separately asserted: each is compared to one constant, so agreement follows and a second finding would be a consequence of the first. schema_version stays gated in corpus.Open (a load failure, not a finding) because at another schema the artifact namespace itself differs.
source-pdfs-match-both-records (Full) -- the FIRST check with Full()==true, so StatusSkipped is now reachable end to end. Recomputes each data/pdf sha256 and compares against BOTH sources.yaml and the manifest. Three states, told apart: wrong bytes = FAIL (a claim about the corpus); an unsmudged Git LFS pointer or an absent file = ERROR naming the file and carrying 'git lfs pull' inline in the message (a claim about the checkout; the hint is inline because ErrHint.Error() drops it and a check's error becomes the report Summary). A pointer's oid is compared to the registry so the report says whether fetching would even reconcile the tree.

WHERE THE PIN LIVES: internal/corpus, beside SchemaVersion, as PinnedExtractorVersion/PinnedPopplerVersion. Not requirements.txt: that file is prose no Go code reads and says in as many words that poppler 'is not pinned the way a pip requirement would be'. requirements.txt now cross-references the Go constants.

New: cmdutil.ExtractedDir (corpus's private const promoted); corpus.ManifestFile, Artifacts() (replacing ArtifactPaths/Artifact), Tree(), SourceFile/SourceBytes/ExtractorVersion/PopplerVersion; registry.LoadSources + Source (strict, schema-gated, the first Go reader of the whole sources.yaml); Subject.Extractions/Sources/SourcePDFs, and Load hashes data/pdf only under Full.

Every check proven failable by mutating a file on disk (internal/check/structural_test.go, 12 mutation tests + the four --full states). Verified by neutering all four checks at once: exactly those 12 tests go red. No test needs Python, the network, or the LFS files -- the --full tests synthesize their own tiny source documents and rewrite the registry and manifests to match.

Default verify still needs no PDFs: 17 pass, 5 vacuous, 1 SKIPPED with its reason, exit 0. --full: 18 pass, exit 0. CI needed no change (confirmed: the default run over a tree with a deleted PDF still exits 0); ci.yml's header note now records that --full exists and that scheduling it is fisc-gxa.5's. Also fixed a grammar bug the lane made reachable: 'N check need --full'.

NOT built, per the scope change already on this bead: cross-language Normalize agreement (moot), cell relocation and dropped-column (fisc-1wr.5.1).
2026-08-17 ROUND 2, after peer review. Blocker and all five must/should-fixes addressed; still uncommitted, still not closed.

BLOCKER (the artifact map was checked for consistency and never for completeness) -- two new tier-0 checks, and fisc-6r5 folded in:

title: Map the p66-67 spine only: all-funds control totals
description:
PROVEN: 136 facts map cleanly from Budget Book PDF pp.66-67 and all 16 column totals tie EXACTLY to the document's own printed totals (General Fund FY2025-26 expenditures $144,650,802; all-funds FY2025-26 revenues $299,969,007).

Structure: rows are 'label followed by N numbers'. p66 carries the labels and the General Fund + Enterprise columns (4 values per row). p67 carries Capital, Debt Service, Special Revenue and Internal Service (8 values per row) with NO labels -- identity is positional from p66.

CORRECTED (fisc-c00): this bead used to say p67 OMITS the all-zero 'Licenses & Permits' row and that the omission must be declared. That was wrong. pdftotext -bbox shows p67 printing all ten revenue rows at the same ten y-positions as p66's ten labelled rows; our extractor was deleting one of three identical all-dash rows. p67 declares NO omitted_rows. The M0 spike's 136 was 128 real values plus 8 invented zeros; the 136 now is 136 real printed cells.

Build the Sankey skeleton from the spine FIRST so the balance checks exist before the detail does. A working reference implementation is in docs/m0-spike/spine.py -- note it maps revenues only from p67 and skips that page's expenditure block.
close_reason: mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml: 5 rules, 10 parts, 240 facts. All 24 columns with a printed total tie exactly; the other six parts are covered by the balance identity, which reconciles all six fund groups in both years against the city's own TOTAL SOURCES and TOTAL USES.

title: fisc build emitting facts.jsonl
description: Options struct + NewCmdBuild(f, runF) + private buildRun per byob-command-shape.1; Options.Validate() first, failing with FlagErrorf before any side effects (byob-input-validation.5).

title: Fact model: content-addressed IDs, specified total order
description:
ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, deliberately EXCLUDING amount_cents and any row/col index -- so a corrected amount is a modified line rather than delete+add, and an upstream row insertion does not renumber the file. An ID collision is a hard build error: two rules claiming the same cell is a real bug.

facts.jsonl total order: (doc_id, page, row_path, column_path, rule_id). Struct-based emission with fixed key order, no omitempty, LF, trailing newline, .gitattributes text eol=lf. verify checks the file is sorted, which catches nondeterminism in CI for free.
close_reason: internal/fact. ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|row_label|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, unit-separator joined so component boundaries cannot shift. row_label is in the tuple because row_path is NOT unique within a rule: p127 prints 13 detail lines all classified taxes/property, and taxonomy.yaml is explicit those are a label not a category -- review caught the collision and it is now a test. Excludes amount and any index, so a corrected figure is a modified line and an inserted row renumbers nothing. Order is the specified (doc_id,page,row_path,column_path,rule_id) EXTENDED by (fiscal_year,basis,id): the specified five tie for two columns of one schedule, and a non-total order defeats the sortedness check it exists to enable. Declared omissions do NOT become facts -- absent is not zero -- so the spine is 128 published facts plus 8 declared absences. amount_cents is always as-printed and sign is presentation, never an instruction to negate.

title: Locator resolution + ambiguity errors listing candidates
description:
Locator = identity, content-INDEPENDENT. For text: {page, section, row_label, ordinal}. For tables: {page, ordinal_on_page, label_fingerprint, bbox_centroid} where label_fingerprint hashes only non-numeric tokens (strip [0-9,.$()%-]) and the centroid rounds to ~10pt.

Why this is separate from the integrity hash: 16 ACFR tables are byte-identical duplicates of another (one 12-way group across pp.12-23; the Budget Book has a 20-way group), so a content hash is NOT an identity. Resolution must require a unique best match; ambiguity or no-match is a hard error printing the top three candidates with their pages and first rows, via ErrHint (byob-errors.2).
notes:
NEXT STEP after fisc-mq4.1 (rule schema, landed). internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml is a working target: the M0 spike proved 136 facts come out of Budget Book pp.66-67 with all 16 column totals tying EXACTLY to the totals the document prints (General Fund FY2025-26 expenditures $144,650,802; all-funds FY2025-26 revenues $299,969,007). A reference implementation is committed at docs/m0-spike/spine.py.

Rule.ExpectedValues(part) is the count a positional read must find -- 72 on p67, not 80, because the all-zero Licenses & Permits row is omitted. A mismatch must be a hard error naming the page, never a best-effort read.
close_reason: Resolver lands in internal/mapping/resolve.go with internal/corpus as the artifact reader. Text locator is {page, section, section_ordinal, stop_at}; ordinal is mandatory because REVENUES:/EXPENDITURES: each occur twice on p66. Table locator is {ordinal, label_fingerprint, bbox_centroid}, and a (page,ordinal) miss is always ErrNotFound -- never a fingerprint search that resolves elsewhere, since ACFR p12/p13 are identical in fingerprint, content hash AND bbox. Ambiguity/not-found list up to 3 candidates with line and context via ErrHint. Proven: 128 values from pp.66-67, 16/16 column totals tie exactly.

title: Rule schema + parser (substrate: text|table|manual)
description:
Page text is the PRIMARY substrate: tables miss 46% of the Budget Book's money pages, including the spine (p66-67), the transfer schedule (p76), and revenue-by-fund (p127-140). Typed string enums, not iota, for anything crossing YAML/JSON (byob-typed-string-enums-sql).

M0 spike findings that the schema MUST accommodate:
 - a logical table can span pages, and the continuation page may carry NO row labels at all (p67 is a positional continuation of p66)
 - the continuation page OMITS rows that are all-zero across its columns, so a naive positional zip silently shifts every label after the gap. Rules need an explicit omitted_rows declaration plus a row-count assertion that fails loudly on mismatch.
 - column identity is (fund_group, fiscal_year), addressed by a column_path, not by a single header string (headers span two rows and Table.columns is always empty)
close_reason: Rule schema + parser landed with review fixes. Schema expresses the spine's label-less continuation and omitted rows; validation rejects duplicate columns, multi-document files, unclassified rows and circular block anchors.

title: tools/extract.py with a deterministic serializer
description:
Standalone Python run via 'make extract' -- Go NEVER shells out to it, so there is no embedded script and no exception to the pure-Go rule (byob-release.8).

Config verified to work offline with no model download:
  {use_cache: False, disable_ocr: True, output_format: 'markdown',
   pages: {extract_pages: True}, pdf_options: {extract_tables: True, extract_metadata: True}}

Determinism requirements (these are what make committed artifacts stable):
 - sort tables by (page_number, y0, x0); do NOT trust doc.tables order (ACFR p34 emits one logical table as three fragments in REVERSE document order)
 - format floats %.2f; sort_keys=True; fixed indent; ensure_ascii=False; LF; trailing newline
 - record n_cols per table and the page-text line each row came from
 - do NOT treat processing_warnings as a quality signal: it was empty on both documents despite a silently dropped column

Emit pages/pNNNN.md (the PRIMARY substrate) and tables/pNNNN-tNN.json.

title: internal/amount: strict fail-closed grammar + case table
description:
The most bug-prone code in the project; lands BEFORE any mapping rule exists.

Observed corruption modes that must be REJECTED or handled explicitly:
 1. digits split by whitespace: '2 40,000' for 240,000 (CIP p40) -- REJECT
 2. em-dash-as-zero glued to the next column: ACFR p54 '48,030,349 | -1,315,352 | 49,345,701' where the true reading is +1,315,352 -- REJECT a leading '-' not preceded by a column boundary
 3. '$' bleeding one cell right: p68 ['Wastewater $ ', '27,799,694 $ ', ...] -- strip orphaned $
 4. parenthesis negatives: '(71.8)' -- negative
 5. '-' means zero; '' means ABSENT -- different meanings, both occur, must not be conflated
 6. units vary (dollars/thousands/millions) and come from the rule, not the token
 7. NEW from the M0 spike: '\\-' (backslash-escaped dash) appears in the extracted markdown as a distinct zero token

Amounts are integer cents, never float. Table-driven tests with google/go-cmp per byob-testing.2, in the same commit per byob-testing.4.
close_reason: internal/amount landed: strict fail-closed grammar, all 7 corruption modes, corpus-validated. Confirmed the glued-dash corruption independently on ACFR p177 by row arithmetic.

title: A graph document with no headline has no path through the packager, and fisc-gkv says the drill-down must have none
description:
fisc-gkv point C decided the finest-grain graph is 'a SECOND Projection type with its own key, its own document, and NO headline'. internal/export cannot express that, and the failure is not a blank space on a page -- it is the whole export.

MEASURED. decodeSankey (internal/export/page.go) refuses a document with no fiscal_year_label and refuses one whose headline all_funds_gross_expenditure_cents is zero. buildSite dispatches 'case TrendsTemplate: buildTrendsPage; default: buildSankeyPage', and buildSankeyPage calls decodeSankey for the opening document and again for every year stem. The error propagates out through Write, so fisc export dies having written NOTHING.

views() DOES NOT SAVE IT. The drop of a view whose document was not built fires only when the stem is ABSENT from the projections map. A drill-down builds fine, so the view is present and the refusal is reached.

AND GIVING IT A HEADLINE IS NOT THE CHEAP WAY OUT. headline-ties-to-facts and headline-transfer-residual both iterate Subject.Graphs() and read Metadata.Headline unconditionally. A revenue-side drill-down has transfers IN and no transfers out, so transfer_residual_cents would publish -21,045,597 and headlineTransferResidual would pass it GREEN -- the figure is the sum of the facts, and the facts are only one leg. A published number that is arithmetically correct and means nothing.

(headline-naive-expenditure is safe: it already skips a graph with no transfers out and no internal-service expenditure gap.)

TWO MORE PACKAGER FACTS IN THE WAY, both measured: View.validate refuses a Lede on any non-TrendsTemplate view, so a drill-down on SankeyTemplate cannot carry its explanatory sentence; and page.go's footer-scope comment argues the scope is not repainted 'because Sankey.Slices fixes it', which a second Sankey-template view at another scope makes false, along with the template's own 'all funds, gross' lede.

SO THE MINIMUM IS A DOCUMENT SHAPE, NOT A PACKAGER TWEAK: a headline-less graph, its own template, its own arm in the shape dispatch, and structural checks that do not assume a headline. That is the piece fisc-gxa.2 does not size, and it is why the drill-down should be planned against it rather than into it.

Found in peer review of a landing plan, 2026-08-27.
acceptance_criteria: a graph document carrying no headline is packaged into a page without fisc export refusing; no headline check reads a figure from a document that does not publish one; the drill-down's lede reaches its page
notes:
2026-08-27 HALF LANDED IN 09cc87d, and it is the half that was a live defect rather than a missing feature.

buildSite's dispatch was 'case TrendsTemplate: ... default: buildSankeyPage', so any template with no arm -- including one that EXISTS in the asset tree -- was handed pageData and rendered as a spine. Measured: with a third template in the tree and a view on it, Write returned NIL and shipped a page of blanks. Every template is now an explicit arm and an unknown one is refused by name.

And a second defect this bead did not name: buildSite collected citations by walking VIEWS, so a projection written to data/<stem>.json with no page contributed none and the pages its metadata.sources names were absent from dist/extracted/. That is the state the drill-down ships in between the commit that builds it and fisc-f75. Citations are now collected over every published projection.

STILL OPEN, and it is this bead's actual subject: the headline-less document SHAPE. decodeSankey's headline refusal is view-gated -- reached only from buildSankeyPage, only via a registered View -- so it does not bite until the drill-down gets a page. What does bite sooner is internal/check: graphBuilder returns *project.Graph, whose Metadata has headline as a required key, so a headline-less document cannot satisfy it and must not be given a zeroed one (this bead's own measurement: transfer_residual_cents would publish -21,045,597 and headlineTransferResidual would pass it green). That is the Subject.Linked() work.
close_reason:
Landed across 09cc87d and d876984. A graph document carrying no headline is now packaged and checked, and no headline check reads a figure from a document that does not publish one.

THE ANSWER IS NOT THE ONE THIS BEAD SIZED. It reasoned from decodeSankey, and decodeSankey is VIEW-GATED: reached only from buildSankeyPage, only via a registered View. So at the drill-down current stopping point -- data/*.json published, no page -- the headline refusal never runs, and "fisc export dies having written NOTHING" does not happen. The refusal becomes blocking when fisc-f75 gives the document a page, and the split of decodeSankeys two refusals is left to that commit rather than done speculatively here.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BLOCKING was internal/check, which this bead did not name: graphBuilder returns *project.Graph, whose Metadata has headline as a required key, so a headline-less document could not satisfy it and must not be given a zeroed one -- this bead own measurement, -21,045,597 published green. Subject.Linked is the fix: the six structural checks read every document made of nodes and links, the three headline checks read the documents whose TYPE publishes one. Structural predicate, never a value test, or a spine whose headline was zeroed would go green over what remained.

TWO DEFECTS THIS BEAD DID NOT NAME WERE FIXED IN 09cc87d. buildSite dispatch was "default: buildSankeyPage", so any template with no arm -- including one that exists in the asset tree -- rendered as a spine; measured, Write returned NIL and shipped a page of blanks. And citations were collected per VIEW, so an unviewed projection cited pages dist/extracted/ did not carry.

STILL OPEN AND NOW OWNED BY fisc-f75: View.validates Lede allow-list, the footer-scope guard for a second Sankey-template view, and the drill-down own template.

title: The year toggle's async lifecycle: a click during the first fetch kills Escape and theme-following
description:
Three defects in the year toggle's async lifecycle, all landed in 9444126 and all found by /code-review of the revenue-trends wave (2026-08-25). They are filed rather than folded into that wave because they are pre-existing and belong to app.js, not to the producer.

(1) A CLICK DURING THE FIRST FETCH KILLS THE PAGE'S KEYBOARD AND THEME LISTENERS. main() (site/app.js:1183) runs

    wireYears(years);
    if (!await showYear(years[0])) return;
    document.addEventListener("keydown", ...)      // Escape
    window.matchMedia(...).addEventListener("change", paint)

wireYears enables the radio group BEFORE the opening year is drawn, so a reader who clicks the other year while the first fetch is in flight bumps `switching`, the opening showYear returns false at its token guard, and main() RETURNS. The clicked year still draws -- its own showYear is running -- so the page looks fine, and Escape and OS-theme-following are dead for the rest of the visit. The return exists for the genuine failure case (fetch refused, bad schema) and cannot tell that apart from "superseded", because showYear returns the same false for both.

(2) A SUPERSEDED FETCH REJECTION PASTES A STALE BANNER OVER A GOOD YEAR. Every other exit in showYear guards on `token !== switching` first. The catch around `await fetch` (app.js:1068) does not: it calls fail() unconditionally. So a reader who switches away while a fetch is failing gets the file:// remediation banner -- role="alert" -- over a year that drew correctly.

(3) THE CHANGE HANDLER SWALLOWS REJECTIONS. app.js:1166 is `void showYear(year)` with no .catch, unlike main().catch(...). `await response.json()` is inside no try, so a truncated or malformed document rejects, the promise is unhandled, no banner appears, and the page is left half-repainted.

WHY THESE SURVIVED THE HARNESS: tools/jscheck exercises the toggle's PAINTING -- "painting a second year replaces the first year's words" -- and never a superseded or rejected fetch. The fix wants cases for a click during the opening fetch, a rejected fetch that is then superseded, and a malformed document.

SHAPE OF THE FIX: showYear should distinguish "superseded" from "failed" rather than returning one boolean for both -- main() must not treat being overtaken as a reason to stop wiring the page. The catch needs the same token guard every other exit has, and the change handler needs the .catch main() already has.
acceptance_criteria: clicking the year control during the opening fetch leaves the Escape handler and the prefers-color-scheme listener attached; a superseded fetch rejection paints no banner; a rejected showYear from the change handler surfaces as a banner rather than an unhandled rejection; showYear distinguishes superseded from failed; tools/jscheck covers all three
notes:
2026-08-26 THE HARNESS WORK IS SPLIT OUT TO fisc-dn9, and it is larger than this bead implies.

This bead's 'SHAPE OF THE FIX' ends with 'tools/jscheck covers all three', which
reads as three new cases in year.mjs. Measured, it is not: the runner is fully
synchronous (zero async/await in the whole of tools/jscheck), fetch is
uninjectable after loadApp returns because main() has already run, FISC_CONFIG is
baked in with ONE year so wireYears bails at app.js:1172 and there is no toggle to
click, document- and window-level addEventListener are no-ops, matchMedia is
undefined, and fail()'s banner is unreachable so 'assert no banner' passes against
the fixed and unfixed app.js alike. That last one matters most: it is a check that
cannot fail, which is what this project exists to prevent.

fisc-dn9 owns all five and now blocks this bead. The three cases stay here.

A CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN SHAPE OF THE FIX, from peer review of the landing
plan. 'showYear should distinguish superseded from failed rather than returning one
boolean for both' is necessary and NOT sufficient, and the insufficiency is the
whole of defect (1).

A three-state return rescues the SUPERSEDED branch and leaves an identical bug on
the FAILED one. clearRefusal's own doc comment (app.js:1002-1006) states the
recovery path: 'A year switch can recover from a failed one.' So: the opening
fetch genuinely fails -- file://, HTTP 500, a bad schema_version -- main() returns
at app.js:1197, the Escape and matchMedia wiring is never reached, the reader then
clicks the other year, it succeeds, clearRefusal() at app.js:1088 takes the banner
down and the chart draws. Same healthy-looking page, same two dead affordances,
reached through the state a three-state return leaves alone.

So the fix is to HOIST app.js:1199-1214 above the await -- above wireYears at
:1196, since :1175 enables the control before any await. main() must not treat ANY
fetch outcome as a reason to stop wiring the page. This is safe: paint (app.js:629)
is DOM-only, it selects existing marks and iterates legend buttons and never reads
`projection`, so it is a no-op before the first draw rather than a throw. Checked.

SECOND CORRECTION: the fix for defect (3) reintroduces defect (2) if taken
literally. A bare .catch on `void showYear(year)` (app.js:1180) with no token guard
paints the role=alert banner for a SUPERSEDED response.json() rejection -- the same
false statement over a correct chart that defect (2) is about, through a new path.
Pull `await response.json()` (app.js:1078) inside the try at :1062-1072, guard the
token in the catch, and let the handler's .catch be a last resort only.
close_reason:
All three defects fixed and each part of the fix proven load-bearing on its own.

THE BEAD'S STATED FIX WAS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the finding worth carrying forward. 'showYear should distinguish superseded from failed' rescues the superseded branch and leaves an identical bug on the failed one: clearRefusal exists because 'a year switch can recover from a failed one', so a REFUSED opening fetch also returned out of main(), the reader clicked the other year, it drew, the banner came down, and the same two listeners were dead. The fix is to wire before the first fetch -- main() must not treat ANY fetch outcome as a reason to stop wiring the page. Safe because neither listener depends on a chart existing: paint() is DOM-only over marks that do not yet exist, and Escape clears state already clear. showYear returns DREW/SUPERSEDED/FAILED anyway, because the catch guard needs it and because one boolean for two facts is what caused this.

Second correction, recorded on the bead before landing: a bare .catch on the change handler would have repainted the banner for a SUPERSEDED json() rejection, reintroducing defect (2) through a new path. Both awaits moved inside showYear's try instead; the .catch is a last resort and has its own reachable case (a document that parses and passes the schema gate but has no graph).

Third, found while writing the checks: the SyntaxError arm was selected with instanceof, which compares against this realm's constructor -- dead under the vm, invisible in a browser where the realms coincide. It is e.name now, and a check asserts the wording so the branch cannot go dead again.

Acceptance, each met: clicking during the opening fetch leaves both listeners attached (and a check DISPATCHES Escape, because attached is not working); a superseded rejection paints no banner; a rejected showYear from the change handler surfaces as a banner; showYear distinguishes superseded from failed; tools/jscheck covers all three -- four checks in lifecycle.mjs, all red against the unfixed app.js, and each individually red when its own part of the fix is reverted.

The harness work it needed went to fisc-dn9 and landed first (8a4610a). Landed in 034dfa8.

title: publishedProjectionBuilt knows one published document, and the site now publishes two
description:
publishedProjectionBuilt (internal/check/coverage.go) asserts that every slice the site publishes was actually built, and its own doc comment says why that matters: "a projection that was not built is not a failure anywhere: it is silence. If the fact store no longer carries facts for a published slice, export publishes a chart of nothing while verify reports on whatever other slices happen to exist."

IT KNOWS ABOUT EXACTLY ONE DOCUMENT. It compares against project.PublishedProjection, project.PublishedBasis and project.PublishedScope, iterating project.PublishedFiscalYears(). That was the whole published set until 2026-08-25. It is not any more: revenue-trends is published too, at its own scope, over four columns, and NOTHING asserts it was built.

HOW THE HOLE OPENS. Trends.Slices returns nil when the store carries no revenue-by-fund fact -- a scope typo in a mapping rule does it, which is the exact incident unprojectedScopes exists for. Then pkg/cmd/export builds no document for it, data/revenue-trends.json is not written, and:

  - projections-build counts len(Projections)+len(ProjectionFailures) and sees nothing missing.
  - documents-are-checked counts len(s.Registered) as its denominator, so it would report "1 projection, each read by the structural checks: 1 graph" -- a pass.
  - trend-points-tie-to-facts and trend-series-are-complete both go VACUOUS, and vacuous is not a failure unless --strict, and under --strict it is silenced by a declaration if anyone adds one.
  - facts-are-projected DOES redden, but only because the 924 facts land in no projection and no unprojectedScopes entry declares them -- it reports 924 findings about facts, not one about a missing document, and it would go quiet the moment someone re-added the declaration to make it green.

So a published document can vanish and the run stays green or reddens for the wrong reason.

WHAT IT WANTS. The published set is a LIST OF DOCUMENTS, not one document plus a year list: each entry names a projection and the slices it is published over. publishedProjectionBuilt iterates that instead of the single triple. The declaration lives in internal/project beside PublishedFiscalYears(), because `fisc export` and `fisc verify` must read the same one -- that shared declaration is the property publishedProjectionBuilt's doc comment calls "the divergence a shared constant cannot close".

DISCOVERED removing documentsAreChecked's "registered and produced no document at all" arm (2026-08-25). That arm caught this case by accident, for a projection that declared no slices. Its stated premise -- "`fisc export` would still publish it" -- was true of the old cartesian build loop and false after fisc-neh inverted it, and keeping it would have made every projection of a schedule a FIXTURE does not carry into a corpus defect across ~70 test call sites. So it went, and this is the half of it that was load-bearing, written down rather than lost.
acceptance_criteria: the published set is a declaration of (projection, slices) pairs read by both fisc export and fisc verify; publishedProjectionBuilt fails when ANY published document was not built, naming the projection and the slice; a trends document that stops being built goes red with a finding about the missing document rather than about 924 facts; the existing spine behaviour and its tests are unchanged
notes:
2026-08-26 THE DEPENDS ON fisc-4ua.3 EDGE IS REMOVED, not annotated.

That edge was recorded when this bead was filed on 2026-08-25, and what it was
waiting for was the trends document EXISTING. It does: 9ebed77 built it and
92e657f gave it a page, so data/revenue-trends.json is published, checked and
cited today. What remains of fisc-4ua.3 is the page's MARK, which this bead does
not depend on in any direction -- the hole is in the harness and is open right
now, with fisc verify reporting 'every SANKEY slice the site publishes was built
and checked' over a site that publishes two documents.

Removed rather than noted because the edge kept this bead out of bd ready, and a
note does not change that: the next session's bd ready would go on hiding a live
P1 while the description explained why it should not. Recorded here so the
removal is a decision rather than a graph edit nobody can account for.
2026-08-26 WHAT fisc-gxa.2 WILL REWRITE HERE, recorded before the work rather than discovered during it.

fisc-gxa.2's 2026-08-24 note re-derives four exact-equality sites that must move
together when Options.Scope becomes Options.Scopes, and TWO of them are this
bead's own files:

  internal/check/coverage.go:189   publishedProjectionBuilt
  internal/check/subject.go:591    factSlices

Its acceptance criteria also turn spineScope (subject.go:45, aliasing
project.PublishedScope at subject.go:49) into a per-projection property. This bead
deliberately LEAVES the Published* consts in place -- removing them is that bead's
business, not this one -- so the published-document declaration landing here will
carry one `scope` string per entry that fisc-gxa.2 converts to a set, and the
describe-documents prose goes with it.

That is the direct and accepted cost of finishing the second document before
closing E6. It is written down here so the next session reads it as planned rework
rather than as a conflict, and so fisc-gxa.2's landing plan can count it.
close_reason:
project.PublishedDocuments is a list of (projection, stem, scope, columns) read by both fisc export and fisc verify. published-projection-built iterates it instead of the single triple plus PublishedFiscalYears(), and fisc verify now reports all three documents by name: sankey (FY2026 adopted all-funds-gross), sankey-2027 (FY2027 adopted all-funds-gross), revenue-trends (FY2024 actual, FY2025 revised, FY2026 adopted, FY2027 adopted revenue-by-fund).

TWO THINGS THE BEAD DID NOT SPECIFY AND THAT THE LANDING FORCED. (1) Each entry carries its STEM, because a stem is not derivable from a declaration -- stemFor asks how many slices a projection declared at runtime, and the trends contract forbids putting that document through PublishedStem at all. Without the stem the export twin would re-derive that rule, which is the second copy this bead exists to remove. (2) Each entry STATES its columns rather than deriving them from the facts, because a published set derived from the corpus agrees with it by construction and goes quiet in exactly the state it is for.

THE COMPARISON IS PER COLUMN, which is more than the bead asked for and closes part of fisc-7dt: a document short a printed column reports 'built without FY2024 actual' rather than being satisfied by existing. Noted on fisc-7dt with the argument for why a stated column list is a declared floor rather than the author-chosen constant that bead refuses.

Acceptance, each met: the published set is a declaration read by both commands (project.PublishedDocuments, via subject.go Load and pkg/cmd/export assertPublishedBuilt sharing project.MissingColumns); publishedProjectionBuilt fails when ANY published document was not built, naming the projection and the slice (it names the stem, the columns and the scope, and distinguishes 'nothing checked it' from 'built without <columns>' because those are different repairs); a trends document that stops being built goes red with a finding about the missing document -- TestARetargetedScopeUnbuildsThePublishedTrendsDocument, which retargets the scope rather than deleting the facts so the 924-finding alternative genuinely exists to be displaced; the existing spine behaviour and its tests are unchanged (TestAPublishedYearNothingBuiltIsReported and TestAPublishedYearBuiltByAnotherProjectionIsNotEnough carry over on spineDocuments()).

Both mutations were run against the pre-change published set and reported 'published-projection-built = pass'. facts.jsonl byte-identical. fisc verify --strict: 32 passed, 0 failed, 3 vacuous, 1 skipped. Landed in abcb43e.

title: documents-are-checked has no arm for a non-graph shape that IS checked
description:
documents-are-checked (internal/check/documents.go:29-127) exists to refuse a projection that no structural check reads. Its test is ONE LINE:

  for _, p := range s.Projections { if p.Graph != nil { checked++; continue } ... }

It does not consult check.All(), does not know a check id, and CANNOT -- its own doc comment (documents.go:33-36) says so: "nothing in Go lets this ask which checks read this projection ... the day that stops being true is the day a second document shape gets its own checks and its own arm here."

THAT DAY IS THE TRENDS DOCUMENT. Landing trend-points-tie-to-facts and trend-series-are-complete has ZERO effect on this check's verdict: the trends projection still carries a nil Graph, so it falls to the "produces no graph, so no structural check reads it" finding and documents-are-checked goes RED with fully checked facts behind it. The only escape today is an uncheckedDocuments entry, and that map's own doc comment says it must stay empty and that an entry is "a promise that someone is coming back" -- exactly the wrong instrument for a shape that IS covered.

WHAT THE ARM HAS TO BE. Not "is this a graph" but "is this projection's SHAPE one some check reads". The crude test was sound while graph checks were all the structural checks there were; it stops being sound at two shapes. The natural unit is the projection NAME, since that is what a check selects on and what Projection.String() already prints: a set of shapes the check tree covers, declared beside the checks that cover them, so a third shape landing with no checks is still red.

WATCH THE FIXTURE. internal/check/fixture_test.go:333 builds through project.Registry(reg) over a SPINE-ONLY fixture, so a registered Trends declares zero slices there and fires the OTHER arm at documents.go:82-89 -- "registered and produced no document at all" -- across ~72 runChecks call sites. That arm is correct in general and wrong here: a projection is not defective for being of a schedule a fixture does not carry. Same trap the detail-ties-to-spine-shape memory records for the detail checks (point 2). Hard-coded counts that move with it: checks_test.go:56 "documents-are-checked": "pass over 1", checks_test.go:103-110 Counts.Vacuous == 15, checks_test.go:90's prose, subject_test.go:247.

Found in peer review of the revenue-trends landing plan, 2026-08-25. The plan's first draft asserted the trend checks would green this; they do not.
acceptance_criteria: documents-are-checked passes over a projection that carries no graph and whose shape is covered by structural checks, without an uncheckedDocuments entry; uncheckedDocuments stays empty; a projection of a shape NO check reads is still red; a projection registered but declaring no slices over a fixture that does not carry its schedule is not reported as a defect; the existing arms and their tests keep their behaviour
close_reason: documents-are-checked now asks which SHAPE a projection built and names the checks that read it, so a shape added without checks still fails. uncheckedDocuments stays empty. Two things came out of doing it that the bead did not predict. The 'registered and produced no document at all' arm was REMOVED rather than narrowed: its stated premise -- 'fisc export would still publish it' -- was true of the old cartesian build loop and false after fisc-neh, and keeping it would have made every projection of a schedule a fixture does not carry into a corpus defect across ~70 runChecks call sites. The half of it that was load-bearing is filed as fisc-w7d. And the subject count moved from len(Registered) to len(Projections), because the registry denominator existed only to hold that arm's subject -- leaving it would report 'pass over 1' for a run that examined no document at all. Subject.Registered is now gone; nothing read it.

title: pkg/cmd/export still builds the cartesian product, and hard-errors on the first non-spine projection
description:
fisc-gxa.2's 2026-08-24 note says the clause "buildProjections stops building the cartesian product len(ps) x len(slices)" MOVED OUT to fisc-744. fisc-744 is closed (95724b1). It fixed internal/check's buildProjections (subject.go:602-669) and NOT pkg/cmd/export's, which is a separate function of the same name.

pkg/cmd/export/data.go:68-106 still loops project.PublishedFiscalYears() x project.Registry(), fixing opts at {year, PublishedBasis, PublishedScope}, and at data.go:88-93 HARD-ERRORS when a Sliced projection does not declare that slice:

  if !slicesContain(want, opts) { return nil, fmt.Errorf("the %s projection is of %d slice(s), none of them the published FY%d %s %s ...") }

slicesContain (data.go:158-165) compares fiscal year, basis AND scope. A trends projection declaring revenue-by-fund fails it, so "fisc export" returns that error on the FIRST invocation, before any file is written. This is a prerequisite for any second projection, not a follow-up.

WHAT IT BECOMES: loop the projections, ask each Sliced projection for its slices, build one document per slice. slicesContain's refusal survives for the SPINE -- its reason is still good there (the two commands must not disagree about which slice the published document is of) and it is the check that keeps "fisc export" and "fisc verify" from diverging.

AND IT NEEDS A STEM RULE FOR A DOCUMENT THAT IS NOT A YEAR OF ANYTHING. project.PublishedStem(name, year) (project.go:105-110) returns name for PublishedFiscalYear and name-year otherwise, so under today's loop a trends projection that got past slicesContain would be written TWICE, at revenue-trends and revenue-trends-2027 -- two byte-identical documents, one of them a lie. PublishedStem(name, 0) is "revenue-trends-0". The rule: PublishedStem applies only to a projection that publishes one document PER YEAR; a projection whose single slice spans several columns is written at its Name() verbatim.

yearStems (data.go:194-204) needs no change -- it is already parameterised by projection name and already filters to stems that were built.

Found reading the code for the revenue-trends landing plan, 2026-08-25.
acceptance_criteria: buildProjections loops projections and builds one document per declared slice, not one per (published year x projection); a projection whose slices do not include the published spine slice does not abort the export; the spine's slicesContain refusal survives with its reason intact; a projection whose slice spans more than one column is written at Name() and not through PublishedStem; pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go:428's stem assertion is updated rather than deleted
close_reason: pkg/cmd/export/buildProjections loops projections and builds one document per declared slice. The refusal that made a second schedule impossible is gone; the half worth keeping survives as an assertion that every published spine year was built, naming both sides. slicesContain and describeSlices went with it. stemFor is the new stem rule and it asks HOW MANY DOCUMENTS the projection publishes, not how many columns one of them carries -- /code-review caught the column-count version, which would have shipped a single-column trends document as revenue-trends-2024.json while the contract's promised path did not exist. Both directions pinned by TestStemForAsksHowManyDocumentsNotHowManyColumns.

title: project.Options cannot express a multi-year document: the column axis
description:
internal/project/project.go:119-159 declares Options with FiscalYear int and Basis singular, and Validate refuses FiscalYear <= 0. But Sliced's own doc comment (project.go:186) promises 'a four-year trend line is a chart of exactly one thing, so a trends projection returns a single slice spanning all four.' THE TYPE CANNOT HOLD THAT SLICE. No bead owned this until now; fisc-4ua.3, fisc-2u4, fisc-2n5, fisc-gxa.2 and fisc-744 were all searched.

THE DECISION: Options.FiscalYear and Options.Basis are replaced by Columns []Column, where Column is {FiscalYear int; Basis mapping.Basis}. Sankey errors on len(Columns) != 1.

WHY NOT A ZERO-VALUE WILDCARD (FiscalYear 0 meaning every year). Absent is not zero is a corpus invariant (docs/agents/conventions.md), and Options own doc comment already warns that an implicit all-years value is how a projection doubles every figure while still balancing. A wildcard would put that failure mode back inside the type built to prevent it.

WHY Column AND NOT []int OF YEARS. Measured on the committed store: FY2026 and FY2027 are BOTH adopted, so basis alone is not a key; and within revenue-by-fund year-to-basis is 1:1 (2024/actual, 2025/revised, 2026/adopted, 2027/adopted), so neither component is redundant. The pair is the key.

THE HARD PART IS NOT A FIELD RENAME. keyOf (internal/check/coverage.go:159) returns ONE sliceKey and factsAreProjected uses it as a map key at coverage.go:302 and :326 to attribute unprojected facts to a REFUSED slice; publishedProjectionBuilt builds one built[slice{}] entry per projection at coverage.go:215. One Options no longer means one slice, so both are a redesign rather than a rename.

THE SITES, re-derived at afd782a. Production: internal/project/sankey.go:325 (Sankey.Slices CONSTRUCTS Options), :497, :499, :527 (selectFacts); internal/project/project.go:143 (Validate); internal/check/graph.go:806 (factsFor); internal/check/subject.go:134, :162 (both String()), :673 (factSlices -- this is one of the four sites fisc-gxa.2's own 2026-08-24 correction names, and it is easy to miss); internal/check/coverage.go:159 (keyOf), :215 (publishedProjectionBuilt); pkg/cmd/export/data.go:69 (opts), :95, :160 (slicesContain), :176 (describeSlices). Tests: internal/project/project_test.go:11,19-22,54; internal/project/fixture_test.go:30; internal/project/sankey_test.go:557; internal/check/document_test.go:30,173,201; internal/check/checks_test.go:1403; internal/check/subject_test.go:396.

testdata/sankey.golden.json STAYS BYTE-IDENTICAL: sankey.go:497-499 reads o.FiscalYear/o.Basis into Metadata, whose field order does not change, so o.Columns[0].FiscalYear emits the same bytes. The guard that matters is internal/project/sankey_test.go:51 (bytes.Equal); pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go:441 decodes both sides and would miss a field reorder. facts.jsonl is untouched -- pkg/cmd/build and internal/build have zero references to internal/project.

THE ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, and it has real force. fisc-gxa.2's acceptance criteria require Options.Scope -> Options.Scopes as a SET over the same exact-equality sites, so landing Columns now and Scopes later edits four filters twice. Rejected because (1) the expensive part -- going from 'one Options -> one sliceKey' to 'one Options -> N' -- is forced by Columns anyway, and once that code path is plural, adding Scopes is an extension of it rather than a second redesign; and (2) a set-valued Scope has ZERO consumers today (every projection is len == 1) and drags gxa.2's 'no declared scope set contains two scopes a reconciliation check relates' tier-1 guard forward with it, which lands a check before any mapped page demands it -- E5's own governing rule. Whoever lands fisc-gxa.2 inherits these sites already plural.

A SECOND ALTERNATIVE, also rejected: leave project.Options alone and make check.Projection.Options a []project.Options, grouping a projection's declared slices into one built document. That leaves sankey.go, Validate and the golden file untouched, but Projection.Build(facts, o Options) still takes ONE Options and so cannot be told to build over four -- it trades an Options break for a break in the Projection interface, which project.go's package doc names as the seam that exists to be stable.
close_reason: Options.FiscalYear and Options.Basis are now Columns []Column, Sankey errors on len != 1, and testdata/sankey.golden.json is byte-identical. The bead's site list was complete except for one it named in passing and one it did not: internal/project/sankey.go:325 CONSTRUCTS Options in Sankey.Slices, and the coverage machinery needed a redesign rather than a rename -- keyOf became keysOf returning one sliceKey per column, publishedProjectionBuilt's built map takes N entries per projection, and factsAreProjected's refused-slice attribution sums over a failure's columns instead of reading one key. The rejected alternative (Columns+Scopes together) stays rejected and the reasoning stands: whoever lands fisc-gxa.2 inherits these sites already plural, so the expensive half -- one Options meaning N slices -- is paid for.

title: The multi-view shell: Views replace PrimaryProjection, and the page stops being a Sankey page
description:
fisc-l25 is answered "several views, the Sankey is the headline". internal/export
cannot express that today.

WHAT IS ALREADY READY: the DATA path. export.go:315-319 writes one
data/<stem>.json per entry in Options.Projections, and has since fisc-gxa.3. A
second DOCUMENT costs nothing.

WHAT IS SINGLE-VIEW, and it is the page:

  - PrimaryProjection (export.go:49) is the const "sankey", and Options.validate
    (export.go:177-179) returns ErrNoPrimary unless a stem is literally named
    that.
  - buildPage (page.go:216) decodes projections[PrimaryProjection] and nothing
    else.
  - pageData (page.go:159-178) is composed entirely from that document's headline
    -- Hero, Figures, PrimaryPath -- and page.go:234-239 hard-refuses a document
    with no fiscal_year_label or a zero headline expenditure. A trends document
    has neither and is not defective for lacking them.
  - site/index.html.tmpl is 170 lines of unconditional markup with no nav and no
    template blocks.
  - clientConfig publishes `primary` as one string; site/app.js:976 reads
    CONFIG.projections[CONFIG.primary] and nothing else.

THE SHAPE: N FLAT HTML PAGES, not hash routing, and the reason is a property the
code already defends. page.go:81-82: "The page renders these figures server-side
so the headline survives without JavaScript." Under hash routing, views 2..N have
no server-rendered content at all. Two further reasons: citations are PER VIEW
(see fisc-fjy), so one page would need a footer listing the union of every view's
sources -- a page claiming provenance for figures it never showed; and
understands() (app.js:962) refuses the whole page on a schema mismatch, which
under one page blanks the site rather than one view.

Flat rather than nested because every asset path in the tree is relative
(style.css, data/x.json, vendor/) and a page one directory deep would need ../
everywhere or a <base>.

  type View struct { Path, Nav, Template, Projection, Title, Lede string }

Options gains Views []View; validate requires every View.Projection to be a built
stem, every Path unique, .html-suffixed and screened by the same rules as
assetPath, and exactly one index.html. reservedPaths is a package var with
"index.html" baked in and must become per-Options, or an asset can shadow
revenue.html. buildPage becomes buildSite, looping views.

func views() []export.View LIVES IN pkg/cmd/export, NOT HERE. That is what keeps
internal/export's stated property -- it "consumes projections as filename stem ->
JSON bytes and knows nothing about how they were built" and never imports
internal/project.

SATISFIES fisc-f75's empty/error-state clause. Does NOT close it: see that bead's
2026-08-24 amendment.
acceptance_criteria: internal/export takes a []View from the caller and still does not import internal/project; PrimaryProjection and ErrNoPrimary are gone or demoted to 'the view the site opens on'; no figure on any page is recomputed by the packager; a view whose projection did not build is an error naming the view and the projection; validate refuses a duplicate Path, a Path that is not .html, a Path that shadows a reserved asset, and a view set with no index.html; the existing single-view output is byte-identical apart from the nav markup
close_reason:
internal/export takes a []View from the caller, still does not import internal/project, and buildPage is buildSite looping views. PrimaryProjection is demoted to 'the spine document, and the default view's projection' -- and NOT, as an earlier draft of its own doc comment claimed, required to be the view at index.html; validate asks only that exactly one view is there, because which document a site opens on is the composition root's decision. reservedPaths became a method on Options, so an asset can no longer shadow revenue.html: TestAnAssetCannotShadowAView. views() lives in pkg/cmd/export.

THE SPLIT THE BEAD NAMED BUT DID NOT SIZE: decodeProjection's two refusals -- no fiscal_year_label, no headline expenditure -- sat in the ONE path every document went through, and internal/project/document.go says in writing that a trends document carries neither. They are now decodeSankey's, invoked by being a Sankey. tilesFor went with them. Options.YearStems became View.YearStems for the same reason: years are a property of the SPINE, and a site-wide list could not say that the revenue trends are one document over four columns with no year to switch between.

AND THE SHELL HAS A CONSUMER RATHER THAN LANDING EMPTY: revenue.html ships, server-rendered, 231 rows x 4 columns, every figure linking to the extracted text of the page it was read from. It loads no app.js -- CONFIG.projections[CONFIG.primary] draws a Sankey and would blank on a document of series -- so the whole page works with JavaScript off, which is the property the spine page defends for its headline applied to a page. A chart is fisc-4ua.3.

/code-review caught a defect worth recording: the table cells were emitted POSITIONALLY, one per point, against headers built from metadata.columns. A series short a column -- a state incompleteSeries explicitly supports, and fisc export runs no checks -- would have slid every later figure one column left, printing FY2026's money under FY2025 with a citation link to FY2026's page. Cells are now keyed on (fiscal_year, basis) and a missing point renders a visible gap. TestAShortSeriesDoesNotShiftItsNeighboursIntoTheWrongColumn.

title: A forecast is not a fact, and Fact.Derived is not the exemption
description:
Settle where a projected figure is allowed to live BEFORE any what-if or
forecasting work starts, because the obvious home for one is the fact store and
that home is closed.

THREE CHECKS FORECLOSE IT, and none of them consults Fact.Derived.
`grep '\.Derived' internal/check/*.go` returns only graph.go:145 and :150, which
are NODE checks over project.Node.

  - factTokenReparses.Run (internal/check/facts.go:189) iterates s.Facts with no
    exemption of any kind. Its doc comment (facts.go:184-188) forecloses the
    empty token in advance and in these words: "a fact is one figure the city
    printed, so a fact with no token has no printed figure behind it, cannot be
    re-derived, and cannot be cited. No fact in the store has one today, and this
    is the answer if one ever does."
  - factOffsetPointsAtToken.Run (facts.go:248) requires
    text[offset:offset+len(token)] == token IN A COMMITTED PAGE. THIS IS THE ARM
    THAT MATTERS, because it is the one that kills the obvious dodge: a forecast
    carrying a synthetic token that happens to re-parse to its own value passes
    the first check and fails here, since no page prints it.
  - factIDsRecompute needs a rule_id and doc_id in the hash tuple; MakeID
    (fact.go:104-105) hashes (doc_id, rule_id, row_path, row_label, column_path,
    fiscal_year, basis).

SO THE DECISION, in the non-dodgeable form: a Derived:true fact in this store can
only ever be a RE-READING or RE-CLASSIFICATION of a figure the city printed at a
page and an offset -- never a computed value. Fact.Derived's own doc comment
(fact.go:93-99) scopes it to STATING the published/derived distinction rather
than exempting anything, and every consumer today reads it as "we inferred this
classification", never as "no page stands behind this number". It must not
become the exemption arm. An exemption arm is the worse of the two failure modes
available here: it does not weaken the store visibly, it weakens it for a set
whose membership is decided by a boolean somebody sets.

WHERE A FORECAST DOES LIVE: a second store, with its own file, its own record
type, its own checks and its own column in the report -- not a flag on this one.
A scenario record cites the FACT IDS AND LOCATORS of the published figures it
derives from, states its method as a member of a CLOSED enumeration, and carries
a rationale. It is derived by construction; there is no other value it may take.

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE for `fisc verify` to police one at all: THE METHOD
MUST BE EXECUTABLE BY THE VERIFIER, NOT DESCRIBED IN PROSE. Then verify can
assert that every base a scenario cites resolves to a fact that exists and whose
amount_cents is what the scenario recorded; that the projected value is EXACTLY
what the declared method applied to those bases produces, recomputed and compared
in integer cents, so a hand-typed figure that has drifted from its own formula
fails; and that the method is one of the closed set, an unrecognised one being an
error rather than a passthrough. A scenario whose method is "staff judgement" is
unpoliceable and does not belong in this repository -- it belongs in a blog post
that links to the facts.

THE CLIENT-SIDE WHAT-IF SLIDER IS A THIRD THING and is not a store at all:
arithmetic in the browser over published figures, computed and discarded. It
ships only if the result is unmistakably marked as THE READER'S OWN ARITHMETIC --
never citable, never in a CSV export, never blended into a chart that also shows
published figures without the marking. If that cannot be made unmistakable, it
does not ship.

WORTH SAYING BEFORE ANYONE BUILDS A MODEL: fisc-4ua.4 is ten years of ACFR
audited actuals, and for most "where is this going" questions it is a better
answer than a forecast -- and it needs no new invariant.

Raised while planning the multi-view site, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: a written decision that no computed value is admitted to facts/facts.jsonl and that Fact.Derived is not the exemption arm; the rule recorded in docs/agents/conventions.md beside the four invariants, citing the two witness checks; the shape of a separate scenario store named, with the requirement that a method be executable by the verifier rather than described in prose; the client-side what-if marking rule stated as a precondition for shipping one
close_reason: Decided and recorded in 5a39583. The rule is in docs/agents/conventions.md beside the four invariants: nothing computed enters facts/facts.jsonl, and Fact.Derived is not the exemption. Three checks enforce it and none consults Derived; the arm that closes the obvious loophole is fact-offset-points-at-token, since a synthetic token can be made to re-parse but no page prints it.
