Where a forecast IS allowed to live, and the requirement that its method be executable by the verifier rather than described in prose, is in this bead's description; fisc-mcm, fisc-a9x, fisc-cnf and fisc-58h carry the work if it is ever wanted.

title: buildPage ships page text for the PRIMARY projection's citations only, so a second view's citations 404
description:
This is the defect the project exists to prevent, waiting for the second view.

internal/export/page.go:245-284 builds `sources`, `clientDocs` AND `cited` from
one place -- `meta.Sources`, the metadata of PrimaryProjection, which buildPage
decoded at page.go:217-233. internal/export/export.go then copies the extracted
text of exactly that `cited` list into the output tree (Write at export.go:249-260,
withPageText at export.go:372-394), and only that list.

So a view whose document cites pages the primary does not -- revenue trends over
pp.127-140, a department view over pp.167-170, anything at all outside pp.66-67 --
renders a citation link to extracted/<doc>/pages/p0127.txt that WAS NEVER COPIED
INTO dist/. The link resolves in the template, is styled like every working
citation beside it, and 404s.

THAT IS PRECISELY fisc-ze7 AGAIN, which was closed on 2026-08-22 for the same
symptom from a different cause: "the site ships two citation classes and only one
works". fisc-ze7 fixed WHERE the text is cited from. This is WHICH text is
shipped, and no part of that fix touches it, because with one view the primary's
sources were the whole set.

IT IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY EXISTING CHECK. fact-offset-points-at-token reads
data/extracted/, the committed corpus -- not dist/. Nothing walks the built tree
and asks whether the files its own hrefs name are present. So this fails in the
browser and passes everything.

WHAT CHANGES. The citation set becomes the UNION over every view's projection
metadata, deduplicated -- the dedup already exists at page.go:271-276 and the
comment there ("a document that cites a page twice is one file to ship, and
shipping it twice is a write collision") is the same argument one scale up. The
footer's Sources list stays PER VIEW, because a page claiming provenance for
figures it never showed is its own defect; only the shipped file set is unioned.

AND IT WANTS A CHECK, because a link nobody clicked is a link nobody tested: walk
the built output, collect every href into extracted/, and assert each names a
file present in the tree. That is cheap, it is Go, and it needs no browser.

Found in peer review of the multi-view landing plan, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: the shipped page-text set is the union of every view's cited pages, deduplicated; each view's footer Sources list stays that view's own; a test builds a site with two views citing disjoint pages and asserts both sets of files are present in the output tree; a check or test walks the built output and asserts every href into extracted/ names a file that exists
notes:
2026-08-25 PARTIALLY ADDRESSED BY THE YEAR TOGGLE (9444126), and the remaining
half is the one this bead is about.

buildPage now unions the CITED PAGES across every published year, so the shipped
extracted/ tree covers all of them. That was forced by the FY2027 export: both
years cite pp.66-67, so the union is the same set today and nothing was visibly
broken, but a year citing a page the opening year does not would have shipped a
dead link.

WHAT IS STILL PRIMARY-ONLY, and it is deliberate rather than missed:

  - the footer's Sources list and clientDocs are the OPENING year's. A page
    listing sources for figures it is not showing is its own defect, so these
    stay per-view; what has to be unioned is only the file set.
  - the footer's scope, basis and sources line does not follow a year switch.
  - and none of it generalises to a view of a DIFFERENT schedule, which is this
    bead: a trends view over pp.127-140 or a department view over pp.167-170
    cites pages no sankey document names, and buildPage would have to read those
    documents' metadata to know it.

So the union loop exists and is the shape the fix takes; what it does not yet do
is run over views rather than over years.
close_reason:
The shipped page-text set is the union over every VIEW, not the primary's. Measured before and after on the real export: dist/extracted shipped 2 files (p0066, p0067) and now ships 16 -- the trends view cites pp.127-140, so the fix is worth exactly fourteen citation links that would have rendered styled like the working ones beside them, resolved in the template, and 404'd in the browser. Each view's footer Sources stays its own: TestEachViewsFooterCitesItsOwnSources asserts the spine page does not advertise p127 and the revenue page does not advertise p66.

THE UNION IS SHAPE-BLIND. citationsOf decodes through documentSources -- metadata.sources, the one block every projection carries whatever its body is -- so a view of a document this packager has never heard of still contributes its pages. That is what makes it general rather than a second special case beside the year loop 9444126 added.

THE CHECK THIS BEAD ASKS FOR IS NOT THE ONE IT DESCRIBES, and /code-review found why. 'Walk the built output, collect every href into extracted/, assert each names a file present' ALREADY EXISTED as TestEveryAssetThePageAsksForWasWritten, and it was green throughout, because the dead links are not in the markup: site/app.js:390-392 composes them at runtime per cited fact as CONFIG.docs[d].page_text_base + pNNNN.txt, and only the footer's handful ever reach the HTML. So two checks landed instead. TestEveryViewsMarkupResolves extends the walk to every view's page; TestEveryCitationTheClientComposesResolves crosses the client's own config against every document it can fetch, which is the set of paths the browser will actually construct. All three of the new tests were run against the union loop reverted to primary-only and all three go red.

title: published-projection-built pins ONE triple, so it cannot see a second published document -- and will not notice FY2027
description:
fisc-kwq says of the FY2027 export that "only the export is pinned". TWO THINGS
ARE PINNED, and the second one is a check.

publishedProjectionBuilt.Run (internal/check/coverage.go:189-220) compares the
projections that were built against three package constants and nothing else:

  want := fmt.Sprintf("FY%d %s %s",
      project.PublishedFiscalYear, project.PublishedBasis, project.PublishedScope)
  ...
  if o.FiscalYear == project.PublishedFiscalYear &&
      o.Basis == project.PublishedBasis &&
      o.Scope == project.PublishedScope {

project.go:63-67 fixes those at (2026, adopted, all-funds-gross). So the check
asserts exactly one slice is built and checked, and it is GREEN today for the
right reason. The moment `fisc export` publishes a second document -- FY2027, or
a trends document over a different scope -- this check keeps passing while
covering strictly less of what the site publishes, which is the same class of
quiet as fisc-rmw.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. This check's own finding text says what it is
for: "`fisc export` publishes this slice and nothing checked it... Every check
below this one reads the projections, so a slice that was not built is not
failed, it is unexamined". That sentence is only true of the slice it names. A
second published slice that is never built is unexamined AND unreported.

WHAT CHANGES. The published triple becomes a published SET -- the declaration in
internal/project (project.go:55-67) already exists precisely so `fisc export` and
`fisc verify` cannot disagree about it, and its doc comment says so, so the set
belongs there and not in either command. publishedProjectionBuilt iterates it and
reports per member, naming any published slice that was not built.

SEQUENCING: this lands WITH the FY2027 export (fisc-kwq), not after it. Landing
the export first leaves a window in which the site publishes a year no check
looks at, and that window is exactly the state the check exists to make
impossible.

Found in peer review of the multi-view landing plan, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: the published slice is a SET declared in internal/project beside Options, not a triple; publishedProjectionBuilt iterates it and reports per member; a published slice that was not built is a finding naming that slice; the check stays non-vacuous with one member; it lands in the same commit as the FY2027 export so no window exists in which the site publishes a year nothing checks
close_reason: Landed in 9444126, in the same commit as the FY2027 export so no window existed in which the site published a year nothing checked. project.PublishedFiscalYears() is the declaration both commands read; publishedProjectionBuilt iterates it, reports per member, and compares the projection NAME as well as the triple (per-projection slices mean matching the triple no longer implies the sankey was built). Subject.PublishedYears carries it so a fixture can be a smaller repository than this one. Two tests pin it: a published year nothing built fails, and another projection covering the slice is not enough.

title: staleDeclarations has no partial arm: a half-drawn scope keeps a declaration that is green and false
description:
unprojectedScopes' own doc comment (internal/check/coverage.go:34-39) states the
guarantee this bug breaks:

  AN ENTRY THAT HAS STOPPED BEING TRUE MUST GO RED, NOT QUIET. factsAreProjected
  consults this map only for UNPROJECTED facts, so the moment a projection starts
  drawing a declared scope the entry goes silent while remaining a false claim
  about the corpus. staleDeclarations is the branch that refuses that.

IT ONLY REFUSES THE TOTAL CASE. staleDeclarations (coverage.go:354) opens with

  for _, scope := range sortedStrings(unprojectedScopes) {
      if declared[scope] > 0 {
          continue
      }

and `declared` is populated at coverage.go:273-276 from facts that fell outside
EVERY projection. So a projection that draws SOME of a declared scope leaves the
rest counted in `declared`, the guard skips the scope, and the entry stays green
while asserting something that is no longer true.

MEASURED, and this is not hypothetical -- it is the shape of the next projection
to land. revenue-by-fund carries 924 facts across four (fiscal_year, basis)
pairs. A revenue-trends projection covering only the two ADOPTED years -- the
obvious first cut, since those are the years the spine prints a column for --
would draw 462 and leave 462 unprojected. declared["revenue-by-fund"] = 462, the
guard skips, and verify goes on printing the entry's reason text verbatim: "the
line-item and per-fund decomposition of pp.66-67's REVENUE rows... drawing them
into the fund-group spine doubles the city's revenue". Half of that scope is now
IN a chart, and the check that exists to say so says nothing.

WHY THE ENTRY BEING PARTLY TRUE IS NOT A DEFENCE. The entry is a claim about a
SCOPE, not about a fact count: verify prints "%d in scope %q (%s)"
(describeDeclared, coverage.go:309-317), so a partly-drawn scope prints a smaller
number beside an unchanged reason. A reader sees the count fall and the
declaration hold, which reads as coverage improving under a stable exemption --
the opposite of what happened.

WHAT A PARTIAL ARM HAS TO SAY. Not "this scope is drawn" and not "this scope is
declared", but which SLICE of it is which. The natural unit is the one
factsAreProjected already keys on, sliceKey{FiscalYear, Basis, Scope}
(coverage.go:152-160): a declaration is stale for a slice the moment any
projection draws that slice, and an entry that is stale for some slices and live
for others must say so in the finding rather than in a count.

THE OTHER TWO BRANCHES ARE FINE and are recorded here so this is not re-derived:
deleting an entry while its facts stay unprojected is NOT quiet -- factsAreProjected
(coverage.go:277-281) emits one finding PER FACT, so 924 findings and a red
check. And retiring a declaration loses NO coverage: expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine
(detail.go:88), revenue-detail-ties-to-spine (revenuedetail.go:137) and
transfers-detail-ties-to-spine (transfersdetail.go:283) all read the fact store
directly via detailSums and never consult this map.

WORKAROUND UNTIL IT LANDS, and it is the reason this is P1 rather than P2: a
projection over a declared scope must select that scope EXHAUSTIVELY -- every
fiscal year and basis it carries -- so the entry retires through the total arm
that does work. That constraint is real and it shapes the trends projection: 924
of 924, not 462.

Found in peer review of the multi-view landing plan, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: staleDeclarations reports an unprojectedScopes entry that has become false for SOME slice of its scope, not only one that exempts nothing at all; the finding names which (fiscal_year, basis) slices are drawn and which are still declared; a scope no projection touches is still silent; the existing total-case arm keeps its behaviour and its test; a fixture in which one of two years of a declared scope is projected goes RED
close_reason: staleDeclarations has a partial arm, keyed on the sliceKey{FiscalYear, Basis, Scope} triple factsAreProjected already uses, and the finding names which slices are drawn and which are still declared. PROVED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: the new subtest was run against the old guard restored, and it reports 'status = pass ... 10 facts in 1 projections, plus 10 in scope expenditure-by-department (<the full reason text>)' -- this bead's failure mode verbatim, the reason printed unchanged beside a halved count. A third arm was added while in there: a scope with a REFUSED slice is now skipped entirely, because factsAreProjected routes those facts to the refusal rather than to declared, so liveSlices can be empty while the scope genuinely still exempts everything -- the check would have demanded deletion on the strength of a projection that did not build. The workaround this bead named (draw a declared scope exhaustively) is no longer load-bearing, but revenue-trends does it anyway and TestTrendsSlicesTakeTheWholeScope pins it, because exhaustive is also what retires the entry through the arm that does the most work.

title: A projection need not be a graph: check.Load hard-errors on the first non-Sankey projection
description:
ADDING ANY NON-GRAPH PROJECTION TO project.Registry BREAKS `fisc verify`
OUTRIGHT, AND NOTHING IN THE BEAD GRAPH RECORDS IT.

internal/check/subject.go:568, inside buildProjections:

  g, ok := p.(graphBuilder)
  if !ok {
      return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("projection %q does not expose its graph, so verify "+
          "cannot check its structure without parsing back the JSON it is validating",
          p.Name())
  }

That is a returned error out of check.Load, not a recorded ProjectionFailure. So
`fisc verify` exits non-zero HAVING PRINTED NO REPORT -- every finding in the run
lost -- which is verbatim the failure mode ProjectionFailure's own doc comment
(subject.go:124-138) says was fixed once already for the department-bearing fact
and must not come back.

check.Projection (subject.go:112-116) is {Name, Options, Graph *project.Graph}: a
projection IS a graph as far as this package is concerned. The blast radius is
smaller than that sounds and it is worth knowing before starting -- ALL 21 reads
of Projection.Graph outside tests live in ONE FILE, internal/check/graph.go.

THREE MORE SITES BREAK ON THE SAME COMMIT, none of them previously recorded:

  - pkg/cmd/export/data.go:58-71 builds EVERY registered projection under ONE
    Options triple, so a revenue-trends projection is asked for
    (2026, adopted, all-funds-gross).
  - internal/check/subject.go:543-587 builds the cartesian product
    len(ps) x len(slices), and factSlices (subject.go:591-623) yields spine
    slices only.
  - pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go:437 freezes the name set:
    cmp.Diff([]string{"sankey"}, keys(got)). internal/project/project_test.go:63
    asserts len(Registry()) == 1. Both move deliberately, not incidentally.

SPLIT OUT OF fisc-gxa.2, WHICH OWNS THIS IN PROSE AND BUNDLES IT WITH THE TIER
HIERARCHY. That bead's acceptance criteria include "buildProjections stops
building the cartesian product len(ps) x len(slices); the len(slices)==0 refusal
becomes per-projection and names which projection wanted which scope". That
clause is separable from tier population, constraint_tier and the editorial
classifications fisc-gxa.2 still needs, and it blocks EVERY second view rather
than only the tier work.

THE SHAPE. graphBuilder (subject.go:101-104) gets a sibling for a projection that
exposes a series rather than a graph; buildProjections dispatches on which one a
projection satisfies and refuses only a projection exposing NEITHER; the graph
checks skip nil-graph entries. Land it while it is provably inert -- with only
Sankey registered, `fisc verify` must report the same counts before and after,
which is the test.

ALSO IN SCOPE, because factSlices is the other half of the same assumption: a
projection says which slices it wants (a Sliced interface returning
[]project.Options) instead of this package hard-coding spineScope. Sankey.Slices
returns today's per-(year, basis) spine behaviour verbatim, so
subject_test.go:381-393 stays green.
acceptance_criteria: check.Load returns no error when a projection exposing no graph is registered; check.Projection.Graph may be nil and the graph checks in internal/check/graph.go skip such entries rather than dereferencing; buildProjections stops building the cartesian product len(ps) x len(slices) and asks each projection which slices it wants; a projection exposing NEITHER a graph nor any other checkable structure is still refused, and the refusal names it; with only Sankey registered `fisc verify` reports byte-identical counts to the run before the change; subject_test.go:381-393 stays green unedited
close_reason: Landed in 95724b1. project.Sliced lets a projection declare its own slices (Sankey.Slices returns today's spine behaviour verbatim); Subject.Graphs() is what the ten structural checks range over, so Projection.Graph may be nil; buildProjections records a non-graph projection instead of returning an error out of Load. The fail-closed half is a new check, documents-are-checked, non-vacuous on day one. Review found three holes the obvious implementation leaves and all three are closed: fisc export refused to honour Sliced (checked under one slice, published under another), a projection declaring zero slices was invisible to every list on the Subject, and published-projection-built matched the triple without the projection name. Four tests pin the regression.

title: A cancelled fisc verify reports every vacuity declaration stale and exits 3
description:
internal/check/vacuity.go:98,108:

  func (d Declaration) Ran() bool   { return d.Status != "" }
  func (d Declaration) Stale() bool { return d.Ran() && d.Status != StatusVacuous }

Ran() documents "did this run contain the check at all", and Stale() is
documented as "the check ran and reported something other than vacuous, so the
work it was waiting for has landed". FIVE STATUSES EXIST, and Stale() treats
three of them as landed-work: StatusPass, StatusFail and -- wrongly --
StatusSkipped and StatusError.

THE REACHABLE TRIGGER IS StatusError, AND IT IS CONTEXT CANCELLATION. run1
(internal/check/report.go:101-103) turns ctx.Err() into errored(...). So a
cancelled or timed-out `fisc verify` marks ALL THREE declarations stale, and
Report.Failed() (report.go:174-181) returns true on len(StaleDeclarations()) > 0
INDEPENDENTLY OF --strict. The run exits 3 printing, three times, "declared
vacuous and reported error; fisc-gxa.2 landed, so remove the declaration" --
about work that has not landed, in response to a Ctrl-C.

StatusSkipped is the same bug and is NOT reachable today, which is worth saying
so nobody widens the fix on a false premise: sourcePDFsMatchBothRecords
(internal/check/structural.go:675) is the only Full() == true check in the tree,
it is a tier-0 artifact check, and no one would declare it vacuous. Guard it
anyway -- the next --full check inherits the hole.

A GENUINE StatusError IS DIFFERENT AND SHOULD NOT BE SILENT. aggregation-invariance
is deliberately built to hard-error the moment any node carries a parent
(internal/check/graph.go:720-725, and its own declared reason says "it cannot be
reached by halves"). When THAT fires, the work really has landed. So the fix is
not "ignore error": it is that stale is a claim about pass/fail, and an errored
declared check needs its own wording rather than StaleReason()s "landed, so
remove the declaration".

Found by /code-review of HEAD~4..HEAD, 2026-08-24. Landed in 40943db.
acceptance_criteria: Stale() is true only for StatusPass and StatusFail; a declared check reporting StatusError or StatusSkipped does not fail the run; a cancelled verify does not report stale declarations; an errored declared check is reported with wording that does not claim its bead landed; tests cover all five statuses
close_reason: Already fixed by 5067e50, never closed. Verified on HEAD (92e657f): vacuity.go:124 is now Stale() { return d.Status == StatusPass || d.Status == StatusFail }, so StatusError and StatusSkipped no longer count as landed work and a Ctrl-C cannot report every declaration stale. A genuine error still fails the run via Report.Failed()'s Counts.Error arm (report.go:174-182), which is what the bead asked for -- an errored declared check gets its own wording in the printer at pkg/cmd/verify/report.go:120-126 ("reported %s, so this run says nothing about the declaration either way") rather than borrowing StaleReason()'s "landed, so remove the declaration". All five statuses are covered by TestADeclarationSurvivesACheckThatReachedNoVerdict (vacuity_test.go:229) -- errored and skipped subtests, plus a loop asserting passed/failed DO go stale. Closed on evidence in a planning session, no code written.

title: transfers-detail-ties-to-spine needs a comparison mode detailtie.go does not have
description:
fisc-aes specifies the check in three clauses. Two of them cannot be expressed
by the machinery detailtie.go provides, and the p76 landing plan understated
both.

WHAT THE CLAUSES NEED.

(b) kind = transfer_out, fund_group in {general, enterprise, internal-service,
    debt-service}: detail sum + a named to-CIP constant == spine sum.
(c) kind = transfer_out, fund_group in {capital, special-revenue}, THE TWO
    JOINTLY: detail sum + non-major to-CIP constant == the two spine columns
    summed.

THREE GAPS.

1. detailRestriction.FundGroup is ONE string. (b) admits four groups and (c)
   two, so it needs a SET.

2. "A per-clause constant" is a scalar and the clauses need a TABLE. Measured
   off p0073.txt / p0075.txt, per (fund_group, fiscal_year):
     general           0 / 0
     enterprise        9,353,147 / 14,220,000
     internal-service  40,000 / 612,000
     debt-service      0 / 0
     non-major (joint) 28,693,590 / 35,930,251

3. AND THE HARD ONE: clause (c) needs KEY COLLAPSING. detailKey carries
   fundGroup and compareDetail compares per key, so as written (c) compares
   capital (211,150 vs 28,584,740) and special-revenue (817,050 vs 1,137,050)
   separately and the joint constant has nowhere to land. Collapsing capital and
   special-revenue into one compared cell BREAKS detailtie.go's stated invariant
   -- "IT IS A FILTER AND NOT A KEY... Collapse the two and a check whose
   schedule spans every group would compare six groups' facts under one key and
   tie on a sum that happens to match." That invariant is right and the collapse
   is a real exception to it, so it needs an argument rather than a quiet edit.
   The argument available: the collapse here is not the restriction leaking into
   the key, it is the DOCUMENT declining to print the split, and the pair is the
   finest granularity the corpus publishes.

WHY (c) IS JOINT AT ALL, corrected. fisc-aes says the FY2026-27 split is
impossible because it would need a to-CIP of -117,485. THAT IS FALSE -- see the
correction on fisc-aes. Both years split cleanly. The real reason is
published-is-not-derived: pp.72-75 print to-CIP per major fund and then ONE
aggregate line for all non-major funds, so a per-group constant would be derived
by difference from p67 while the pair is printed.

Found in peer review of the p76 landing plan, 2026-08-24. Blocks fisc-5gk.3.1.
close_reason: Landed in ced45b4. p76 publishes 88 facts at scope transfers-by-fund (22 rows x 2 budget years x 2 legs) and transfers-detail-ties-to-spine reconciles them in three clauses: IN exact with no constant, OUT-major with the printed to-CIP figures added back, OUT-non-major with capital+special-revenue+permanent collapsed. Doubling proven by measurement rather than argued: republished at all-funds-gross the GF in-leg goes 480,400 -> 960,800 while three graph checks stay green. Only the two budget columns are published. See each bead's own note for what it owed.

title: p76 prints one total for the whole schedule and a Rollup is refused twice over
description:
The second thing that must be settled before p76's YAML can be written.

p76 prints ONE grand total beneath its last section -- $29,947,677 /
$27,679,706 / $21,525,997 / $21,624,633 -- and no per-section totals. So no
single rule can carry it as total_row, and the obvious answer, a Rollup over the
section rules, is refused twice by parse.go:

(1) a covered rule with TotalRow == "" is refused, because "a rollup sums the
    totals its covered rules PRINT, so every one of them must print one". None
    of p76's sections prints one.
(2) covered rules whose Parts[0].Columns differ are refused. p76's sections
    declare DIFFERENT fund_group per column -- general, enterprise,
    debt-service, permanent, special-revenue -- so they are not the same columns
    by construction.

THE OPTIONS.

(a) Rollup.Unassertable with a reason. Precedent exists (other-funds-total-sources).
    Honest and cheap. Cost: the page's own printed total then checks nothing at
    build time, and it is the only arithmetic p76 offers against itself.

(b) A cross-rule ROW-SUM concept -- a total that sums covered rules' VALUES
    rather than their printed totals. internal/mapping/rule.go argues against
    exactly this: "a rollup summing leaves would tie or fail depending on
    whether the document's roundings happened to cancel". That argument was made
    about a different case and should be re-stated against this one rather than
    inherited, because p76's four columns tie EXACTLY on the two budget years
    (0 delta, internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go) so there is no rounding to
    cancel.

(c) Leave the cross-rule sum in Go, where transfers_p76_test.go already has it.
    Cost: it checks the fixture, not the published rules.

STATE THE CONSEQUENCE WHICHEVER WAY IT GOES: fisc build's parts_unchecked count
goes 6 -> 11 when p76's five sections publish without a total_row. That number is
reported by pkg/cmd/build/report.go and a jump in it should be explained by the
commit that causes it, not discovered afterwards.

Found in peer review of the p76 landing plan, 2026-08-24, which asserted a
rollup over the six in-leg rules would work.
close_reason: Landed in ced45b4. p76 publishes 88 facts at scope transfers-by-fund (22 rows x 2 budget years x 2 legs) and transfers-detail-ties-to-spine reconciles them in three clauses: IN exact with no constant, OUT-major with the printed to-CIP figures added back, OUT-non-major with capital+special-revenue+permanent collapsed. Doubling proven by measurement rather than argued: republished at all-funds-gross the GF in-leg goes 480,400 -> 960,800 while three graph checks stay green. Only the two budget columns are published. See each bead's own note for what it owed.

title: A published part needs a channel for a column the page prints no header over
description:
Budget Book p76 cannot be published until this is settled, and it is a schema
question rather than a p76 question.

THE MECHANICS, verified.

parse.go requires column_headers to carry one entry per column INCLUDING every
skip: true one, and refuses an empty entry. p76 needs five columns: four years
plus the footnote marker, which the fixture declares as {skip: true}
(internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml). The page prints four headers,
over the four year columns, and nothing over the footnote
(testdata/pages/budget-p0076.txt line 9). internal/mapping/geometry.go matches
all headers on ONE printed line, so there is no fifth header anywhere to name.

AND OMITTING column_headers IS NOT AN OPTION. TestPublishedPartsDeclareColumnHeaders
(internal/mapping/mappings_test.go) is a ratchet: all 120 published parts declare
them today. p76 would be the first published part with a skipped column, and the
design has no channel for it.

WHY THE SKIPPED COLUMN IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT COSMETIC. amount.Parse reads
"(10)" as NEGATIVE TEN DOLLARS, because negatives are parenthesised throughout
this corpus. Nothing downstream sees that value only because the column is
skipped. Measured: every one of p76's 22 rows carries a marker, and there are
ten distinct ones -- (1) through (10).

THE OPTIONS.

(a) Move the markers to wrapped_labels. WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS: the gap does trim
    to "(10)", but all ten distinct markers would have to be declared, and they
    are footnote REFERENCES rather than wrapped label fragments. The declaration
    would say something untrue about the page in order to satisfy a guard.

(b) Give column_headers an explicit channel for a headerless column -- a null,
    or a rule that a skip: true column takes no entry. The cost is that the
    entry count stops being a check on the column count, which is part of what
    the guard buys.

(c) Something else. Note the guard's purpose: it is the column-grid check, and
    what it defends against is a rule whose columns have silently drifted from
    the page's. Whatever lands has to keep defending that.

Found in peer review of the p76 landing plan, 2026-08-24, which had this as a
one-line bullet.
close_reason: Decided and landed (fb28394): column_headers accepts an explicit null entry, legal only opposite a skip:true column and only in the last position. Option (b) of the three on the bead. The entry count stays the column-count check, which is what the guard buys. Two things the bead did not anticipate, both found by building it: yaml.v3 drops a null element from a sequence rather than decoding it, so ColumnHeaders had to become a named slice with its own unmarshaler; and an all-null list has to be refused, because the grid IS the headers. The restriction to the LAST position is the argument that keeps the weakened guard honest -- between two headers the gap has known bounds the grid would have checked.

title: Three committed fixtures are checked by nothing: fixturePages does not have to cover testdata/
description:
testdata/pages/ and testdata/geometry/ each carry eleven fixtures.
internal/mapping/resolve_test.go:169's fixturePages lists EIGHT:

  budget: 66, 67, 76, 127, 167        committed: 66, 67, 76, 127, 167, 168, 169, 170
  cip:    29, 40                      committed: 29, 40
  acfr:   177                         committed: 177

So budget pp.168, 169 and 170 -- six files, three page-text and three geometry
-- are read by tests and checked against the extraction by NOTHING.
TestFixturesAreVerbatimCopies iterates the list, not the directory.

They landed in a430cec, which added them and did not add the rows. The doc
comment on fixtureCopies says "Adding a fixture means adding a row here and
nothing else", and that sentence is exactly the gap: it describes a convention,
and a convention is not a check.

MEASURED 2026-08-24: none of the six has drifted yet, so this is a live hole
rather than a live failure. That is the whole reason to fix it now.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING ROW. TestFixturesAreVerbatimCopies' own doc
comment says it "is what makes every other test in this package mean anything",
and names the xberg -> poppler migration (fisc-yqv.5) as the case where fixtures
drifted from the extraction and every test reading them stayed green against a
substrate that no longer existed. Three fixtures currently sit outside that
guarantee, and every arithmetic claim proved against them -- the p168 two-level
rounding chain the whole Rollup design rests on, p170's General Fund Total
Expenses tie to the spine -- is proved against a file nothing says is real.

It also gets worse immediately: fisc-5gk.1 commits thirteen more page/geometry
pairs for pp.128-140. Adding thirteen rows by hand to a list nothing verifies is
the same coin flip twenty-six more times.

THE FIX IS NOT THE THREE ROWS, it is a test that the list COVERS THE DIRECTORY:
read testdata/pages and testdata/geometry, and fail on any file no fixtureCopy
names. That makes the convention machine-checked and turns "someone forgot" into
a red build in the commit that forgets. Same shape as unprojectedScopes'
staleDeclarations arm and fisc-2sd's remove-the-declaration branch: a
declaration that has stopped describing the tree must fail rather than go quiet.

Found while preparing fisc-5gk.1's fixtures, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: budget pp.168-170 are in fixturePages; a test reads testdata/pages and testdata/geometry and fails on any committed fixture no fixtureCopy names; that test is proven failable by removing one row from the list
close_reason:
Fixed, and the class is closed rather than the instance.

budget pp.168-170 are in fixturePages. More to the point,
TestEveryCommittedFixtureIsListed now reads testdata/pages and
testdata/geometry and fails on any committed file no fixtureCopy names, so the
list cannot fall behind the directory again. Proven failable by dropping p170
from the list: two findings, one per substrate, each naming the file and the fix.

It also refuses a vacuous pass -- a fixture directory that reads as empty is an
error rather than a loop that ran zero times, which is the failure mode a
directory-walking test invites.

fixtureCopies' doc comment said "Adding a fixture means adding a row here and
nothing else", which was the whole gap: it described a convention, and a
convention is not a check. It now names the test that enforces it and this bead.

None of the six files had drifted, so nothing that was proved against them was
wrong. What was wrong is that nothing said so.

title: CheckRollup compares only the COUNT of covered rules' columns, not which columns they are
description:
internal/mapping/resolve.go:964-985. CheckRollup takes `cols` from the FIRST covered rule's total-bearing part and then, for every later rule, checks only `len(stated) != len(sums)`.

So two covered rules whose bearer parts declare the same NUMBER of columns but DIFFERENT columns are summed against each other, column by column, without complaint. A rollup could add rule A's FY2026 general column to rule B's FY2027 enterprise column and report a clean tie.

WHY THE EXISTING GUARDS DO NOT CLOSE IT. validateRollups cross-checks units and columns at parse time, but against `Parts[0].Columns`. CheckRollup's own comment (resolve.go:958-963) explains why that is not enough -- 'which part bears the total needs the pages' -- and then does the weaker check anyway. The two halves of the argument are both present in the file; only the conclusion is missing.

NOT REACHABLE ON pp.167-170: the 23 division rules all declare the same four columns on every part, so the department lane cannot trigger it. It becomes live the moment a rollup covers rules whose bearer parts differ, which is what p130's 'Total General Fund' over pp.127-130 will be (fisc-5gk.1).

FIX: compare the bearer parts' Columns element by element (fund_group, fiscal_year, basis, skip), not their length, and name the two rules and the first differing column when they disagree.

TEST: two covered rules with same-width, differently-labelled columns must fail. A length-only test passes with the bug present, which is how it survived.

Found by /code-review of the fisc-o15 landing, 2026-08-23, and verified against the source.
close_reason: Landed in a3adb0e. fisc-7fe fixed element-wise on the EFFECTIVE basis (the Column.Basis override half was found in review of the fix); fisc-7a6 fixed at both sites, its premise corrected on the bead first; fisc-t9h guarded before both rules[0] indexes. Each test proven red against the prior code. Kind/scope left uncompared and filed separately.

title: Is one picture the product? fisc-gkv point D, and only the owner can answer it
description:
fisc-gkv decided points A, B and C -- a projection MAY select more than one scope
(Options.Scopes as a set), two scopes may NOT be selected together if a
reconciliation check relates them, and Sankey keeps exactly one scope. Those are
engineering conclusions backed by measurement and they are closed.

POINT D IS NOT AN ENGINEERING QUESTION AND fisc-gkv SAID SO. It recommends that
the finest-grain graph be a SECOND document, selecting {revenue-by-fund,
gf-department-object} and not the spine, with NO headline. Its own confidence
line reads: 'Medium on (D), the two-document split, because it trades a reader
question for a code guarantee and the reader question is not answerable from
this repository.'

THE QUESTION, in the form only the repo owner can answer: is one picture --
following a dollar from source to spend in a single view -- the product?

WHY IT CANNOT BE DECIDED BY MEASUREMENT. fisc-gxa.2's pitch is one picture. The
two-document answer means a reader cannot see $157,873,470 arrive from ~71
detail lines and leave through 11 departments without a client-side join across
two fetches, and no check covers that join. fisc-gkv's answer is that the join
is not across the two documents -- revenue-by-fund and gf-department-object are
disjoint and travel together in the tier document, so the spine document is the
citywide overview and the tier document is the drill-down. Two views, not two
halves of one view. That is a product claim, not a code claim.

WHAT IT COSTS IF THE ANSWER IS 'ONE PICTURE'. fisc-gkv (4) measured the price
and it is four changes, not one. Adding `fund` to cellKey is inert today (all
240 committed facts carry fund 0) and INSUFFICIENT tomorrow: with a tier-3
endpoint the graph builds and publishes a gross revenue of 36,411,276,900
against the golden file's 29,996,900,700, because Headline accumulates PER CELL
(sankey.go:393, 404, 412, 418) and splitting one cell into two adds both.
headline-ties-to-facts (check/graph.go:407-445) then re-sums the same facts the
headline was accumulated from and reports GREEN on the wrong number. And
revenue/taxes/property gains two outbound links carrying the same $64,143,762,
so d3 draws that node at twice its true width -- a visual double-count no
per-link check sees.

A HEADLINE IS A PROPERTY OF A SINGLE-GRAIN DOCUMENT. Once one document holds two
grains of the same money, 'the total' is ambiguous and no cell key can
disambiguate it, because the ambiguity is in the ACCUMULATION and not in the
key. So 'one picture' costs: the key, tier-aware endpoints, tier-aware headline
accumulators, and teaching headline-ties-to-facts which grain it is summing.

WHAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON IT. Nothing in the coverage lanes. fisc-5gk.1 and
fisc-5gk.2 publish facts at their own scope and are reconciled by fact-level
checks reading Subject.Facts, not any graph. Only the tier-hierarchy commit --
fisc-gxa.2, fisc-oxf, fisc-1wr.1.1, fisc-ix2 -- consumes the answer.

SO IT IS DECIDABLE LATER AT NO COST, AND BETTER DECIDED AGAINST A CHART THAT
EXISTS THAN AGAINST ONE THAT DOES NOT. That is fisc-gkv's own recommendation and
the reason this is split out rather than left blocking the wave. If the answer
turns out to be 'one picture' after the thing is drawn, the fallback is the
four-part redesign above, and fisc-gkv asks that it be re-opened deliberately
rather than improvised at the keyboard.

Split out of fisc-gkv on 2026-08-23 so that bead's decided points A/B/C could
close without this one closing with them.
acceptance_criteria: a recorded answer to whether the finest-grain view is a SECOND document or one graph carrying tiers 0-5; if two documents, the client join and its absence of checks is accepted in writing; if one graph, the four-part redesign in fisc-gkv (4) is scheduled and owned before fisc-gxa.2 starts
notes:
2026-08-24 ANSWERED BY THE OWNER: TWO DOCUMENTS, AND THE SITE IS NOT ONE PICTURE.

The question this bead asks -- "is one picture, following a dollar from source
to spend in a single view, the product?" -- is answered NO, and the answer is
larger than the bead's own framing. The direction is that the Sankey is the
site's HEADLINE VIEW and not the product: the site becomes several distinct
interactive views over different aspects of the budget, more like USAFacts than
like a single chart. So the finest-grain drill-down is a SECOND DOCUMENT, and
the four-part redesign fisc-gkv (4) priced -- fund in cellKey, tier-aware
endpoints, tier-aware Headline accumulators, and teaching headline-ties-to-facts
which grain it is summing -- is NOT TAKEN and is not scheduled.

THE COST IS ACCEPTED IN WRITING, which is what this bead's acceptance criteria
require of the two-document answer. A reader cannot see $157,873,470 arrive from
~71 detail lines and leave through 11 departments in one view without a
client-side join across two fetches, and NO CHECK COVERS THAT JOIN. Nothing in
internal/check sees the client, so a join that silently drops or double-counts a
node is invisible to `fisc verify`. That is the price of not paying for the
redesign, it is known, and it is accepted.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE, recorded so the next reader does not over-read it:
fisc-gxa.2's tier hierarchy is UNBLOCKED, not descoped. Tiers still populate,
node.parent still gets filled, and aggregation-invariance still goes
non-vacuous -- within one document per grain rather than across one document
spanning all grains.
close_reason: Answered two documents, not one picture. The Sankey is the site's headline view, not the product; the finest-grain drill-down is a second document; fisc-gkv (4)'s four-part redesign is not taken. The unchecked client-side join is accepted in writing -- see the 2026-08-24 note. Unblocks fisc-gxa.2 and fisc-f75.

title: Tier 1: the computed fund-balance residual equals the document's STATED change in fund balance
description:
Extracted from fisc-1wr.2 during its 2026-08-22 rewrite. That bead's surviving
clauses all want a DOCUMENT-DERIVED TOLERANCE for a source that declares coarser
precision, and the only such source in the corpus is the ACFR MD&A, which is
unmapped. This clause wants no tolerance at all, applies to a page that IS
mapped, and is therefore tier 1 rather than tier 2 -- so it should not wait
behind an ACFR mapping bead that does not exist.

THE CLAIM: the fund-balance residual this project COMPUTES equals the change in
fund balance the document itself STATES.

WHY IT IS WORTH HAVING, and this is the part that makes it different from the
other checks in the tier: most of what fisc verify asserts ties the graph to the
facts it was built FROM. This ties a computed quantity to an INDEPENDENTLY
PRINTED one. fisc-u2v's coverage.go incident and the whole scope axis exist
because "the graph agrees with its own inputs" is a weak claim. This is a strong
one, and pp.66-67 already print both sides.

VERIFIED to tie at zero tolerance in all twelve fund-group x fiscal-year cells
during the fisc-1wr.2 rewrite. Worked example, General Fund FY2026:
  158,353,870 - 159,388,024 = -1,034,154
which equals the printed CHANGE IN WORKING CAPITAL cell exactly.

Note what this is NOT: it is not the transfer residual (that is
headline-transfer-residual, already shipping), and it is not CheckTotals, which
is a build-time per-part assertion against a printed TOTAL row rather than a
check over the projection.

SIZE: small. Both sides are already in the fact store -- the spine's
fund_balance rules ship 48 facts -- so this is a check, not a mapping change.
acceptance_criteria: the check reports Subjects > 0 over pp.66-67 and passes at zero tolerance in all twelve fund-group x year cells; it is proven failable by mutating one fund_balance fact; it is registered in the tier-1 lane and not behind fisc-1wr.2
notes:
2026-08-23 ALREADY SATISFIED, and by a stronger assertion than this bead
proposes. Found while implementing it; verified by running the test.

internal/mapping/mappings_test.go:253 TestPublishedSpineBalancesPerFundGroup
asserts, over the same six fund groups and the same two budget years:

    sources = revenue + transfer_in + max(0, -change)
    uses    = expenditure + transfer_out + reserve_increase + max(0, change)
    sources == uses

which rearranges to exactly this bead's claim,

    revenue + transfer_in - expenditure - transfer_out - reserve_increase
        == fund-balance/change

and it then goes FURTHER than this bead asks: it pins both sides to the
printed TOTAL SOURCES / TOTAL USES control totals for all twelve cells --
rows that are mapped by no rule, which is what makes it a cross-check rather
than a restatement. This bead names no control total at all.

MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY off facts/facts.jsonl before finding the test: all 12
cells tie at zero, General Fund FY2026 = -1,034,154, this bead's worked
example to the cent.

THE ONE REAL DELTA, recorded so it is not lost: the existing assertion is a Go
test over the RESOLVED MAPPING, and `fisc verify` makes no such claim over the
committed fact store. That gap is narrower than it looks -- CI runs
`fisc build` and cmp's byte-for-byte against facts/facts.jsonl, so mapping and
artifact cannot drift -- and a mutated amount_cents or token is already caught
by fact-token-reparses and fact-offset-points-at-token, which tie every figure
to the page it was read from. What a verify-side version would add over all of
that is the axis, not the claim.

CONSEQUENCE FOR fisc-1wr.7, which this blocks: its scenario 3 must name
TestPublishedSpineBalancesPerFundGroup as the existing catch rather than wait
for a check that would duplicate it. fisc-1wr.2's 2026-08-22 note says "the
part that does not exist is clause 2, the fund-balance residual against the
document's stated change" -- that is the premise this closure corrects; it
does exist, one package over.

STILL UNASSERTED, filed separately rather than folded in here:
beginning + change - ending == 0, which also holds at zero in all 12 cells
(measured), and which neither the test above nor any check makes.
close_reason: Already satisfied by TestPublishedSpineBalancesPerFundGroup (internal/mapping/mappings_test.go:253), which asserts the same identity over the same 12 cells and additionally pins the printed TOTAL SOURCES / TOTAL USES control totals. See the 2026-08-23 note for the measurement and for the consequence to fisc-1wr.7.

title: [bug] label_tail re-keyed the row index on Identity() but omitted_rows, the total_row guard and ActiveRows still use bare Label
description:
The 2026-08-21 label_tail work re-keyed the parser's row index on
Row.Identity() (Label + "\x1f" + LabelTail) but left three sites validating and
filtering on the BARE Label. Each is a fail-open, which is the wrong direction
for this repo.

(1) omitted_rows IS UNMATCHABLE FOR A TWO-ANCHOR ROW. internal/mapping/parse.go
    validates omitted_rows entries against the bare label while the index is
    keyed on Identity(). Omitting a row that carries a label_tail errors with
    "is not one of this rule's rows", and NO YAML value can match, because the
    key contains a \x1f the author cannot type. Part.OmittedRows' own doc calls
    the declaration MANDATORY -- "without it a positional read shifts every
    label after the gap, which is a silent mismapping rather than an error". So
    a page that needs both features cannot be expressed.

(2) THE total_row "IS ALSO LISTED IN rows" GUARD IS SILENTLY DISABLED for any
    row carrying a label_tail. The guard exists to stop a printed total being
    mapped as a data row. With the key change it no longer fires, and the
    failure surfaces -- if at all -- as an unexplained CheckTotals mismatch,
    which is exactly the "row was missed" hint the resolver prints when it
    cannot tell you what actually happened.

(3) Rule.ActiveRows still filters by Label.

WHY ONE BEAD: all three are the same edit half-applied, and fixing one without
the others leaves the inconsistency somewhere else. The fact model has the same
defect from the other end -- see the fact-id bug -- but that one is a published
claim and gets its own id.

Also here, minor and in the same file: the "label_tail is blank" branch is
UNREACHABLE. A whitespace-only tail is caught by the preceding whitespace check,
so the blank branch cannot be entered and a caller who writes label_tail: ""
gets the wrong message.

Found by /code-review over the 8 commits ahead of origin/main, 2026-08-22.
acceptance_criteria: a two-anchor row can be named in omitted_rows; the total_row 'is also listed in rows' guard fires for a two-anchor row; ActiveRows filters on the same key the index uses; the unreachable blank-label_tail branch is removed or made reachable; each fix has a test that fails without it
close_reason: Landed in 3589fa2 with a fifth site neither bead named (canonicalRows pairing on Label, colliding RowIndex with omissions). MakeID takes PrintedLabel(); the reasoning and its accepted cost are in the doc comment.

comments.author: Jon Crussell
comments.text:
Fixed, plus one more site of the same defect the description did not list.

SYNTAX CHOSEN FOR omitted_rows. An entry is written the way the ROW is written:
a bare label for a row named by one anchor, the two fields for a row named by
two. Both spellings in one list.

  omitted_rows: ["Licenses & Permits"]
  omitted_rows:
    - {label: "Transfer From Wastewater", label_tail: "to Stormwater"}

Implemented as mapping.OmittedRow with an UnmarshalYAML that accepts a scalar
or a mapping. Matching is on Row.Identity(), the same key the row index uses,
so an entry addresses exactly one row and no author has to type a \x1f.
Rejected alternative: one string spelling both anchors -- that would mean
asserting the run of spaces the page prints between the fields, which is the
one thing label_tail exists in order not to do. Every existing declaration is
unchanged: the scalar form is still the scalar form.

FAIL-CLOSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, as required:
  - names no row      -> "%q is not one of this rule's rows" (unchanged)
  - names more than one -> "Transfer From General Fund" names 3 rows, which
    differ only in their label_tail: [...]; hint: a row named by two anchors is
    omitted by naming both
  - declared twice, blank label, whitespace-padded label_tail: all refused
  - KnownFields(true) does not reach a custom unmarshaler, so unknown keys are
    refused inside UnmarshalYAML: label_tial would otherwise be dropped and the
    entry would silently name a different row

THE FOUR FIXES, each with the message its mutation produces:

(1) parse.go omitted_rows validated on Identity() [internal/mapping/parse.go]
    mutate -> rowIndex[o.Label]:
    TestATwoAnchorRowIsOmittedByNamingBothAnchors: two-anchor.yaml: rule
    "two-anchor": parts[page 76].omitted_rows: "Transfer From General Fund to
    Wastewater" is not one of this rule's rows

(2) ActiveRows + resolve.go omissions() filter on Identity() [rule.go via the
    new omittedSet helper, shared by both so they cannot drift]
    mutate -> set keyed on Label:
    TestActiveRowsDropOnlyTheRowNamed: ActiveRows (-want +got): + "Transfer
    From General Fund to Wastewater" -- i.e. one entry dropped all three rows,
    and TestATwoAnchorRowIsOmittedByNamingBothAnchors then fails at resolve
    time with: rows: row "Transfer From General Fund": second anchor "to
    Wastewater" does not occur after it

(2b) NOT IN THE DESCRIPTION: resolve.go canonicalRows() paired active rows to
    rule rows on Label too, so with an omission the surviving rows got the
    OMITTED row's RowIndex -- values and omissions then land in the same slot,
    which is exactly what Omission.RowIndex's doc says must not happen.
    mutate -> Label:
    TestATwoAnchorRowIsOmittedByNamingBothAnchors: value 2 has RowIndex 1,
    want 2

(3) total_row "is also listed in rows" guard now tests the row's Label (and its
    PrintedLabel), not rowIndex. A total_row is a plain string the author types
    and the resolver finds in the page text, so it can NEVER equal an Identity()
    carrying a \x1f -- testing the index disabled the guard outright.
    mutate -> rowIndex[r.TotalRow]:
    TestTotalRowInRowsIsRefusedForATwoAnchorRow: parsed; a total_row that is
    also a data row double-counts it

(4) the blank label_tail branch is now reachable: the blank test runs BEFORE the
    whitespace test, so "   " is reported as blank instead of as stray
    whitespace. Keeping it (rather than deleting it) is worth it because the two
    messages send the author to different places -- one to trim a character, one
    to name the anchor they meant.
    mutate -> original order:
    TestBlankLabelTailIsReportedAsBlank: error does not say the tail is blank:

title: [bug] p140 Total Sources exceeds the pages it closes by ~$57M, differently per column
description:
p0140.txt:52 prints, as the closing line of the REVENUE SOURCES BY FUNDS /
OTHER FUNDS run (pp.131-140):

  Total Sources    $201,271,189   $219,927,720   $219,633,968   $216,596,302

Nothing on those pages sums to it, and the shortfall is a DIFFERENT amount in
every column, so it is not a rounding artefact and not a single omitted fund.

MEASURED off data/extracted, by summing the 69 printed `Total <fund>` lines on
pp.131-140 (all four columns, dashes excluded, no figure typed in):

  printed         summed          gap
  201,271,189     142,497,642     58,773,547   FY2023-24 actual
  219,927,720     161,091,271     58,836,449   FY2024-25 revised
  219,633,968     163,141,134     56,492,834   FY2025-26 budget
  216,596,302     159,222,794     57,373,508   FY2026-27 budget

(The FY2023-24 sum is 142,497,642 against fisc-u2v's 142,497,640; the $2 is the
document's own rounding in that column, which fisc-2sd declares per block.)

THE FIGURE APPEARS NOWHERE ELSE IN THE CORPUS. Verified:
`grep -rl "219,633,968" data/extracted` returns p0140.txt and its own
geometry/p0140.json, and nothing else across all 786 extracted pages.

WHY THIS IS A FINDING AND NOT A FOOTNOTE. fisc-5gk.1 maps these ten pages and
fisc-u2v's decision rests on them being a COMPLETE, EXACT, ALTERNATIVE
DECOMPOSITION of the spine's revenue side -- which they are, per fund group, to
the cent. A printed total on the same pages that exceeds their own contents by
~$57M is either (a) a claim about money the schedule does not itemise, or
(b) a total over a wider set than the pages it closes. Neither reading is
recorded anywhere, and fisc-u2v names it only in passing while ruling it
unassertable.

The name is the clue worth chasing: SOURCES, not REVENUES. The
headline-ties-to-revenues-not-sources memory records that on pp.66-67 TOTAL
SOURCES = revenues + transfers in, a different printed row from TOTAL REVENUES.
So the likeliest explanation is that p140's Total Sources includes a component
the fund sections do not itemise -- use of fund balance being the obvious
candidate. That is a hypothesis, NOT a finding; it has not been checked.

WHAT SETTLING IT BUYS. If the gap has a published decomposition, this row
becomes a real check on the lane. If it does not, the lane must SAY so -- via
the reason channel the cross-rule rollup bead asks for -- rather than mapping
ten pages and silently declining to mention that the page's own closing total
does not reconcile.

DO NOT resolve it with a stated_total_deltas entry. A $57M delta is not the
city's rounding, and fisc-2sd cannot catch a fictional declaration.

Found while verifying the backlog waves, 2026-08-22, from fisc-u2v DEFECT 4.
acceptance_criteria: the gap between p140's printed Total Sources and the sum of pp.131-140's fund totals is explained from published figures, or the lane declares the row unassertable through a reason channel that says the DOCUMENT prints a total this rule structure cannot reconcile; no stated_total_deltas entry absorbs it
notes:
2026-08-24 INVESTIGATED AND SETTLED, and the bead's own hypothesis is REFUTED
rather than merely unproven. Every figure below was derived by summing the pages
in data/extracted; nothing is typed in but the printed totals being tested.

THE GAP, reproduced exactly as the bead states it. Summing the 69 printed
`Total <fund>` lines on pp.131-140, all four columns:

  printed p0140.txt:52   summed 69       gap
  201,271,189            142,497,642     58,773,547   FY2023-24 actual
  219,927,720            161,091,271     58,836,449   FY2024-25 revised
  219,633,968            163,141,134     56,492,834   FY2025-26 budget
  216,596,302            159,222,794     57,373,508   FY2026-27 budget

FUND BALANCE IS NOT THE MISSING COMPONENT. The bead names "use of fund balance"
as the obvious candidate. The non-General-Fund aggregate draw on fund balance,
read off pp.68-75, is 10,849,816 / 53,470,745 / -2,938,500 / 6,607,809. In
FY2025-26 those funds COLLECTIVELY ADD $2.9M to fund balance while the gap in
that column is +$56.5M. Even the most generous reading -- summing only the
positive draws group by group and ignoring the funds that add -- gives
19,087,150 / 55,750,717 / 9,244,229 / 15,958,968, which misses every column.
The hypothesis is refuted, not open.

NOR IS IT THE GENERAL FUND. Adding p0130.txt:40's Total General Fund
(142,028,002 / 148,800,148 / 157,873,470 / 164,358,147) gives 284,525,644 /
309,891,419 / 321,014,604 / 323,580,941, which OVERSHOOTS the printed row by
83,254,455 / 89,963,699 / 101,380,636 / 106,984,639. That combined figure is
itself the real all-funds total: p0063.txt:22 prints `Total Sources - All Funds
285,263,097 / 314,930,752 / 321,495,004 / 324,067,676`, the small differences
being General Fund transfers in (p0068.txt:17, 737,455) and the capital
4,125,627 named below. So 201,271,189 is NEITHER the Other-Funds total
(142.5M) NOR the all-funds total (285.3M): it sits between them and matches
neither in any column.

NO PUBLISHED DECOMPOSITION EXISTS. Three exhaustive searches, each requiring
agreement in ALL FOUR columns simultaneously, all returning zero solutions:
all subsets of the 21 citywide revenue-category aggregates; all subsets and all
SIGNED +/-1 combinations of a 29-item pool (fund-type totals, transfers out to
CIP, non-major revenues and transfers, total expenses, beginning balances); and
all 0/1/2-coefficient combinations of the 15 fund-type revenue and transfer-in
components, which is the level at which the book actually builds its totals.
Subset-sum on any SINGLE column is satisfiable -- the values are numerous and
small -- which is exactly why the four-column requirement is the honest test.

AND THE FIGURE OCCURS NOWHERE ELSE. `grep -r` over all 786 extracted pages of
all three documents finds 201,271,189 / 219,927,720 / 219,633,968 / 216,596,302
only on p0140.txt:52 and in its own geometry/p0140.json. The four GAP figures
(58,773,547 / 58,836,449 / 56,492,834 / 57,373,508) appear NOWHERE AT ALL.

Closest near-misses, all coincidences that fail another column badly, recorded
so nobody re-finds them and believes them: gap col 1 vs Other-Funds Charges for
Services FY23-24 58,881,835 (0.18% off, cols 2-4 miss by 4-18%); gap col 2 vs
the CIP five-year plan's FY2024-25 total 59,192,538 (cip p0218.txt:43, 0.6%
off); gap col 4 vs FY26-27 CIP-fund sources 58,988,871 (p0204.txt:19, 2.8%).

RESOLUTION: Rollup.Unassertable, which internal/mapping/rule.go:162-173 already
names this row and this bead for. NOT stated_total_deltas -- a $57M delta is not
the city's rounding, and fisc-2sd catches a STALE declaration but has no way to
catch a FICTIONAL one, which is the bead's own instruction.

A SECOND REASON THE ROLLUP CHANNEL IS THE ONLY ONE, found while checking this
and not previously recorded: a `covers` rollup over the 69 fund rules is
IMPOSSIBLE by construction, whatever p140's arithmetic turned out to be.
CheckRollup compares whole Column values including Column.Fund
(internal/mapping/resolve.go:1023, firstDifferingColumn at :1408-1428, landed
a3adb0e), and each of the 69 rules carries a different fund number. So
`unassertable` is not merely the honest route here, it is the available one.

WHAT THE INVESTIGATION ESTABLISHED POSITIVELY, which is the more useful half and
is NEW: pp.131-140 are a complete and internally exact schedule, corroborated by
two citywide pages the lane does not map. Summing the 69 fund totals BY FUND
GROUP against p0063.txt:16-21 (Table 2, Total Sources - All Funds):

  group             n   FY2024        FY2025        FY2026        FY2027
  enterprise        9   +1            tie           tie           tie
  capital          13   -1            -4,125,627    tie           tie
  debt-service      3   tie           tie           tie           tie
  permanent         1   tie           tie           tie           tie
  special-revenue  38   +2            +500          tie           tie
  internal-service  5   tie           tie           tie           tie

FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 TIE EXACTLY IN ALL SIX GROUPS -- the two columns
fisc-u2v's decision rests on. FY2023-24 ties within the document's own rounding
(+1/-1/+2, the same blocks fisc-2sd declares). FY2024-25 does NOT, and both
discrepancies are explained from published pages:

  - CAPITAL SHORT BY 4,125,627. p0194.txt:29 prints `General Fund CIP Reserves
    $34,954,363 | - | $4,125,627 | $39,079,990` and p0192.txt:14 carries it into
    the capital line as `Revenues 30,713,648 + Transfers In 4,125,627`. My sum of
    the 13 capital fund totals is 30,713,648 -- p192's REVENUES figure to the
    cent -- and NO capital fund on pp.132-134 prints a Transfers In row at all.
    So the money is a transfer into a fund pp.131-140 print no section for.
    p0198.txt:14 and p0204.txt:14 print `-` in that column, which is exactly why

  - SPECIAL REVENUE OVER BY 500. p0139.txt:56 prints `Oth Financing Source - |

    p0192.txt:11 excludes it too (Revenues 18,980,619 + Transfers In 685,500 =
    19,666,119 against my 19,666,619). Two independent citywide schedules agree.
    This is the FIRST published evidence anywhere about where
    `other-financing-sources` lands in the citywide roll-up, and the answer is
    that it lands nowhere: data/taxonomy.yaml:279-289 says "which of the ten p66
    categories absorbs this line is not printed anywhere in the document" and

TWO LABELLED SPECULATIONS about the row itself, neither checkable in this
corpus, recorded so the next reader does not repeat the search: (a) the row is
stale, carried from the prior FY2023-25 book whose Other-Funds section covered a
different fund set -- that book is not in data/extracted; (b) it is an ERP query
over a wider account set (CIP, gross interfund activity) the book never
publishes.
close_reason:
Settled, no code. The gap has no published decomposition and the bead's own
fund-balance hypothesis is REFUTED: in FY2025-26 the non-General-Fund groups
collectively ADD $2.9M to fund balance against a +$56.5M gap. Adding the General
Fund overshoots by $83-107M and lands past p0063.txt:22's real all-funds total.
Three exhaustive searches -- all subsets of the citywide revenue aggregates, all

Resolution is Rollup.Unassertable, which rule.go:162-173 already names this row

values including Column.Fund and each rule carries a different number. The YAML

The positive half is the more useful one and is new: pp.131-140 ARE complete and

groups -- the two columns fisc-u2v's decision rests on -- and FY2023-24 ties
within fisc-2sd's rounding. FY2024-25 does not, and both discrepancies are
