lede, the tiles, the chart, the footer basis and the data-year-path citation are
all FY 2025-26. Fix either way: read the checked input in wireYears and open on
that year, or force input.checked back onto years[0] when wiring.

(2) THE THEME BUTTON INVERTS WHEN THE OS SWITCHES THEME UNDER IT. wireTheme's
`sync` is a local closure and the prefers-color-scheme listener is wired to
`paint` alone. A reader with no stored theme opens in light mode (button reads
"Dark mode", aria-pressed="false") and the OS auto-switches to dark at sunset:
the CSS media rule darkens the page and paint() re-reads the palette, but the
button still announces aria-pressed="false" on a dark page -- and because
prefersDark() now returns true, clicking the button labelled "Dark mode" makes
the page LIGHT. Wiring the listener to a function that calls both sync() and
paint() fixes both halves.

A THIRD, IN THE STYLESHEET, and it is the one with a measured number attached.
site/style.css's `.year-toggle:disabled { opacity: 0.55 }` silently invalidates
the contrast table 20 lines below it, in exactly the state that comment says a
no-JS reader sees for the WHOLE VISIT. The table measures the selection ring at
7.11:1 light / 8.26:1 dark against WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 -- opaque-element numbers.
The fieldset ships `disabled`, so with JS off (or if app.js 404s) the group
composites at 55% over --plane throughout. Recomputed with the model that
reproduces their 7.11 exactly: ring vs fill falls to 2.51:1 in light (BELOW
3:1) and 3.47:1 in dark, and the selected year's label text to 4.17:1 (below
1.4.3's 4.5:1). Since the fill is identical between checked and unchecked --
the comment's own 1.000:1 finding -- that 2.51:1 ring is the ONLY remaining
signal of which year is on screen for a no-JS reader in light mode. Dim
something other than the whole group, or re-derive the ring token for the 0.55
case. See fisc-6at, which is about the same stylesheet's numbers being pinned
by nothing.
acceptance_criteria: the year toggle names the year the page is drawing after F5 and after Back; the theme button's label and aria-pressed follow an OS theme change; the disabled fieldset's ring meets 3:1 or the measured table says what it actually measures
notes:
2026-08-27 THE YEAR-TOGGLE HALF IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, twice, in /code-review of the drill-down branch.

site/app.js's main() ends with showYear(years[0]) and never reads the radio's checked state, and index.html.tmpl ships the year radios with no autocomplete="off". So: select FY2026-27, press F5. The browser restores the user-modified radio to FY2026-27, wireYears re-enables the fieldset, and the page draws data/sankey.json -- the toggle reads FY2026-27 while the tiles, lede, <title>, footer basis and chart all read FY2025-26. No change event fires, so it never self-corrects.

That is verbatim the state index.html.tmpl's own comment calls worse than no control. Either autocomplete="off" on the inputs or opening on the checked radio closes it; the second is better, because it makes the restored selection do what the reader expects rather than discarding it.

title: Sankey.Graph validates its column count and never its scope, so the spine is the one document that does not fail closed on a foreign schedule
description:
FOUND BY /code-review 2026-08-26, reproduced by calling the function.

internal/project/sankey.go's Graph checks len(o.Columns) and never looks at
o.Scope. Trends.Document does (internal/project/trends.go), refusing a foreign
scope with a hint. So:

  (&Sankey{}).Graph(facts, Options{Columns: []Column{{2026, BasisAdopted}},
                                   Scope: TrendsScope, Version: "x"})

returns a FULLY FORMED GRAPH built over the pp.127-140 revenue-by-fund rows:
netCells groups them by (kind, category, fund_group) and emits
revenue/<cat> -> fund-group/<group> links, with metadata.scope
"revenue-by-fund" and a headline.all_funds_gross_revenue_cents that is a
DIFFERENT total from the spine's.

UNREACHABLE TODAY and that is not the point. Sankey.Slices and slicesOf's
fallback both pin PublishedScope, so nothing in the tree calls it this way. The
asymmetry is the defect: Options.Scope's own doc comment says the field exists
to stop the fisc-u2v doubling, and the one document the site publishes as its
headline is the one that does not enforce it, while the newer and smaller
document does.

FIX: the same refusal Trends.Document makes, in the same shape and with the
same hint, so the two projections agree about what Scope is for.

A SECOND, SMALLER THING FROM THE SAME REVIEW, filed here because it is one line
in the same file: Sankey has `var _ Projection = (*Sankey)(nil)` but no
`var _ Sliced = (*Sankey)(nil)`, unlike Trends which asserts both. Sliced is
consumed ONLY through runtime type assertions (pkg/cmd/export/data.go,
internal/check/subject.go). If Sankey.Slices' signature ever drifts -- someone
drops the `version` parameter -- everything still compiles, both assertions
silently return false, `fisc export` falls back to
PublishedFiscalYears() x PublishedBasis and `fisc verify` to factSlices, and
the spine stops being built over the years it declares with no compile error
anywhere. That is the blank-ident-assert idiom, and the spine is the case it
matters most for.
acceptance_criteria: Sankey.Graph refuses a scope it is not of, in the shape Trends.Document already uses; Sankey carries a compile-time Sliced assertion; a test calls Graph with a foreign scope directly
close_reason:
Landed in 2949e96. Sankey.Graph refuses a foreign scope in Trends.Document's shape and with the same hint; Sankey gains the var _ Sliced assertion it lacked. TestGraphRefusesAForeignSchedule calls Graph directly, which is the only way to reach it, and was proved failable by removing the guard.

ONE CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD, measured while landing it. The text says the foreign-scope build returns 'a headline.all_funds_gross_revenue_cents that is a DIFFERENT total from the spine's'. IT IS THE SAME TOTAL -- 29,996,900,700 both -- and necessarily so, because revenue-detail-ties-to-spine is the check that makes pp.127-140 sum to pp.66-67's figure to the cent. The defect is STRUCTURAL: 17 nodes against the spine's 25 and 29 links against its 58, with no expenditure side, no fund balance and no transfers out, published under the spine's contract. A reader looking for the wrong number would not have found one.

title: publishedProjectionBuilt unions each projection's columns, so verify passes a corpus export refuses
description:
SPLIT OUT OF fisc-rmx, whose 2026-08-26 note ends "whoever takes this should
decide whether that asymmetry is its own bead". A slice touching
internal/check/coverage.go four times opened that file and did not fix it, so it
is filed rather than left in a note on a bead about something else.

THE DEFECT. publishedProjectionBuilt (internal/check/coverage.go) keys its
built-set on struct{name, scope} and UNIONS each matching projection's columns.
So a spine carrying two BASES for one fiscal year -- an FY2026 revised column
mapped beside the adopted one -- unions to {2026 adopted, 2026 revised, 2027
adopted} and satisfies every published document. The check passes.

`fisc export` REFUSES the same corpus. stemFor tells documents apart by
project.PublishedStem(name, o.Columns[0].FiscalYear) -- year alone -- so the two
FY2026 slices compute the same stem and the duplicate-stem guard fires, taking
the whole export down including the files that were fine.

WHY IT MATTERS SEPARATELY FROM fisc-rmx. fisc-rmx owns making the stem a
function of the whole column list, which is a four-site change across
pkg/cmd/export and internal/project plus published URLs. THIS is the smaller
and differently-shaped claim: verify's job is to tell you before export does,
and here it tells you the opposite. A check that greens a corpus the next
command in the pipeline rejects is worse than no check, because it is the one a
reader trusts to have looked.

Whether the fix is to key the built-set on the columns rather than union them,
or to have this check compare against what stemFor would produce, is the
decision. The first is local to coverage.go; the second couples a check to a
command's naming scheme, which this package has avoided elsewhere.

Found by /code-review 2026-08-26, and independently in fisc-rmx's own planning
pass the same day.
acceptance_criteria: a spine carrying two bases for one fiscal year is reported by fisc verify rather than passing; the finding names the collision export would hit
close_reason:
Landed in be735a5. The union is gone: a published document is covered by ONE slice, and a slice no published document claims is reported naming the stem it would take and the document already there.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD LEFT OPEN IS ANSWERED: the check asks project.PublishedStem, not pkg/cmd/export's stemFor. PublishedStem is the shared declaration and its own doc comment says it lives beside the year list 'because fisc verify has to name the same documents the site serves in order to say one of them was not built'. Reaching into the command's helper would have been the coupling this package avoids elsewhere.

BOTH HALVES MEASURED END TO END. verify reported PASS on a spine carrying FY2026 revised beside FY2026 adopted, and fisc export over the same corpus printed 'the sankey and sankey projections both want the stem "sankey": FY2026 adopted and FY2026 revised' and wrote NO file at all.

A SECOND DEFECT OF THE UNION THIS BEAD DOES NOT NAME, and it is the quieter one: N single-column slices satisfied an N-column document. project.MissingColumns returns empty for revenue-trends' four declared columns against a union of four one-column slices, so a Trends returning one slice per column would ship four files with verify green and the file at the declared stem covering a quarter of what it declares. Export SUCCEEDS there -- no loud guard -- so it would have shipped.

title: Map the ACFR MD&A tables, pp.34-46: the only source in the corpus that declares a coarser unit
description:
FILED 2026-08-26 to give fisc-1wr.2 something real to block on. Until this
exists, the document-derived tolerance that bead is named for has ZERO
consumers, and a P0 with no consumer heads bd ready every session.

WHY THIS IS THE ONLY CANDIDATE, measured off data/extracted (re-derived on
fisc-1wr.2, 2026-08-22): the Budget Book (268 pages) and the CIP (323 pages)
contain ZERO occurrences of "(in millions)", "(in thousands)" or the word
"rounding". Only the ACFR declares a coarser precision -- seven MD&A pages
captioned "(in Millions)" (p0034, p0036, p0039, p0041, p0042, p0045, p0046),
plus one Statistical Section page, p0170:8 "(In thousands)", which belongs to
fisc-4ua.4 and is blocked there on the non-amount-column decision.

AND THE MD&A GENUINELY NEEDS IT, which is what makes this a real dependency
rather than a placeholder. ACFR p0034 Table 1, governmental activities 2025:
729.2 + 38.2 - 280.1 - 3.5 = 483.8 against a printed total net position of
483.9. The Total column the same: 1,085.6 + 43.1 - 321.5 - 14.2 = 793.0 against
793.1. Four terms at unit 0.1 gives a 0.2 tolerance and the observed error is
0.1. The other four columns of that table tie EXACTLY, which is what makes
these two the document's own rounding rather than a misread. An exact gate can
never go green here: the pages are footnoted "Due to rounding amounts may
differ from what's reported on the financial statements" (p0034.txt:32 and :56;
p0036.txt:7 and :47 says it again).

THE UNIT IS THE LEAST SIGNIFICANT PRINTED DIGIT, NOT THE CAPTION'S WORD. The
MD&A says "(in Millions)" and prints tenths, so unit is $100,000. Reading the
caption instead would give a four-term sum $2,000,000 of slack. This is
fisc-1wr.2's rule and it is restated here because it is the thing this page
will test.

SCOPE: this is a MAPPING bead, not a verification one. It needs the pages read,
a scope decided (the MD&A is a summary of the same money the statements
publish, so the fisc-u2v doubling question applies and must be answered before
anything is published), Rule.Units carrying millions, and the tolerance from
fisc-1wr.2 landing beside it. Nothing here is started.

NOT VERIFIED: the 0.2-covers-0.1 arithmetic above is done by hand on fisc-1wr.2
and could be wrong about which four terms a rule would actually sum. No ACFR
page has ever been mapped.
acceptance_criteria: an ACFR MD&A page is mapped and published; its stated totals reconcile under a tolerance derived from the printed unit and the term count, and a tolerance one unit too tight goes red

title: A projection's stem must be a function of its whole column list, not its first fiscal year
description:
SPLIT OUT OF fisc-lmz, whose two safe halves landed in 19a580f (the unchecked Columns[0] index and the guard's misattributed message). This is the part that is NOT a one-function fix, and the split was made on peer review of the landing plan.

THE DEFECT. Sankey.Slices derives one slice per (fiscal year, basis) pair the spine carries; stemFor tells the resulting documents apart by project.PublishedStem(name, o.Columns[0].FiscalYear) -- YEAR ALONE. So the instant the spine carries two BASES for one year (an FY2026 revised column mapped beside the adopted one), Slices declares two slices, stemFor computes the same stem for both, and the duplicate-stem guard fires. Sankey.Slices' own doc comment presents mapping a revised column as needing no other change; that claim is false while stemFor is year-keyed.

NOTE THE GUARD FIRING IS CORRECT. It fails closed with a good message, and that is not what to fix. What the bead objects to is that the collision is REACHABLE -- and that it takes 'fisc export' down entirely, so no file is written including the ones that were fine.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-FUNCTION CHANGE, measured: stems are computed in THREE places -- pkg/cmd/export/data.go stemFor, pkg/cmd/export/data.go yearStems (the client config's per-year 'stem' field), internal/project/project.go PublishedDocuments -- compared in TWO more (internal/check/subject.go, internal/check/coverage.go), and rebuilt in internal/check/fixture_test.go. Changing only stemFor splits the written files from the config's stems, from assertPublishedBuilt, and from published-projection-built.

AND STEMS ARE PUBLISHED URLS. data/sankey.json is promised by docs/sankey-contract.md, data/revenue-trends.json by docs/revenue-trends-contract.md, and the stem is the year radio's value in site/app.js (years.find(y => y.stem === target.value)). A scheme that renamed them would break both the contract and the toggle.
acceptance_criteria: a spine carrying two bases for one fiscal year exports two distinct stems and does not abort; the stem is derived from the whole Column list in ONE place that all three current call sites use; a test pins the literal strings sankey, sankey-2027 and revenue-trends unchanged for today's corpus; docs/sankey-contract.md and Sankey.Slices' doc comment agree with whatever ships
notes:
2026-08-26, from planning-time exploration rather than implementation. THREE CORRECTIONS AND ONE ADDITION to this bead's own text.

(1) IT CITES TestStemForDistinguishesAYearFromAWhole, WHICH EXISTS NOWHERE IN THE TREE. It was a phantom citation in pkg/cmd/export/data.go's comment, corrected in 034dfa8 for exactly this reason; the bead text inherited it. The real test is TestStemForAsksHowManyDocumentsNotHowManyColumns (pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go), and it pins only ONE of the two directions this bead claims: every case uses PublishedBasis or a basis that is unique per year, so no case exercises two bases for one year.

(2) STEMS ARE DERIVED IN FOUR PLACES, NOT THREE. The bead lists data.go stemFor, data.go yearStems and project.go PublishedDocuments. internal/check/fixture_test.go spineDocuments is a fourth, and it hardcodes PublishedBasis alongside the year.

(3) yearStems IS THE ONE THAT BITES, and the bead does not say why. It re-derives PublishedStem(name, y) over PublishedFiscalYears() and filters to what was built -- so a stem stemFor produced that yearStems cannot reconstruct FROM A YEAR ALONE gets written to disk and never offered to the reader. Any scheme keyed on more than the year has to change both or the toggle silently loses a document.

THE ADDITION, and it is worth more than the corrections: fisc verify WOULD NOT CATCH THIS. publishedProjectionBuilt (internal/check/coverage.go) keys on struct{name, scope} and UNIONS each projection's columns, so a spine carrying two bases for 2026 unions to {2026 adopted, 2026 revised, 2027 adopted} and satisfies every published document. verify passes a corpus export refuses. Whoever takes this should decide whether that asymmetry is its own bead.

AND A FIFTH SITE, outside Go: site/index.html.tmpl renders the year radios as id="year-{{$y.Year}}" with <label for=...> keyed on the same integer. Two documents for one fiscal year produce duplicate DOM ids and a label pointing at whichever radio parsed first -- independently of what the stem is called.
close_reason:
Landed in a197be7. project.Stem is the one spelling of the rule, reading the whole column list; stemFor delegates, yearStems reads the declared stems instead of rebuilding them (the fourth derivation is gone, not moved), and site/index.html.tmpl keys the year radio ids on the stem rather than the year.

THE LITERALS ARE UNCHANGED AND PINNED: sankey, sankey-2027, revenue-trends (TestTheCommittedStemsAreUnchanged). Verified end to end: a spine carrying FY2026 revised beside FY2026 adopted now exports sankey, sankey-2026-revised, sankey-2027 and revenue-trends and does not abort. Before, dist/ was empty.

/code-review CAUGHT THE SAME MISTAKE ONE LEVEL DOWN and it is worth recording, because the bead's acceptance criterion did not reach it. Stem first took a COUNT of documents, and the count meant three different things at its three call sites: pkg/cmd/export counted the slices a projection DECLARED, internal/check counted the ones that BUILT and only within one scope, and PublishedDocuments counted published YEARS. One spelling of the rule over three spellings of its input establishes nothing. Stem takes the declared list itself now, and internal/check assembles it from the built and the refused together -- which is the list export names its files from.

A COHERENCE PROPERTY NOTHING HELD, found reproducing that review finding: Stem gives the bare name to PublishedFiscalYear while PublishedDocuments walks PublishedFiscalYears(), and nothing made the constant the list's first entry. Editing one alone makes the declaration name a stem every derivation computes differently. Pinned by TestTheOpeningPublishedYearOpensTheYearList.

fisc-lmz closes with it -- its remaining half was this bead.

title: The footer's scope, basis and cited pages are the opening year's, and paintYearWords never repaints them
description:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26, alongside fisc-yi4 and distinct from it. fisc-yi4 is about clientConfig.Docs; this is about the footer's own prose.

site/index.html.tmpl:196 renders 'Scope {{.Scope}}, basis {{.Basis}}' and :184 renders the list of cited pages, both from the OPENING year's metadata. paintYearWords writes year.basis into #lede-year and #chart-title and rewrites [data-year-path], but touches neither of these.

yearView carries a per-year Basis precisely because it varies. Publish a year on a 'proposed' basis, or one citing pp.68-69 instead of pp.66-67, and after a switch the lede reads 'FY 2026-27 proposed' while the footer three screens down reads 'basis adopted' and cites the other year's pages -- one page stating two different things about one document.

LATENT TODAY because both published years are adopted and cite the same two pages. Same shape as fisc-yi4 and probably wants the same landing: the union across years for the page list, and a per-year repaint for the basis.
close_reason: The footer's basis follows the year through #page-basis. The cited-page half of this bead was already fixed by 19a580f (unionSources) and the bead text was stale; the footer's <h3> now says it covers every year the page can show, rather than leaving a reader to assume the narrower set. Scope is NOT repainted and must not be: it cannot vary (Sankey.Slices fixes it) and the lede states the same claim again in prose that no switch touches, so a repaint would fix one of two copies. buildSankeyPage refuses a year stem whose scope or generated_by disagrees instead. Both extra guards and the lede/footer coupling pin came out of /code-review of this change.

title: A year document that parses but throws while drawing leaves the page split across two years
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26, while fisc-8cg was landing. It is the residue
of that fix rather than something it caused, and it is filed because the fix's
own harness drives the exact document and asserts only half of what matters.

site/app.js showYear: the try now covers the fetch AND response.json(), which is
what fisc-8cg widened it for. It does NOT cover the drawing that follows.
paintYearWords(year) runs FIRST, then buildLegend / buildDerivedList /
buildTable / render, none of them guarded.

SO: a year document that parses, passes the schema gate, and is structurally
wrong -- a null or absent nodes array is enough, and nothing validates that the
keys the schema_version promises are present -- throws in buildLegend. The
change handler's .catch paints a banner, and the page is left with THE NEW
YEAR'S tiles, caveats, lede, <title> and [data-year-path] over THE OLD YEAR'S
chart and flow table.

That is a page whose words and whose figures are about different fiscal years,
with a citation link pointing at the year that is not drawn. It is the same
class fisc-fjy and the [data-year-path] repaint were about, reached from the
other side.

WHY THE HARNESS PASSES ON IT TODAY. The last case in tools/jscheck/lifecycle.mjs
-- "a year document that parses but will not draw is reported, not swallowed" --
feeds precisely this document and asserts ONLY that a banner appears. It does
not look at what the rest of the page now says. So `make js` is green over the
split state, and the check is right as far as it goes: extend it rather than
replace it.

TWO CANDIDATE SHAPES, and the choice is a real one.

  (1) DRAW FIRST, PAINT WORDS LAST. Move paintYearWords below render() so a
      throw leaves the page wholly on the old year with a banner over it. Small,
      and it makes the failure atomic in the direction that matters -- a page
      consistently showing the previous year is honest, a page showing two is
      not. Check the ordering does not break the tile/hero measurements
      year.mjs pins.

  (2) VALIDATE THE DOCUMENT'S SHAPE where understands() validates its version.
      Stronger, and it is what the schema_version gate already implies it does:
      the version is a promise about which keys exist and nothing checks that
      the promise was kept. More work, and it needs a decision about how much of
      the document to validate client-side when internal/check validates all of
      it server-side.

(1) is the smaller and probably right one; (2) is worth stating in the bead so
it is not re-derived.
acceptance_criteria: a year document that parses and then throws while drawing leaves the page wholly on the year it was already showing, with a banner; the existing lifecycle.mjs case is extended to assert the lede, tiles and data-year-path, not only that a banner appeared; year.mjs's tile and hero checks still pass
close_reason: Landed in 2439af3. render() is split into layOut(doc) (computes, touches nothing) and render(laid) (draws), and showYear lays out BEFORE repainting -- that ordering, not the gate, is what makes a failed draw leave the page wholly on the previous year. Mutation-verified both ways. Neither of the bead's two candidate shapes was taken: re-ordering the repaint only moves which half is stale, and widening the try would have left both .catch handlers with no reachable case (lifecycle.mjs says that makes them unfalsifiable claims). drawableSankey() beside understands() buys the MESSAGE only -- measured: nodes.map throws inside layOut, so with the gate deleted the page still refuses without splitting; what changes is 'the file is truncated' vs a TypeError shown to a reader. The check asserts the wording for that reason. The last-resort .catch keeps a reachable case via a new and more honest fixture: a link naming a node the document does not carry.

title: The trends page trusts counts it never checks, and buildCells drops a point it cannot place
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26, and reproduced with an overlay test.

internal/export/page.go's buildCells SILENTLY DROPS any point whose
(fiscal_year, basis) is not among metadata.columns, and its own comment
justifies that with "which is why the caller compares counts.points against what
it rendered". THE CALLER DOES NOT. trendsMetadata.Counts.Points is decoded and
read nowhere -- only .Facts and .Series are used -- so:

  A 1-column document with a 2-point series exports successfully, renders ONE
  cell, loses the other figure with NO error, and the lede still prints
  "1 columns, 2 figures in all".

That is a published page whose own prose contradicts what it drew, which is a
plausible wrong value with provenance disagreeing with it -- the class this
project exists to refuse. The same gap runs the other way: .Count is
counts.series and is never compared with len(body.Series).

NOT REACHABLE THROUGH internal/project TODAY, because Trends.Document filters
points on the same o.Columns the metadata is built from. So this is a packager
that does not fail closed, not a live corruption -- and the fix is the
comparison the comment already promises, not a redesign.

RELATED, SAME FILE, SAME SHAPE: internal/check/trends.go's two checks jointly
claim to cover the published document and do not cover this one corruption.
Verified: build a Trends document over [{2026 adopted}], append a GENUINE FY2027
point (every field matching its real fact), and trend-points-tie-to-facts passes
over 3 points while trend-series-are-complete passes over 2 series. comparePoint
compares a point only against its own fact, and the reverse sweep walks only
factsFor(p.Options); nothing compares a point's COLUMN against metadata.columns.
Fix both together or the packager's guard is the only one.
acceptance_criteria: buildTrendsPage refuses a document whose rendered cell count disagrees with counts.points, and whose series count disagrees with counts.series, naming both numbers; a test builds the 1-column-2-point document directly and shows the refusal; internal/check gains an arm comparing each published point's column against metadata.columns, with the append-a-real-point mutation as its evidence
close_reason: Landed in the packager/check commit. buildCells now reports what it PLACED and buildTrendsPage reconciles that against counts.points, plus len(series) against counts.series, naming both numbers; two points in one column is refused separately because the counts still reconcile in that case. The check gains a column-membership arm -- measured as invisible to both existing arms, since comparePoint compares a point to its own fact and the reverse sweep filters facts on the same columns. Evidence is a GENUINE appended FY2027 point, with trend-series-are-complete asserted green in the same run. fisc-ewt's QUIET block now asserts, and records the two checks as OVERLAPPING on a dropped point rather than dividing labour, reproduced by running the mutation.

title: Four checks in internal/check report a wrong verdict or wrong wording, and uncheckedDocuments has no test
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26. Four defects in one package, none of which
changes a published figure and all of which send a reader to the wrong place.
Filed together because they share one cause: an arm added for a shape that no
longer exists alone. Each was reproduced with a throwaway test.

(1) documents-are-checked CAN REPORT PASS HAVING EXAMINED NOTHING, which
documents.go's own comment calls the one thing this package exists to prevent.
`subjects` is len(s.Projections), which COUNTS projections exempted by
uncheckedDocuments, so the `nothing:` branch is unreachable once every
projection is declared. With uncheckedDocuments = {"blob": ...} and one
shapeless projection named blob: PASS, summary "0 projections structurally
checked (), plus 1 of \"blob\" (no checks yet) declared unchecked". Note also
the empty "()" from describeShapes over an empty map.

(2) THE STALE-DECLARATION FINDING HARDCODES THE GRAPH SHAPE
(documents.go:116). A declared projection carrying only a TrendsDocument reports
"every projection of that name now carries a graph" -- in the check that was
widened precisely so a document need not be a graph. It sends a reader looking
for a graph that does not exist.

(3) staleDeclarations ARM 1 MASKS ARM 3 (coverage.go:553). Arm 1 tests only
len(drawnSlices) > 0 && len(liveSlices) == 0 and never consults `carried`, so a
scope carrying NO facts reports "all 0 of its facts are in some projection's
slice; the declaration is exempting nothing and must be removed" whenever any
projection merely DECLARES that scope. The correct diagnosis -- carried == 0,
meaning no rule writes it, which is the mistyped-scope case the map exists for
-- is unreachable.

(4) STRANDED-FACT COUNTS ARE DOUBLE-REPORTED (coverage.go:385). `n` is summed
over keysOf(f.Options) for each ProjectionFailure independently while `refused`
is keyed only on (year, basis, scope), so two failures sharing a slice key each
claim the full count. Message-only, and the number is what a reader triages on.

AND THE REASON ALL FOUR SURVIVED: uncheckedDocuments (documents.go:29) SHIPS
WITH NO TEST AT ALL -- no emptiness guard, no exercise of its stale branch --
unlike its sibling incompleteSeries, which has TestIncompleteSeriesIsEmpty,
TestAStaleIncompleteSeriesDeclarationIsCaught and a withIncompleteSeries swap
helper. (1) and (2) are exactly what that missing test catches. Write it first.

FIFTH, SMALLER: subject.go's ProjectionFailure doc comment is left dangling by
an earlier edit -- "Neither is a verdict about the corpus: the first is a
programming error and the second is..." describes two items that no longer
exist, and mislabels the single remaining hard error. Line 174 is 105 chars,
past the file's wrap.
acceptance_criteria: uncheckedDocuments has an emptiness guard and a stale-branch test in the shape incompleteSeries already has; documents-are-checked counts only projections it EXAMINED, so a fully-declared run is vacuous rather than a pass over zero; its stale finding names the shape the projection actually carries; staleDeclarations consults carried before arm 1, so a scope no rule writes is diagnosed as that; a slice key shared by two refusals is counted once; ProjectionFailure's doc comment describes the arms that exist
notes:
2026-08-26 A FIFTH, confirmed independently by two reviewers in the same pass.

projections-build (coverage.go) reports a count of PROJECTIONS under the unit
"projection slices", and it under-reports on the committed corpus TODAY:

  PASS  projections-build  3 projection slices built, none refused

Six slices were built -- 2 sankey columns plus revenue-trends' 4. subjects is
len(s.Projections) + len(s.ProjectionFailures) and the unit says slices.

keysOf was added to this same file precisely because one Options is no longer
one slice -- its own comment says 'anything keying a map on a projection has to
iterate this rather than call it once' -- and Run does not use it.

WORSE THAN A WRONG NUMBER: with two multi-column projections failing, the
finding count can EXCEED the denominator, so the summary reads '7 findings over
3 projection slices'. A check whose numerator can pass its denominator is
reporting on two different things and calling them one.
close_reason: landed in 1f8c107, 056d355, 1ae566f; each defect reproduced with a test before being fixed

title: tools/jscheck cannot reach the flow table or the legend swatches: querySelector answers one selector shape
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26, while fisc-dn9 was landing. It is the same
species fisc-dn9 fixed and was left behind by it, so it is written down rather
than absorbed.

harness.mjs's element-level querySelector answers exactly one selector shape --
a bare class against the element's own descendants, added for `.refusal`. Two
things app.js does are therefore reached by NO check:

  (1) buildTable() does `el("flow-table").querySelector("tbody")` and returns at
      its `if (!body) return` guard in EVERY check. Probed after a full draw:
      flow-table has 0 children. The flow table is the largest part of what a
      year switch repaints and half of what fisc-kwq is about.
  (2) paint() loops `document.querySelectorAll("#legend button .key")` and gets
      [], so the swatch-recolouring half of theme-following never executes.
      Probed: legend has 6 buttons, derived-list 2 items, and every swatch's
      background is undefined.

Neither reads as a gap. Both read as green checks, which is the property that
makes this worth an id.

THE SHAPE, AND THE LINE NOT TO CROSS. harness.mjs says why it does not parse
CSS: "a selector engine here would be a second implementation of a thing the
browser already has". That argument survives. What is wanted is not an engine
but two more ANSWERED SHAPES, each the smallest thing that reaches a real code
path: a bare tag name among descendants, and a descendant chain of the
`#id tag .class` form. Both are mechanical; anything beyond them should be
planted with document.plant() instead, which is the escape hatch that already
exists.

WHAT TO CHECK ONCE IT IS REACHABLE, because a seam with no check on it is the
thing this bead is about: that a year switch replaces the flow table's rows
rather than appending them -- the fisc-kwq defect, in the part of the page
nothing has ever looked at -- and that paint() rewrites every legend swatch.
acceptance_criteria: buildTable() reaches its tbody under jscheck and a check asserts a year switch replaces the flow table's rows rather than appending; paint()'s legend-swatch loop executes and a check asserts every swatch is recoloured; the stub still refuses selector shapes it does not answer, visibly, rather than fabricating an element; harness.mjs's 'not a selector engine' rationale is restated against whatever ships
close_reason: Landed in a2ffffe. The stub's reach is now written down (KNOWN_SELECTORS) and pinned by seam.mjs against the shipped app.js, both directions mutation-verified. buildTable's tbody is reached by planting via selectable -- a bare-tag grammar would NOT have worked, because the stub's flow-table node has no children for any walk to find. paint()'s swatch loop is reached by drawing, reading back what buildLegend built, planting those and calling paint (now in NAMES; render() already called it, so no behaviour added). Making an unanswered selector THROW was measured and rejected: fail() and clearRefusal() both call querySelector, so the throw lands inside app.js's own error path and takes the run down. 'button' is declared unanswered rather than omitted, so the run prints that applyEmphasis's loop executes in no check. 30 checks to 33.

title: The footer's Sources and clientConfig.Docs are the OPENING year's, while CONFIG.years covers every year
design:
FOUND BY /code-review of the fisc-w7d landing, 2026-08-26. Latent today and
invisible when it fires, which is the worse pairing.

internal/export/page.go builds the footer's `Sources` list AND `clientConfig.Docs`
from the metadata of ONE document -- the view's opening year -- while CONFIG.years
lists every published year and site/app.js will happily switch to any of them.

WHAT BREAKS. app.js composes a citation link per cited fact as
CONFIG.docs[d].page_text_base + pNNNN.txt, and citations() skips a fact whose
doc_id is not in that map:

    if (!doc) continue;

So a published year whose document cites a doc_id the OPENING year does not --
an ACFR-backed column, a schedule mapped out of a different book -- has its
citations silently DROPPED. Not a 404, not a banner: the provenance panel simply
shows fewer rows than the chart has facts, and nothing says so. That is the
failure mode this project exists to prevent, arriving through the one channel
that produces no error.

The footer's Sources list has the same shape one level less severely: it would
advertise the opening year's pages under a chart drawn from another year's.

WHY IT IS LATENT. Both spine years cite pp.66-67 of the same document, so the
union and the opening year's set are equal today. It stops being latent the first
time two published years of one view cite different documents.

THE FIX IS THE ONE fisc-fjy ALREADY MADE ONE LEVEL UP, and that is the argument
for it being right. fisc-fjy made the SHIPPED page-text set the union over every
VIEW, and did it shape-blind through citationsOf -> metadata.sources, "the one
block every document carries whatever its body is". This is the same union over
every YEAR of a view, feeding clientConfig.Docs and the footer instead of the
copied files. Same helper, same reason.

Note the asymmetry that must survive: fisc-fjy's TestEachViewsFooterCitesItsOwnSources
asserts a view's footer does not advertise another VIEW's pages. That stays true
-- this is a union within one view, across its own years, not across views.
acceptance_criteria: clientConfig.Docs is the union over every year stem a view publishes, so no citation the client composes can name a doc_id the config omits; the footer's Sources likewise; TestEachViewsFooterCitesItsOwnSources still passes, because the union is within a view and not across views; a test builds a view whose second year cites a document the first does not and shows the citation surviving
notes:
2026-08-26 CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY by a second /code-review pass, with the test's own escape hatch named. TestEveryCitationTheClientComposesResolves degrades to t.Logf + continue in exactly the case this bead is about -- a year stem citing a doc_id the config does not carry -- and its `checked == 0` guard only catches TOTAL vacuity, so a run where one year of two resolves nothing still passes with a log line nobody reads. Fixing clientConfig.Docs without tightening that guard leaves the hole covered by a message. Also confirmed: buildSite ALREADY unions citations across every year for the shipped FILE SET (fisc-fjy), so the two halves disagree inside one function -- the files are unioned and the config that names them is not. 2026-08-26 A THIRD SITE, from the same cause, found by /code-review. Besides clientConfig.Docs, index.html.tmpl's footer renders 'Scope {{.Scope}}, basis {{.Basis}}' and its

Sources

page citations SERVER-SIDE from the opening year's metadata, and paintYearWords repaints only [data-year-path]. So after a switch the footer lists the opening year's PDF and extracted-text page numbers, and its basis, beside a chart drawn from the other schedule. Latent for the same reason as the rest of this bead -- both published years are adopted and cite pp.66-67 of one document -- and it becomes visible the moment two published years differ in basis. year.basis is already in CONFIG.years, so the client has what it needs; what is missing is the repaint and the per-year sources. This is the same defect the [data-year-path] hunk was added to fix, one element to the left, which is worth noting because that hunk shipped without anyone asking what ELSE in that paragraph was year-specific.
close_reason: Landed in 19a580f. The footer's Sources and clientConfig.Docs are now the union over every year of the view, accumulated in the loop that already decodes each year's metadata. Same shape fisc-fjy used one level up (union over VIEWs); the within-a-view/across-views asymmetry survives and TestEachViewsFooterCitesItsOwnSources still holds. Latent today, so the test builds the state: a second year citing the ACFR alongside the budget book, asserting FISC_CONFIG.docs carries both and the second year's page text ships. Mutation-verified.

title: stemFor tells documents apart by fiscal year alone, and Sankey.Slices keys on (year, basis)
design:
FOUND BY /code-review of the fisc-w7d landing, 2026-08-26. Latent today, and it
hard-fails the WHOLE export when it fires rather than shipping a wrong file --
so this is a blocked release, not a corrupted one.

THE TWO SPELLINGS. Sankey.Slices (internal/project/sankey.go) derives one slice
per (fiscal year, basis) pair the spine carries:

    for _, f := range facts {
        if f.Scope == PublishedScope { seen[key{f.FiscalYear, f.Basis}] = true }
    }

stemFor (pkg/cmd/export/data.go) tells the resulting documents apart by YEAR
alone, through project.PublishedStem(name, o.Columns[0].FiscalYear).

So the instant the spine carries two BASES for one year -- an FY2026 revised
column mapped beside the adopted one -- Slices declares two slices, stemFor
computes the same stem for both, and buildProjections' duplicate-stem guard
fires: "the sankey projection wants two documents at the stem \"sankey\"". That
guard is correct and fails closed with a good message. The defect is that it
fires at all, and that it takes `fisc export` down entirely: no file is written,
including the ones that were fine.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A LATENT BUG. Sankey.Slices' own doc comment presents
mapping a revised column as needing no other change -- the projection derives its
slices from whatever the store carries. That claim is false while stemFor is
year-keyed, and the person who discovers it is whoever maps pp.66-67's revised
column and finds the site will not build.

WHAT IT IS NOT. This is NOT the fisc-w7d published-set problem and is not fixed
by it. project.PublishedDocuments declares stems, so the PUBLISHED set is
unambiguous; this is about the stems of documents nobody declared, which is every
non-published slice a projection derives.

THE SHAPE. The stem has to be a function of what distinguishes the documents,
which is the whole Column list and not its first year. stemFor's own doc comment
already argues the general form -- "the column count is a property of a document;
the stem is a property of a SET of them" -- and the same argument applies one
level down to the basis. Candidates: suffix the basis when a year carries more
than one, or key the stem on project.Describe(o.Columns) slugified. The first
keeps data/sankey.json and data/sankey-2027.json exactly as they are today, which
the contract promises and every existing link depends on; the second does not.

Note TestStemForDistinguishesAYearFromAWhole and
TestStemForAsksHowManyDocumentsNotHowManyColumns already pin both directions
stemFor gets right; the new case goes beside them.
acceptance_criteria: a fact store carrying two bases for one published spine year builds two documents at two distinct stems rather than failing the export; data/sankey.json and data/sankey-2027.json are unchanged for the corpus as committed; a test constructs the two-basis store directly rather than waiting for the corpus to grow one
notes:
2026-08-26 THE TWO SAFE HALVES LANDED IN 19a580f: stemFor no longer indexes o.Columns[0] blind (it returns an error -- the bare index panics inside the command that writes files, leaving a half-exported directory), and the duplicate-stem guard now names BOTH projections, since builtAt spans the whole registry loop and a cross-projection collision read as a fault in whichever was second.

WHAT REMAINS IS THE STEM IDENTITY, and it is bigger than the bead implies. Stems are computed in THREE places (data.go stemFor, data.go yearStems, project.go PublishedDocuments), compared in TWO more (check/subject.go, check/coverage.go), rebuilt in check/fixture_test.go, AND are published URLs promised by docs/sankey-contract.md and used as the year radio's value in app.js. Changing only stemFor splits the written files from the config's stems and from published-projection-built. Needs a test pinning the literal strings sankey, sankey-2027, revenue-trends unchanged for today's corpus.

Note also, from peer review: the guard FIRING is correct fail-closed behaviour. What this bead objects to is that the collision is reachable at all, not that it is refused.
2026-08-26: this bead also cites TestStemForDistinguishesAYearFromAWhole, which exists nowhere in the tree (see fisc-rmx's note for the detail and for three more corrections). The real test is TestStemForAsksHowManyDocumentsNotHowManyColumns, and it does NOT pin the two-bases-for-one-year direction this bead is about.
close_reason:
Landed in a197be7. project.Stem is the one spelling of the rule, reading the whole column list; stemFor delegates, yearStems reads the declared stems instead of rebuilding them (the fourth derivation is gone, not moved), and site/index.html.tmpl keys the year radio ids on the stem rather than the year.

THE LITERALS ARE UNCHANGED AND PINNED: sankey, sankey-2027, revenue-trends (TestTheCommittedStemsAreUnchanged). Verified end to end: a spine carrying FY2026 revised beside FY2026 adopted now exports sankey, sankey-2026-revised, sankey-2027 and revenue-trends and does not abort. Before, dist/ was empty.

/code-review CAUGHT THE SAME MISTAKE ONE LEVEL DOWN and it is worth recording, because the bead's acceptance criterion did not reach it. Stem first took a COUNT of documents, and the count meant three different things at its three call sites: pkg/cmd/export counted the slices a projection DECLARED, internal/check counted the ones that BUILT and only within one scope, and PublishedDocuments counted published YEARS. One spelling of the rule over three spellings of its input establishes nothing. Stem takes the declared list itself now, and internal/check assembles it from the built and the refused together -- which is the list export names its files from.

A COHERENCE PROPERTY NOTHING HELD, found reproducing that review finding: Stem gives the bare name to PublishedFiscalYear while PublishedDocuments walks PublishedFiscalYears(), and nothing made the constant the list's first entry. Editing one alone makes the declaration name a stem every derivation computes differently. Pinned by TestTheOpeningPublishedYearOpensTheYearList.

fisc-lmz closes with it -- its remaining half was this bead.

title: tools/jscheck cannot drive an async path: the runner is synchronous and fetch is uninjectable
design:
fisc-8cg needs three checks that drive site/app.js's FETCH path, and the harness
can express none of them. This is filed separately because it is a change to a
SHARED TOOL that every check module runs on, not a change to the toggle -- and
because folding it into fisc-8cg as "unavoidable scope" is exactly how fisc-y0k's
own text says work becomes free: "without an id, it becomes free."

MEASURED against tools/jscheck at 92e657f. Five separate gaps:

(1) THE RUNNER IS FULLY SYNCHRONOUS. run.mjs:11 is `for (const c of [...layoutChecks(),
...yearChecks()])` with no await anywhere in the directory -- zero occurrences of
async or await in run.mjs, layout.mjs, year.mjs or harness.mjs. Each check's `ok`
is an already-evaluated boolean, usually an IIFE. A Promise assigned to `ok` is
truthy and reports PASS UNCONDITIONALLY, so an async check added today would be a
check that cannot fail. run.mjs must await, and the check modules become async.

(2) FETCH IS UNINJECTABLE AFTER THE FACT. harness.mjs:134-136 is a fixed
`fetch: () => Promise.reject(new Error("harness: no network"))`, and its comment
says "a check that wants a document installs its own" -- but there is no mechanism
and no check does. loadApp SPREADS the stub into a new sandbox object
(harness.mjs:166: `const sandbox = { console, Intl, ...stub }`) while `app.dom = stub`
hands back the original, so assigning app.dom.fetch changes nothing. And main()
has already run to completion by the time loadApp returns, because runInContext
(harness.mjs:204) executes app.js including `main().catch(...)` at app.js:1217.
Injection must therefore happen BEFORE runInContext, which means a loadApp
parameter, not a post-hoc assignment.

(3) FISC_CONFIG IS BAKED IN WITH ONE YEAR. harness.mjs:186-198 plants a
single-year config. wireYears bails at app.js:1172 on `years.length < 2`, so with
the default config there is no toggle, no change listener, and nothing a
"click during the opening fetch" check can drive except calling showYear directly
-- which is not the bug. A config seam is needed as well as a fetch seam. The id
side is already fine: "year-toggle" is in TEMPLATE_IDS (harness.mjs:47-51).

(4) DOCUMENT- AND WINDOW-LEVEL LISTENERS ARE DISCARDED, AND matchMedia IS
UNDEFINED. Element nodes record listeners (harness.mjs:73), but
`document.addEventListener() {}` (harness.mjs:113) and the window-level one
(harness.mjs:138) are NO-OPS, and matchMedia is undefined (harness.mjs:133) so
main()'s guard at app.js:1209 never enters under any check today. Proving "the
Escape handler is still attached" -- and dispatching an Escape to assert
resetDetail/setIsolated ran -- needs both recording.

WARNING FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: defining matchMedia changes prefersDark()
(app.js:936) for every currently-green check in layout.mjs. Re-run them; do not
assume the stub is additive.

(5) fail()'s BANNER IS UNREACHABLE, SO ASSERTING ITS ABSENCE IS VACUOUS. fail()
reaches the banner through `document.querySelector("main")` (app.js:987). The
stub answers by exact selector string out of a `selectable` map that starts empty
(harness.mjs:117-121), so `content` is always null and NO BANNER IS EVER CREATED
under jscheck. A check asserting "no .refusal banner" therefore passes against the
fixed and the unfixed app.js alike -- a check that cannot fail, which is this
project's defining defect. Such a check must document.plant("main", node) first
and inspect content.children for className === "refusal". Note the planted node's
querySelector returns null (harness.mjs:79) and node.remove() is a no-op
(harness.mjs:82), so clearRefusal (app.js:1008-1013) can neither find nor remove
one -- the stub needs to answer for real, or the check has to account for it.

DO NOT ADD main TO NAMES. main() is invoked at file scope during runInContext, so
exporting it hands back the FUNCTION, not the in-flight promise. Calling app.main()
boots a second page: a second wireTheme click listener, a second wireYears change
listener, and ++switching at app.js:1059 superseding the first opening fetch. A
check must resolve its injected fetch and drain microtasks instead. showYear is
the half worth exporting. Note also that `switching` is a `let` and the appended
export line snapshots its VALUE at load time, so a check must observe the token's
effect, never the variable.

THE CONSTRAINT THIS MUST NOT BREAK. harness.mjs:145-148: the appended export line
"is the ONLY difference between what runs here and what a browser runs, and it
adds no behaviour: it reads bindings that already exist." Do not add a top-level
binding to app.js for the harness's benefit. If a seam cannot be built without
one, that is a finding worth recording rather than a licence.

Node 22 is pinned in ci.yml so Promise.withResolvers is available for
deterministic sequencing. The sandbox is `{ console, Intl, ...stub }` -- there is
no setTimeout and no queueMicrotask, so any sequencing must be promise-based.
acceptance_criteria: run.mjs awaits its checks and an async check that returns a rejected or false promise FAILS rather than passing; loadApp takes a fetch and a config seam applied before runInContext; document- and window-level addEventListener record their handlers and matchMedia is stubbed; every existing layout.mjs check is re-run and still green after the matchMedia stub lands; fail()'s banner is reachable under jscheck, demonstrated by a check that goes red when the banner is painted and green when it is not; app.js gains no binding that exists only for the harness
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason: the bead that owns the unmet criterion is fisc-wcy, not fisc-o1i. fisc-o1i does not exist -- the id was written before the bead was filed and never checked back. The criterion is the one-selector-shape limit leaving buildTable() at its tbody guard and paint()'s legend-swatch loop iterating nothing.
close_reason:
loadApp takes fetch and config seams applied before runInContext (the only moment either can be installed -- app.js ends in main() at file scope); run.mjs awaits every check and turns a throw into a failed check rather than a crashed run; document- and window-level addEventListener record and matchMedia answers; fail()'s banner is reachable, because remove() detaches for real and an element's querySelector answers one selector shape for real. createTextNode was missing too, and its absence surfaced through main()'s own .catch AS A BANNER -- so a check asserting 'a banner appears' passed on the harness failing rather than on app.js reporting.

seam.mjs is the acceptance evidence and each check was verified to go red with its seam reverted: matchMedia to undefined, document listeners to a no-op, remove() to a no-op, the config seam removed, the fetch seam removed. The last takes three checks down at once, which is the measure of how much was unobservable.

Every existing layout.mjs check was RE-RUN after matchMedia became a function rather than assumed unaffected -- that was the criterion most likely to be skipped. app.js gained no binding that exists only for the harness; main and switching stayed out of NAMES for the reasons recorded in the file.

ONE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS NOT MET AND IS FILED, not quietly dropped: 'fail()'s banner is reachable' is satisfied, but the one-selector-shape answer leaves buildTable() returning at its tbody guard in every check and paint()'s legend-swatch loop iterating nothing. Found by /code-review while this landed. fisc-o1i owns it.

Landed in 8a4610a.

title: trend-series-are-complete cannot see a whole column vanishing from the corpus
description:
trend-series-are-complete (internal/check/trends.go, fisc-d5n) compares each series against the columns its projection was BUILT over -- Options.Columns. Trends.Slices derives those from the facts that survive:

  seen := map[Column]bool{}
  for _, f := range facts { if f.Scope == TrendsScope { seen[Column{f.FiscalYear, f.Basis}] = true } }

So the declared columns and the document's published columns are the same list by construction, and the check's coverage has a hole shaped exactly like that identity.

WHAT IS CAUGHT: a ROW dropped from ONE column. The other 230 series still carry that column, so it stays in Options.Columns and the short series is short a point in a known position. That is fisc-d5n's stated case and it is the one that arrives when a city reprints a schedule.

WHAT IS NOT: a WHOLE COLUMN vanishing. All 231 series lose FY2023-24 together, Slices returns three columns, every series is complete over three, and the check passes green over 231 subjects. counts.facts falls from 924 to 693 and counts.points with it, and nothing compares either against anything.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY FIXED HERE. The check would need to know what the corpus USED to hold, and there is no page that says so -- an expected-column list would be a constant nobody could justify off a document, which is the class of thing this project refuses (see the toCIP constants: every figure is read off a page, none derived). Two candidate shapes, neither obviously right:

  (1) A COVERAGE RATCHET. fisc-1wr.4 is exactly this idea for facts per (fiscal_year, basis, scope) and is deferred. A column count is the same species of claim and probably belongs there rather than in a second mechanism.
  (2) THE SCHEDULE'S OWN PRINTED COLUMN HEADERS. pp.127-140 print four column headings on every page, and the mapping rules already resolve against them -- a rule declaring four columns whose facts produce three is a discrepancy the MAPPING layer can see, and it can see it against the page rather than against history. That is a stronger check than anything internal/check could do from the fact store alone, and it may already be partly covered by CheckTotals.

Found by /code-review of the revenue-trends landing, 2026-08-25. The doc comment on trendSeriesAreComplete overclaimed on this point and has been corrected rather than left to be believed; docs/revenue-trends-contract.md says the same.
acceptance_criteria: a corpus that loses one of the four printed columns entirely goes red somewhere; the mechanism compares against a page or a declared floor rather than against an author-chosen constant; trend-series-are-complete's per-series arm and its tests are unchanged
notes:
2026-08-26 THE COLUMN HOLE IS CLOSED FROM THE PUBLISHING SIDE, by fisc-w7d. Whether that retires this bead is the owner's call; the arithmetic is here either way.

This bead's first acceptance criterion -- 'a corpus that loses one of the four
printed columns entirely goes red somewhere' -- is now met.
project.PublishedDocuments states that the site publishes revenue-trends over
project.TrendsColumns()'s four columns, and published-projection-built compares
that against the columns the corpus actually built, ONE COLUMN AT A TIME. A
corpus that loses FY2023-24 entirely now fails with 'the site publishes
revenue-trends (...) and it was built without FY2024 actual'.
TestAPublishedDocumentShortAColumnIsReported is the evidence, and it asserts in
the same run that trend-series-are-complete still PASSES -- so the bead's third
criterion ('the per-series arm and its tests are unchanged') holds by
construction rather than by inspection.

ON THE SECOND CRITERION, which is the one worth arguing rather than asserting:
'the mechanism compares against a page or a declared floor rather than against an
author-chosen constant.' TrendsColumns IS author-chosen. The claim is that it is
a DECLARED FLOOR in this bead's sense and not the constant it refuses, and the
distinction is what the constant is ABOUT:

  - The refused kind is a claim about WHAT THE CORPUS USED TO HOLD. No page
    states it, nobody could justify it off a document, and it is the class the
    toCIP constants are the counter-example to.
  - TrendsColumns is a claim about WHAT THE SITE PUBLISHES. It is the same
    species as PublishedFiscalYears() = {2026, 2027}, which is also author-chosen,
    also stated, also justified by nothing on a page -- because a publishing
    decision is not a reading of a document -- and has been load-bearing since
    fisc-kwq.

So the corpus can no longer contradict the site's own promise without something
going red, and the promise is a decision recorded in a commit rather than a
memory of a corpus.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, and it is this bead's option (2): it does not compare
against THE PAGE. pp.127-140 print four column headings on every page and the
mapping rules already resolve against them, so a rule declaring four columns
whose facts produce three is a discrepancy the MAPPING layer can see against the
document rather than against a declaration. That is still the stronger check and
still unowned. If this bead stays open, that is what it is for -- and it should
say so in its title, because 'trend-series-are-complete cannot see a whole column
vanishing' is no longer true of the run as a whole.
close_reason: Closed as covered, per the bead's own 2026-08-26 note and the plan's owner's-call default. Its first acceptance criterion -- 'a corpus that loses one of the four printed columns entirely goes red somewhere' -- is met by fisc-w7d's published-projection-built (internal/check/coverage.go), which compares project.PublishedDocuments against the columns the corpus actually built, ONE COLUMN AT A TIME. TestAPublishedDocumentShortAColumnIsReported is the evidence and 'fisc verify' prints the check green today over all three published documents. The third criterion holds by construction: that test asserts trend-series-are-complete still PASSES in the same run, so the per-series arm is unchanged rather than merely believed to be. The second criterion -- 'the mechanism compares against a page or a declared floor rather than an author-chosen constant' -- is the one worth arguing, and the bead argues it: TrendsColumns is author-chosen but is a claim about what the SITE PUBLISHES, not about what the corpus used to hold, which is the class the bead refuses. The stronger mapping-layer alternative (a rule declaring four printed column headers whose facts produce three) is NOT built and is not owned by any open bead; if it is wanted it should be filed fresh rather than kept alive here.

title: trend-points-tie-to-facts: every published point equals the fact it cites
description:
fisc-d5n opens "Separate from trend-points-tie-to-facts on purpose" and nothing owns the sibling it names. Filed 2026-08-25 while landing the revenue-trends slice.

WHAT IT ASSERTS: every point a trends document publishes equals the fact it came from, cent for cent, and cites that fact's own doc_id, page, offset and token. It is the trends analogue of link-values-tie-to-facts (internal/check/graph.go), which ties every link's value_cents to the sum of its fact_ids -- and it is the ONLY thing standing between the published series and the fact store, because a trends document has no nodes and no links and every graph check is silent about it.

WHY IT IS NOT link-values-tie-to-facts. That check sums MANY facts into one link. A trend point is ONE fact: no netting, no cell key, no sign decomposition. The comparison is 1:1 and the check is correspondingly stricter -- a point whose fact id is not in the store is a finding, and so is a point whose amount disagrees, and so is a fact in the projection's slice that no point publishes (the direction that catches a dropped row, which fisc-d5n's shape check catches for a dropped COLUMN).

WHY IT IS SEPARATE FROM fisc-d5n, in that bead's own words: one check is about VALUES and one about SHAPE, and a combined check would report "N of M" over two different units.

NON-VACUOUS AND GREEN THE DAY IT LANDS: 924 facts, 231 series x 4 points, measured on the committed store.
acceptance_criteria: every point in a trends document equals its fact's amount_cents and carries that fact's doc_id, page, offset and token; a point citing a fact id not in the store is a finding; a fact in the projection's slice that no point publishes is a finding; the check reports 924 subjects on the committed corpus; a deliberately mutated point goes red
close_reason: trend-points-tie-to-facts lands green over 924 points, both directions. It compares every field a point PUBLISHES -- amount, doc, page, offset, token, derived, column -- rather than the amount alone, because a point citing the right figure off the wrong page is a broken provenance link every arithmetic check passes; and it recomputes the SERIES id from the fact, which catches a point filed under a different printed row with every other field still agreeing. TestAMutatedPointIsCaught runs one subtest per published field.

title: export.Builder must return assets as well as projections
description:
pkg/cmd/export/export.go:33 declares

  type Builder func(repoRoot string) (map[string][]byte, error)

and exportRun never sets Options.Files. So the non-projection asset channel
fisc-ze7 landed is reachable only from INSIDE internal/export, where it is used
for cited page text -- the command cannot ship anything through it.

fisc-4ua.8 needs exactly that channel for the fact shards and the CSV, and
fisc-ze7's own text says to "build it once and use it twice". The second use
needs this signature to change:

  type Builder func(repoRoot string) (Result, error)
  type Result struct {
      Projections map[string][]byte
      Files       map[string][]byte
  }

Internal-only and small, but it ripples into export_test.go's runF seam, so it
belongs in the wave that needs it rather than landing speculatively ahead.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES fisc-4ua.8: assetPath (export.go:207) REJECTS anything
under data/. Shards cannot live beside the projections; put them at a top-level
facts/ and no guard changes.

title: trend-series-are-complete: every series has a point in every column, or a declared exception
description:
Separate from trend-points-tie-to-facts on purpose: one check is about VALUES and
one about SHAPE, and a combined check would report "N of M" over two different
units.

Measured on the committed store: all 231 revenue-by-fund series carry exactly
four points, and all 49 expenditure-by-department series do too. So this check is
non-vacuous and green the day it lands, which is the point -- it exists for the
day that stops being true.

THE CASE IT IS FOR: the city drops a printed row from one column, or adds a line
mid-book that only the later years carry. Either is a real event in a document
that reprints the same schedule every year, and neither is visible to a check
that only asks whether each published point matches a fact -- a missing point
publishes nothing to disagree with.

A series that legitimately lacks a column must be DECLARED, with the reason, the
same way unprojectedScopes declares a scope no projection draws. Fail closed: an
undeclared gap is a finding.
close_reason: trend-series-are-complete lands green over 231 series, incompleteSeries empty with both stale arms and a test that the map stays empty. The dependency on fisc-4ua.3 was right when filed -- the check needs a trends document to exist -- and is now satisfied by the producer half; fisc-4ua.3 stays open for the page. ONE CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S SCOPE, found by /code-review and written into the check's doc comment and the contract rather than left to be believed: it catches a ROW dropped from ONE column (the other 230 series keep that column in Options.Columns, so the short series is short a point in a known position) and it does NOT catch a WHOLE COLUMN vanishing -- Trends.Slices derives the columns from the surviving facts, so all 231 lose it together and every series is complete over what remains. Filed as fisc-7dt with two candidate shapes, neither of which is an author-chosen constant.

title: The projection envelope: what internal/project shares between documents, and what it must not
description:
internal/project's Metadata, Source, Counts and Headline are all declared in
sankey.go as Sankey's own types. A second document needs some of them and must
not inherit the rest. Decide which before two projections exist, because
retrofitting after three is the expensive version of this change (project.go's
own doc comment makes that argument about the Projection interface).

WHAT IS GENUINELY SHARED: Source, Counts's idea, GeneratedBy, Scope, Currency,
Units, Caveats.

WHAT IS NOT, AND THIS IS THE CRUX: Metadata carries FiscalYear (singular),
FiscalYearLabel, Basis (singular) and Headline. A four-year trends document must
carry NONE of those four -- it spans four years and four bases, and Headline's
keys are literally all_funds_gross_revenue_cents and naive_expenditure_cents.
Hoisting Metadata wholesale would hand every future document a fiscal_year it
cannot honestly fill.

THE BYTE CONSTRAINT, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS. testdata/sankey.golden.json
must stay byte-identical. The real guard is internal/project/sankey_test.go:51
(bytes.Equal), seconded by internal/export/export_test.go:186 (string compare).
pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go:441 decodes BOTH SIDES into map[string]any and
deletes generated_by before cmp.Diff, so it is SEMANTIC and would not catch a
field reorder -- do not lean on it for this.

Moving a type between files in the same package changes no bytes; encoding/json
emits fields in declaration order within a struct. ADDING a field to Metadata
does change bytes, and omitempty is forbidden here in three separate doc comments
(project.go, page.go, fact.go), so there is no quiet way to add one.

SO THE CANDIDATES ARE: (a) hoist Source and Counts verbatim, declare a separate
Envelope for non-spine documents, and accept two structs sharing several leading
fields; or (b) restructure Metadata by embedding, which reproduces key order
exactly but couples the spine document's shape to every future one. This bead
picks one and says why, and whichever it picks, a test must assert the shared
leading JSON tags do not drift apart.

ALSO IN SCOPE, because it is the one extraction the byte test genuinely earns:
hoist the encoder configuration -- HTML escaping off, two-space indent, single
trailing newline -- so a second projection cannot ship with escaping on and turn
"Fines & Forfeitures" into "Fines & Forfeitures".
close_reason: The remainder landed: Envelope in internal/project/document.go, envelope(), and TestSharedMetadataTagsHaveNotDrifted. Option (a) confirmed by measurement rather than taste -- Metadata's shared keys are INTERLEAVED with the spine's own (generated_by, fiscal_year, fiscal_year_label, basis, scope, currency, units, ...), so embedding Envelope there would reorder them and change testdata/sankey.golden.json. TrendsMetadata does embed it, which is what gives the contract's key order for free. Both key orders are now pinned by their own tests, so a reorder fails with a message saying what moved rather than only as a byte diff. The encoder hoist the bead called 'the one extraction the byte test genuinely earns' was already done in e129574 and is now covered by TestEncodeLeavesHTMLAlone. Counts share only their FIRST key with TrendCounts, and a test refuses a facts_cited on the trends side: /code-review found it equalled both facts and points, which is three names for one number.

title: Freeze the revenue-trends document contract before writing the Go
description:
A published document shape is a decision in this repository, not a bullet inside
the bead that implements it. fisc-oxf states the precedent: "The contract was
frozen in its own commit precisely so producer, packager and consumer could be
built concurrently against it. Changing it is a decision, not a bullet inside
another bead -- same precedent as fisc-j8f (YAML) and fisc-zna (d3)."

So docs/revenue-trends-contract.md lands first and alone, matching
docs/sankey-contract.md.

WHAT THE CONTRACT HAS TO SETTLE:

SERIES IDENTITY. Measured on the committed store: revenue-by-fund carries 231
series and EVERY ONE HAS EXACTLY FOUR POINTS. The identity is
(doc_id, rule_id, row_path, row_label, column_path) -- precisely fact.MakeID's
tuple MINUS (fiscal_year, basis) -- and that is not a coincidence: two facts are
the same printed row at different times exactly when they agree on everything the
id hashes except the year and the basis. Publishing series_id as the same sha256
construction with those two components held constant makes it stable when a fifth
year is mapped and re-derivable by anyone holding the facts.

EVERY POINT CARRIES ITS OWN BASIS, PAGE, OFFSET AND TOKEN. This is not
redundancy with the fact store; it is what lets a point be cited on its own and
what makes the comparability problem below visible in the data rather than only
in prose.

THE COLUMNS ARE NOT ONE MEASUREMENT. FY2024 is actual, FY2025 revised, FY2026 and
FY2027 adopted. The document must carry the basis per column AND a
comparable_group, so a consumer can enforce the distinction instead of reading a
caveat. It must NOT carry growth_cents, cagr or any inter-column arithmetic --
"never name a key for a concept the code does not compute", and growth from an
actual to an adopted figure is not a concept this project can compute.

AND FY2024 "ACTUAL" HERE IS THE BUDGET BOOK'S RESTATEMENT, NOT THE ACFR'S
AUDITED FIGURE. mapping.BasisAudited exists and is a different basis. The
contract must forbid this document calling that column audited; fisc-4ua.4 is
where audited actuals come from.
close_reason: docs/revenue-trends-contract.md landed, alone in its commit per fisc-oxf's precedent. It settles everything the bead asked for -- series_id as fact.MakeID's tuple minus (fiscal_year, basis), every point carrying its own basis/page/offset/token, comparable_group per column, no growth_cents or cagr, and FY2024 forbidden from calling itself audited -- plus four questions the bead did not raise and the code forced: fund_name (231 series over 70 funds and row_label is NOT unique across them -- 'Property Taxes' is printed by 4 funds and 'Use of Money & Prop' by 38 -- so project.Labels gains FundName); one schema_version spanning both contracts, versioning the ENVELOPE, with the cost stated; the stem rule for a document that is not a year of anything (Name() verbatim, never PublishedStem, which would write two byte-identical files one of which lies); and whether fisc-zl9's caveat is owed. On the last: it is, and the contract carries the full reconciliation rather than the one figure. Summing all 231 series into fund groups against p63 Table 2 ties EXACTLY in 20 of 28 cells, and every one of the 8 that does not is already filed -- general x4 is the missing GF Transfers In row (480,400/486,735 in the adopted years, owed to transfers-by-fund), capital FY2024-25 is fisc-zl9's 4,125,627, special-revenue FY2024-25 is fisc-94b's 500 (re-derived here from the opposite direction to that bead), and the two +/-1 cells are the FY2023-24 rounding class fisc-2sd declares. No series is wrong; the caveat exists because a reader who sums the document and compares it with the city's own summary table will find those differences.

title: Department pages: who pays for it, once the funding sources are mapped
description:
The second half of fisc-4ua.2 as originally written, split out because it needs
coverage that does not exist and the first half does not.

Once fisc-71j maps Department Funding Sources, a department page can answer the
question a resident actually asks -- what does Police cost and which funds pay
for it -- instead of the General-Fund-share-only version fisc-4ua.2 is now scoped
to. With fisc-7q6 as well, it can also state the department's whole cost rather
than the mapped divisions' subtotal.

The join is per page and printed: Total Department Funding Sources equals Total
Department Expenditures on each of the 14 pages, so the two sides of this view
reconcile against each other by construction rather than by our arithmetic.

title: Department Funding Sources, pp.85-125: the half of fisc-4ua.2 that answers who pays
description:
The "Department Funding Sources" block at the foot of each of the 14
departmentwide pages (p0085, p0089, p0093, p0097, p0101, p0102, p0105, p0108,
p0111, p0115, p0119, p0120, p0124, p0125) is what fisc-4ua.2's "and who pays for
it" actually needs, and it is extracted and unmapped.

Shape, from p0097 (printed p93):

  Department Funding Sources
  General Fund                    6,311,564  6,634,085  6,686,710  6,739,046
  Information Technology          6,474,390  7,068,328  7,505,369  7,555,789
  Total Department Funding Sources  $12,785,955  $13,702,413  $14,192,079  $14,294,835

Roughly 11 departments x 2-8 fund rows x 4 columns.

IT CARRIES ITS OWN RECONCILIATION AND THAT IS WHY IT IS WORTH MAPPING FIRST OF
THE TWO: on every page, in every column,

  Total Department Funding Sources == Total Department Expenditures

exactly. A schedule that proves itself on its own page is the cheapest coverage
in the corpus -- no cross-page arithmetic, no hand-typed figure, no tolerance.

The rows are FUND NAMES, so they resolve through data/funds.yaml the way
revenue-by-fund's do, and row-funds-match-their-anchors already exists to check
that a hand-typed fund number matches the name the page prints.

title: Departmentwide expenditures, pp.85-125: the divisions pp.167-170 do not print
description:
14 pages of the budget book print "DEPARTMENTWIDE EXPENDITURES WITH FUNDING
SOURCES" -- p0085, p0089, p0093, p0097, p0101, p0102, p0105, p0108, p0111,
p0115, p0119, p0120, p0124, p0125 -- and they are the whole department, not the
General Fund slice of it.

WHAT THEY ADD OVER pp.167-170, measured on p0097 (printed p93), Administrative
Services: five divisions where the fact store has three. Information Technology
($6,840,179 FY2025-26) and Cybersecurity ($665,190) appear on this page and in
NO fact today. Department total $14,192,079 against a General Fund share of
$6,686,710.

Same four columns as every other schedule in this book -- Actual FY2023-24,
Revised FY2024-25, Budget FY2025-26, Budget FY2026-27 -- so each row is a
four-point series with the same shape as revenue-by-fund and
expenditure-by-department.

ITS OWN SCOPE, not an extension of expenditure-by-department: these rows OVERLAP
that schedule's, so netting them together would double the General Fund
divisions. Same reasoning as fisc-u2v and the same fix -- a distinct scope with a
declared reconciliation rather than a merge.

THE TIE THAT MAKES IT PUBLISHABLE is printed on each page: Division Totals sum to
"Total Department Expenditures", and where a division also appears on pp.167-170
the two schedules must agree on the General Fund portion. Both are checkable
without leaving the corpus.

title: Checks for the scenario store: bases resolve, the method recomputes, derived is stated
description:
What `fisc verify` asserts over the scenario store, once one exists. Four things,
and the second is the one that makes the rest worth having:

1. Every base a scenario cites resolves to a fact that EXISTS in
   facts/facts.jsonl, and whose amount_cents is what the scenario recorded. A
   scenario built on a figure the city has since revised must go red, not stale.
2. The projected value is EXACTLY what the declared method applied to those bases
   produces, recomputed by internal/scenario and compared in integer cents. This
   is the independent-witness pattern the fact checks already use -- a hand-typed
   figure that has drifted from its own formula fails.
3. No scenario output reaches any published document without derived:true and a
   rationale. derived-nodes-justified already enforces this on the graph side; a
   sibling must enforce it on whatever document shape a scenario ships in.
4. The method is one of the closed set (fisc-cnf). Unrecognised is an error.

VACUOUS, NOT PASSING, WHEN NO SCENARIO EXISTS -- and declared as such, so the
declaration retires itself the day the first scenario lands rather than leaving a
green check nobody has exercised.

title: The closed set of forecast methods, and why an open set is unpoliceable
description:
fisc-nvw's condition for a forecast being checkable at all is that THE METHOD IS
EXECUTABLE BY THE VERIFIER. That only holds if the set of methods is closed and
each member is an integer-cents computation with a stated rounding rule.

Candidates, each needing a worked example proved against real figures before it
is admitted: constant; linear-from-two-actuals; cagr-over-n; pct-of-base.

THE ROUNDING RULE IS NOT A DETAIL. Amounts are integer cents and never float
(docs/agents/conventions.md), so a growth rate applied to a base has to say what
it does with the remainder, and two implementations that disagree by a cent make
the recompute check fail on correct data. State it once, per method.

AN OPEN SET IS UNPOLICEABLE and that is the whole point of writing this down: a
method the verifier cannot execute reduces the check to "the author says this
number follows", which is the class of claim this repository exists not to make.
Fail closed -- an unrecognised method is an error, never a passthrough.

title: internal/scenario: the derived store, its record type and its file format
description:
The second store fisc-nvw decides a forecast must live in, if one is ever built.

A scenario record is NOT a fact and must not be shaped like one. What it carries:
the fact ids AND locators of every published figure it derives from; the method,
a member of the closed set fisc-4x0 defines; the method's parameters; the
