So the citywide schedule already contains the CIP as a $38.1M transfer-out that goes NOWHERE unless CIP funds are modelled as nodes. The diagram does not balance without them. Bridge table is p222 ('CIP Project Fund (Receiving) / Operating Fund (Transferring)'); dedicated CIP funds are listed at p253-254.

TWO HARD FILTERS: only FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 are appropriated (the CIP's tables run to FY2030-45, which is planning intent, not budget); and the CIP's $141.3M two-year figure includes $35.2M of carry-forward (p211), so only the $106.1M of NEW appropriations is FY26+FY27 money.

title: ACFR as a separate function-axis view (scope: governmental-net)
description:
NOT a sibling in a year toggle -- it is structurally a different chart. The ACFR has three fund columns (General, Low Income Housing, Other Governmental), an expenditure axis by FUNCTION (Police, Fire, Public Works) rather than object category, ISF eliminated, and $55,286,695 of fiduciary custodial payments that are not the city's money (declare fiduciary out of scope with a note on the page). There is no object-category breakdown anywhere in the ACFR.

The UI must never offer a year-toggle between datasets of different scope. Label it as a different accounting basis.

title: All-funds toggle rendering tiers 0-3 with the constraint tier
description:
The General Fund is $144.7M of $254.1M (57%); the other 43% is water/sewer/airport ratepayer money, gas tax, impact fees, assessments and grants, almost all legally restricted. A single all-funds Sankey makes the visual claim that money pools and is then allocated, which is false for that 43% -- water rates cannot pay for police. So all-funds is a deliberate second click, and restricted funds render as a visually separated, labelled band driven by funds.yaml constraint_tier, not merely a different hue.

Also surface the Internal Service Fund double-count: ISF expenditures are $25,077,367 whose $18,969,834 of revenue is charges to other city departments, already counted inside those departments. The ACFR eliminates ISF activity; the Budget Book does not.
notes: 2026-08-18 THIS, NOT fisc-gxa.2, IS WHERE AN EARLY-RENDER ARGUMENT BELONGS. Landing plan wanted a visible milestone between the coverage lanes. fisc-gxa.2 cannot supply one after fisc-5gk.1 alone (see its note of the same date: within the General Fund tier 3 is a single node). But pp.131-140 print 'REVENUE SOURCES BY FUNDS / OTHER FUNDS' fund by fund, which does make a real tier-3 axis: data/funds.yaml already carries 112 numbered funds with constraint_tier, and fact.Fact.Fund int already exists (internal/fact/fact.go:72). So the all-funds tiers 0,1,2,3 view this bead describes becomes genuinely renderable once fisc-5gk.1 lands, without waiting for departments. If that ordering is wanted, argue it here and record the reasoning.

title: Tier 2: reconciliation with document-derived tolerance
description:
TIER 2 IS THE TIER FOR A COMPARISON AGAINST A FIGURE THE DOCUMENT PRINTED AT A
COARSER PRECISION THAN THE CENT. There an exact gate can NEVER go green: the
ACFR's MD&A tables are captioned "(in Millions)" and footnoted "Due to rounding
amounts may differ from what's reported on the financial statements"
(p0034.txt:32 and :56; p0036.txt:7 and :47 says it again as "Numbers might not
tie to financial statements due to rounding"). So any comparison against a
number PRINTED in such a source takes its tolerance from that source's own
declared precision.

THE TOLERANCE RULE. 0.5 x unit x n_terms, or ceil(n_terms/2) cents for
dollar-precision tables. Rules carry units: dollars|thousands|millions.

The tolerance is COMPUTED FROM THE PAGE -- from the printed unit and the number
of terms in the sum -- and is never a number an author picks. Two boundaries
keep it honest, and both are already load-bearing elsewhere:

  - `unit` is the LEAST SIGNIFICANT PRINTED DIGIT, not the caption's word. The
    ACFR MD&A says "(in Millions)" and prints tenths, so unit is $100,000. Read
    the caption instead and a four-term sum would carry $2,000,000 of slack.
  - The dollar-precision branch is deliberately far too tight to absorb the
    corpus's real dollar-level discrepancies, and must not be widened to. Budget
    Book p127's Total Property Taxes is a 13-row sum off by $1; ceil(13/2) is 7
    CENTS. That $1 is the city's arithmetic and is carried by fisc-2sd's
    stated_total_deltas -- a named declaration -- not by this tolerance. The two
    mechanisms are disjoint on purpose; neither is an escape hatch for the other.

THE TWO CHECKS.

1. MAPPED ROWS SUM TO THE TABLE'S STATED TOTAL ROW.
2. THE COMPUTED FUND-BALANCE RESIDUAL EQUALS THE DOCUMENT'S STATED CHANGE IN
   FUND BALANCE. This is the clause that turns a tautology into a real
   cross-check: sources minus uses is arithmetic over facts we mapped, while the
   printed CHANGE IN WORKING CAPITAL is a figure the city published independently
   of them. Nothing in internal/check does this today.

WHAT ACTUALLY NEEDS A DOCUMENT-DERIVED TOLERANCE TODAY: ONLY THE ACFR, AND THE
ACFR IS UNMAPPED. Measured off data/extracted 2026-08-22.

  - The Budget Book (268 pages) and the CIP (323 pages) contain ZERO occurrences
    of "(in millions)", "(in thousands)" or the word "rounding". Only the ACFR
    declares a coarser unit: seven MD&A pages captioned "(in Millions)" (p0034,
    p0036, p0039, p0041, p0042, p0045, p0046) and one Statistical Section page,
    p0170:8 "(In thousands)", Taxable Sales by Category, which belongs to
    fisc-4ua.4 and is blocked there on the non-amount-column decision.
  - The MD&A really does need it. ACFR p0034 Table 1, governmental activities
    2025: 729.2 + 38.2 - 280.1 - 3.5 = 483.8 against a printed total net position
    of 483.9. The Total column likewise: 1,085.6 + 43.1 - 321.5 - 14.2 = 793.0
    against 793.1. Four terms at unit 0.1 gives a 0.2 tolerance and the observed
    error is 0.1. The other four columns of the same table tie exactly, which is
    what makes these two the document's rounding rather than a misread.
  - The mapped corpus does not need it. The spine (pp.66-67, all 240 published
    facts) ties EXACTLY: both total_row rules -- "TOTAL REVENUES:" and "TOTAL
    EXPENDITURES:" -- pass at zero tolerance today, and the fund-balance residual
    ties in all twelve (fund group x budget year) cells. FY2026: general
    158,353,870 - 159,388,024 = -1,034,154 against the printed CHANGE IN WORKING
    CAPITAL; enterprise 3,894,384; capital -2,500,213; debt-service 0;
    special-revenue 8,874,949; internal-service -6,147,533. FY2027: 2,351,098 /
    1,410,280 / -10,129,416 / 0 / 9,021,972 / -7,160,645. So check 2 is
    implementable on today's facts at ZERO tolerance.
  - pp.127-140 tie exactly in both budget columns (fisc-u2v, re-derived twice).
    pp.167-170: the 49 object rows sum to the printed General Fund Total Expenses
    in ALL FOUR columns (123,228,190 / 141,120,420 / 144,650,802 / 149,014,579)
    and the FY2026/FY2027 category sums equal p66's Wages & Benefits
    81,801,011 / 83,825,633 and Services & Supplies 62,849,791 / 65,188,946, with
    Capital Outlay and Debt Services 0/0. Six INTERMEDIATE stated totals are off
    by exactly $1, all in the FY2023-24 Actual column: p168 Finance +1 and
    ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES TOTAL +1, p169 Planning -1 and COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
    TOTAL -1, p169 Public Works Administration +1, p170 Environmental Services -1
    (the last two cancel, so PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT TOTAL ties). Those are
    stated_total_deltas material, not tolerance material -- see the ceil(13/2)
    argument above.

CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT. On the corpus as mapped, both
surviving checks are TIER 1 -- exact, zero tolerance. The tolerance machinery
this bead is named for has no consumer until an ACFR page is mapped, and no bead
proposes mapping the MD&A. Under this epic's own governing rule (verification
work happens only when a page being mapped demands it) that makes this bead's
P0 wrong: it should be P2 and deferred behind an ACFR mapping bead that does not
yet exist. What is P0-shaped is the fund-balance residual check at zero
tolerance over pp.66-67, which is a genuinely new claim about the corpus and
could land in the tier-1 lane (fisc-1wr.1.1) tomorrow.

SCOPE OF WORK, IF WORKED AS WRITTEN. Units on Rule; a tolerance derived per
comparison from unit and n_terms; the two checks above registered at their real
tier; and a test that a tolerance one unit too tight goes red and one unit too
loose is refused rather than accepted. There is no code in this bead for the
expenditure side of the spine -- see the 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-22 notes.
notes:
2026-08-26 DEMOTED P0 -> P2 AND BLOCKED ON fisc-9hf, acting on this bead's own
2026-08-22 recommendation, which said the move was the epic owner's call. The
owner made it.

The argument is unchanged and is the bead's own, measured rather than argued:
every surviving clause wants a document-derived tolerance; the only source in
the corpus that declares a coarser precision is the ACFR MD&A; the Budget Book
and CIP contain zero occurrences of "(in millions)", "(in thousands)" or
"rounding" across 591 pages; and no bead proposed mapping the ACFR. Under this
epic's governing rule -- no check lands that no mapped page demands -- the
tolerance machinery had zero consumers and was heading `bd ready` every session
as the top P0.

fisc-9hf is now filed and this depends on it, so the deferral is a real edge
rather than a note nobody reads. The two dependent edges this bead's notes call
unjustified (fisc-1wr.3, fisc-1wr.4) are NOT touched -- same reasoning as the
2026-08-22 pass: removing an edge from a chain can un-block work that should
stay blocked, and that is a separate decision from this one.

title: fisc reanchor --accept
description: Bulk-rewrites integrity hashes after a reviewed extraction change. This is what converts an xberg bump from 're-anchor N rules blind' into one commit with a readable diff.

title: Schema-validation test over every committed data file
description: Every file under data/ validates against its schema_version. Runs in CI over the whole tree.

title: Determinism test: re-extract a fixture, assert byte-identical
description: Determinism is already confirmed empirically (ACFR run 3x, identical hashes); this test keeps it true. Note doc.tables order was stable across three single-machine runs but is not documented as stable across core counts -- the explicit sort in the serializer is what removes that dependency.
notes:
2026-08-22 THIS BEAD IS WRITTEN AGAINST THE RETIRED EXTRACTOR and needs
re-framing before it is actionable. Flagged while planning the backlog waves.

The description says "doc.tables order was stable across three single-machine
runs but is not documented as stable across core counts -- the explicit sort in
the serializer is what removes that dependency". There is no doc.tables. The
poppler migration (fisc-yqv) removed the table substrate entirely; see the
poppler-not-xberg memory: "There is NO table substrate and no Substrate enum".
So the specific determinism hazard this bead names no longer exists.

WHAT REPLACES IT is not nothing -- determinism is still a real property with
real hazards, just different ones. docs/agents/conventions.md states them:
"words sorted by position rather than by the tool's emission order, canonical
JSON with sorted keys, bboxes rounded to 2dp, atomic writes". Each is a thing
that could regress.

THE HARD CONSTRAINT this bead has to design around, and it is why the answer is
probably not a Go test: conventions.md says "Go tests never require Python, the
source PDFs, or the network", and re-extracting a fixture requires poppler AND
a PDF from LFS. So this cannot be `go test`. Candidates:

- a job in the monthly --full workflow (fisc-v87), which already takes the LFS
  cost and already has the PDFs checked out;
- a `make` target run by hand at extractor-bump time, which is when the
  property is actually at risk;
- a pure-Go test over the SERIALIZER only, feeding it synthetic word lists and
  asserting sorted output -- which needs no PDF and would catch the sort
  regression, though not a poppler-side change.

The third is the only one that fits the Go-tests-are-hermetic rule, and it
tests our half rather than poppler's. Decide which of the three (or which
combination) before writing anything.

Also worth stating: determinism was confirmed empirically at extraction time
(ACFR run 3x, identical hashes) and artifacts-match-manifest already guards the
COMMITTED artifacts against drift on every fisc verify run. So the gap is
narrower than the bead implies -- it is specifically "a re-extraction produces
the same bytes", which only matters at extractor-bump time.

title: rule-funds clause 2 claims totals per DOCUMENT and reports them per PAGE
description:
unclaimedFundTotals sweeps the pages a fund-bearing rule reads and reports every printed fund total no rule or rollup declares. Its stated claim is per page -- "on the pages a schedule maps, the schedule maps all of it" -- and its "claimed" set is keyed on (doc_id, printed label) with NO page dimension.

So one page mapped total silences an identical printed total on every other swept page of the same document, and an entirely unmapped fund section on a swept page goes invisible: the exact hole clause 2 exists to close.

MEASURED, and no collision exists today: rollup gf-total-revenues (page 130) claims "Total General Fund" for the whole document, and p0166 and p0172 print that same line. Neither is swept yet. But both adjoin pp.167-170, whose 23 division rules now declare fund: 100, so any rule whose parts reach p166 or p172 opens the hole.

AND 1148392 WIDENED THE EXPOSURE in a second way: the set(claimed, ...) call was moved ahead of both guards (correctly, for fisc-948), so rules that declare NO fund and rules whose columns declare two now also plant document-wide claims.

The fix is a page dimension on the key, which needs deciding where a rollup total is considered printed -- a rollup declares one page, a rule declares parts.

Found by /code-review of the drill-down branch, 2026-08-27, and independently by a second reviewer in the same run.
acceptance_criteria: a printed fund total on one page is not silenced by an identically-worded total claimed on another; a test with the same label on two swept pages reports the unclaimed one

title: [export] the trends page reconciles rendered cells against counts.points and prints counts.facts
description:
internal/export/page.go's buildTrendsPage compares the number of rendered cells against meta.Counts.Points, and the sentence that guard exists to protect prints a DIFFERENT number: revenue.html.tmpl:45 renders {{.Facts}} ('N figures in all'), fed from meta.Counts.Facts.

THE TWO ARE INDEPENDENT BY DESIGN AND THE CODE SAYS SO. internal/project/trends.go's TrendCounts doc comment states that facts is computed off the SELECTION and points off the series actually BUILT, and that 'a document that dropped a series publishes points below facts'. So a document with counts.facts 924, counts.points 920 and 920 rendered cells passes the reconciliation, exports successfully, and publishes a lede claiming 924 figures over a table carrying 920 linked ones -- the 'page whose own prose contradicts what it shows' the guard's own comment claims to have closed.

Two ways out, and they are not equivalent: reconcile rendered against Facts as well (the lede keeps its meaning and a dropped series goes red), or render Counts.Points in the lede (the sentence becomes true and the dropped series stays silent). The first is the one the guard's comment implies.

Found by /code-review of the drill-down branch, 2026-08-27.
acceptance_criteria: the number the trends lede prints is the number the packager reconciles against; a test drops a series and the export refuses

title: [bug] View.YearStems on a trends view is silently dropped, which is the trap the adjacent Lede rule refuses
description:
Found by /code-review of the fisc-rmx landing, 2026-08-27.

internal/export/export.go declares View.YearStems and Options/View validation refuses a Lede on any non-TrendsTemplate view -- a deliberate, documented refusal, because a field the template will not render is a caller's intent thrown away in silence.

YearStems has the mirror-image hole and no such rule. Only buildSankeyPage reads it; buildTrendsPage does not. So a caller setting YearStems on a TrendsTemplate view gets no year control, no error, and no way to tell which of the two happened. A trends document over four columns has no year to switch between -- fisc-qkh's close reason says exactly that, and it is why Options.YearStems became View.YearStems -- so the field is meaningless there, in the same way and for the same reason a Lede is meaningless on a Sankey view.

FIX: the same shape as the Lede refusal, in the same function, so a reader meets both rules together.

NOT INTRODUCED BY fisc-rmx -- that change rewrote yearStems' derivation, not its validation -- so it is filed rather than folded in.
acceptance_criteria: View.validate refuses YearStems on a view whose template does not render it, in the shape the Lede rule already uses; a test names the field and the template

title: A drill-down's tier-2 vocabulary is seven fund groups, not the spine's six
description:
docs/sankey-contract.md's tier table has one column, 'on the spine', and gives tier 2 as 6. A second document at another scope does not inherit that number.

MEASURED: revenue-by-fund spans SEVEN fund groups -- general, enterprise, capital, debt-service, special-revenue, internal-service AND permanent. pp.66-67 print no Permanent column at all, which is fisc-u8o. So a revenue drill-down folding tier 3 to tier 2 produces a fund-group node the spine document does not contain, and the two documents' tier-2 vocabularies differ by one.

internal/project's builtinLabels ALREADY carries 'fund-group/permanent' -> 'Permanent Funds', so the label is there and nothing fails. That is exactly why this is worth filing: the difference is invisible until someone compares the two charts and finds a column in one that is absent from the other, with no note anywhere saying which is right.

WHAT IT COSTS: the contract's table needs a column per document rather than a copy of the spine's counts, and site/app.js's FUND_ORDER is six ids -- a seventh group has no place in the measured colour ordering and no swatch, so buildLegend would skip it and linkColor would fall through to --muted. fisc-y0k's CVD re-run has to cover seven, not six.

Found in peer review of a landing plan, 2026-08-27.
acceptance_criteria: the contract states tier counts per document rather than only for the spine; a seventh fund group has a colour and a legend entry, or the document declares why it does not
notes:
2026-08-27 THE CONTRACT CLAUSE IS DONE (c94680a); THE COLOUR CLAUSE IS REFUSED FOR NOW, on evidence already in the tree.

docs/sankey-contract.md's tier table no longer carries an 'on the spine' column. It states that how many nodes a tier holds is a property of the DOCUMENT, names the spine's own counts separately, and says revenue-by-fund draws seven fund groups where pp.66-67 print six.

THE SEVENTH HUE MUST NOT LAND HERE. site/style.css:983-987 already says, in writing, that revenue-by-fund carries seven groups and that 'A seventh hue would invalidate a measured result' -- the six-hue ordering was chosen by enumerating all 720 orderings against a CVD validator, and app.js:157-165 pins the resulting figures. Adding a slot while fisc-y0k (the CVD re-run) is open would ship a palette whose own published measurements no longer describe it, which is the class of stale claim this repo files beads about. The drill-down is not rendered yet either, so the hue buys nothing today.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD: the seventh fund group's colour and legend entry, to land WITH fisc-y0k's re-measurement in one commit, or with fisc-f75 when the document first reaches a page.

title: ComparableGroup is the basis verbatim, so two separately-adopted budget cycles will read as one
description:
FOUND BY /code-review 2026-08-26. A trap for whoever widens the published
declaration, not a live bug -- filed so it is found before that rather than
after.

internal/project/trends.go sets ComparableGroup to string(c.Basis) verbatim. Its
own doc comment defines the field as "produced by the same process", and
caveatComparability tells readers the two later columns are "intentions adopted
together". Those coincide only while EXACTLY ONE budget book is mapped.

When the FY2027-29 book's revenue-by-fund pages land, Trends.Slices picks up
FY2028/FY2029 exhaustively and all four adopted columns get
comparable_group: "adopted" -- telling a consumer that enforces on that field
that FY2026 -> FY2028 growth is arithmetically legitimate across two separate
adoption events, which is precisely what the key exists to forbid.

WHY IT IS NOT LIVE: TrendsColumns() is stated rather than derived, and
PublishedDocuments()/MissingColumns make the widening fail closed first. So the
declaration has to be edited before this can fire, and whoever edits it is the
person this bead is for.

FIX: derive the group from (basis, doc_id) rather than basis alone. A budget
book is the adoption event, and the doc id is what names it.
acceptance_criteria: two adopted columns from different budget books carry different comparable_group values; a test pins the current corpus's four columns unchanged

title: Three missing guards in internal/export: an unlabelled nav link, an ignored YearStems, and an unreconciled printed count
description:
FOUND BY /code-review 2026-08-26, each reproduced by running the code. None is reachable through the committed views; all three are the shape this package already refuses elsewhere, which is what makes them worth closing. (1) A VIEW WITH NEITHER Nav NOR Title SHIPS AN EMPTY, UNLABELLED IN EVERY PAGE'S NAV. internal/export/page.go does `label := v.Nav; if label == "" { label = v.Title }` with no third fallback, and View.validate requires neither field. A second view {Path: "extra.html", Template: SankeyTemplate, Projection: "sankey"} -- the exact shape views_test.go uses throughout -- exports cleanly and puts `
    • ` into index.html: a zero-width link with no accessible name, on every page of the site. The package hard-refuses a Lede that would merely be dropped by a template; an unreachable nav entry is a strictly larger silent failure than the one it already guards. (2) View.YearStems IS ACCEPTED ON A TRENDS VIEW AND SILENTLY IGNORED, which is precisely the trap View.Lede is refused for. validate checks year stems only for existence, uniqueness and stems[0] == v.Projection; it never asks whether the view's template can render a year control, and buildTrendsPage never reads the field. A trends view with YearStems: {"revenue-trends", "sankey"} returns nil from Write: the extra stem's page text is shipped (buildSite collects its citations), no year control appears, no error is raised. (3) THE TRENDS LEDE PRINTS counts.facts, THE ONE COUNT NEVER RECONCILED. The template renders "{{.Count}} printed rows across {{len .Columns}} columns, {{.Facts}} figures in all", where Facts is meta.Counts.Facts copied through unchecked -- while the fisc-4j5 guard reconciles counts.points and counts.series, neither of which the page prints. A document with counts:{facts:999, series:1, points:2} carrying two real points is accepted, and the page reads "1 printed rows across 2 columns, 999 figures in all" while drawing 2. That is exactly the class the reconciliation's own comment names -- a published page whose prose contradicts what it shows -- arriving through the number the reader sees. RELATED AND ALREADY FILED: the fiscal-year distinctness guard the same review found (two year stems declaring one year emit duplicate id="year-2026" and mis-bound labels) belongs to fisc-rmx and fisc-b8o, which own the stem scheme.
acceptance_criteria: a view with no nav label is refused; YearStems on a template that cannot render a year control is refused; the number the trends lede prints is the one the reconciliation checks

title: Two jscheck checks pass for a reason their detail strings do not claim
description:
FOUND BY /code-review 2026-08-26, each proved by mutating app.js and watching
the check stay green. Same class as the three lifecycle checks 613888f fixed:
a harness that cannot observe what it says it observed.

(1) tools/jscheck/seam.mjs -- the `disabled`-attribute half of "a two-year
config gives the page a live year control" CANNOT FAIL. The stub's node()
(harness.mjs) starts with `attributes: {}` and nothing in the harness or the
template-id set ever puts `disabled` on the year-toggle node, so
`getAttribute("disabled") === null` is already true BEFORE app.js runs. Proved
by loading the harness with the default single-year config, where wireYears
returns at `years.length < 2` and never reaches removeAttribute: the probe
prints `change handlers: 0` and `getAttribute(disabled): null`. Deleting
`group.removeAttribute("disabled")` from app.js -- which would leave the toggle
permanently inert for every reader with JS on -- leaves this check green, while
its detail string asserts "the template's disabled attribute was removed". Fix:
set `disabled` on the toggle node at construction, since the template ships it.

(2) tools/jscheck/lifecycle.mjs -- "a document that lays out badly reaches the
last-resort catch" NEVER REACHES layOut, and the check's own printed detail
says so. The fixture supplies `metadata: { fiscal_year: 2027 }` with no
`sources` array, so drawableSankey rejects it at the metadata.sources arm before
layOut is called. The run output confirms it: the banner reads "...which
promises metadata.sources, and the file does not carry it", not a d3-sankey
`missing: not-a-node`. So the .catch on the change handler -- the thing that
block exists to keep reachable, per its own 14-line comment -- runs in ZERO
checks, and this check duplicates the metadata.sources one. Fix: add
`sources: []` to the fixture's metadata so it falls through to layOut.
acceptance_criteria: deleting removeAttribute("disabled") from app.js turns the seam check red; the lifecycle fixture reaches layOut and its banner names a layout failure rather than a missing sources array

title: The stylesheet's state indicators and its contrast numbers are pinned by nothing
description:
FOUND while landing fisc-8qx, 2026-08-26, and verified rather than assumed.

NOTHING IN THE TREE RENDERS OR PARSES CSS. tools/jscheck reads site/style.css only to harvest custom-property NAMES (harness.mjs, the FUND_COLOR_VAR check); no Go test and no jscheck module reads a declaration. The one CSS assertion that exists, TestTheDisabledYearToggleKeepsItsSelectionUnderTheCursor in internal/export/export_test.go, matches SELECTOR strings and is green through any change to what those selectors declare -- deliberately, and its own doc comment argues why a specificity calculator or a CSS parser would be worse.

WHAT THAT LEAVES UNPINNED, measured:

(1) THE MEASURED CONTRAST TABLE in the revenue mark's comment block (six ratios for --ink-2, --ink-1, --critical and --muted, light and dark). Changing any of those four tokens in any of the three palette blocks silently falsifies it. fisc-36r's commit called it 'pinned'; it is not, and that correction is where this bead starts.

(2) THE YEAR TOGGLE'S SELECTED STATE, as of fisc-8qx. The checked ring is var(--ink-2) at 7.11:1 light / 8.26:1 dark against the composited fill, and the hover fill is var(--wash). Setting them back to the same value -- which is the defect fisc-8qx fixed -- reddens nothing.

(3) THE THREE PALETTE BLOCKS AGREE BY HAND. :root, the prefers-color-scheme block and the [data-theme=dark] block define the same tokens; the two dark ones are byte-identical by design and nothing asserts it.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUS WHAT TO DO, which is why this is a bead rather than a patch. The honest options each cost something: a headless browser puts a second runtime on the check path that the node boundary in conventions.md deliberately keeps narrow; a CSS parser in Go is the second implementation of a browser thing jscheck refuses to write one layer up; and computing composited contrast in a test means re-implementing alpha compositing plus sRGB linearisation, which is small and real but only pins the arithmetic if the test also knows which rules apply to which element -- back to a selector engine.

A CHEAPER PARTIAL that may be the whole answer: assert that named PAIRS of declarations differ, by extracting two known rule blocks by their selector string and comparing the one property in question. Not a parser -- two string indexes and a compare -- and it would have caught (2) exactly. It cannot catch (1).

Note the cost of getting this wrong is not a broken build: it is a page that looks fine to whoever changed it and is unreadable to somebody else, or a comment full of numbers that were true once.

title: The year toggle's hover and checked states are the same colour, so hovering an unchecked pill looks like selecting it
description:
FOUND BY /code-review of the fisc-36r landing, 2026-08-26. Split out of that bead deliberately: it is a design change, not a bug fix.

site/style.css:327 gives '.year-toggle label:hover' background: var(--wash), and :346 gives '.year-toggle input:checked + label' the SAME var(--wash). So hovering an unchecked year gives it the checked background, and the only remaining discriminators are box-shadow and colour. On a two-option toggle that reads as two selected years under the pointer.

fisc-36r fixed the no-JS half (the checked pill losing its fill under the cursor) by narrowing the disabled suppression. This is the JS-ON half and needs a different answer: a distinct, weaker hover treatment.

WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A ONE-LINER: any new colour needs contrast numbers, and style.css:938-951 carries a MEASURED contrast table that -- verified -- nothing in the tree reads. jscheck never loads style.css and no Go test mentions it. So the numbers must be re-derived by hand and put in the commit body; do not treat that table as a gate.
close_reason: The checked pill's ring is var(--ink-2) instead of var(--rule): 7.11:1 light / 8.26:1 dark against the composited fill, where --rule was 1.60:1 / 1.26:1 -- BELOW WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 in both themes, which is why the ring could not do the work the fill had stopped doing. Hover and checked still share var(--wash); the ring is what tells them apart now. A weaker hover (--wash-weak at half alpha) was computed and rejected: 1.045:1 light against the checked pill while halving the hover affordance's own visibility, i.e. one indistinguishable pair traded for an invisible one. All six ratios re-derived by hand and recorded in the rule's comment. SHIPS UNPINNED and the comment says so -- nothing in the tree renders CSS; filed as fisc-6at.

title: paintYearWords hardcodes the packager's title prefix and overwrites a configured Title
description:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26.

site/app.js paintYearWords sets document.title to 'City of Livermore budget flows — ' + year.label, unconditionally. That literal is a second copy of buildSankeyPage's FALLBACK (internal/export/page.go:795), which applies only when v.Title == ''.

So give the Sankey view a Title the way the revenue view already has one: the server renders it into <title>, and app.js replaces it during the opening showYear, before the reader has touched anything. The caller's words are dropped without a word.

RELATED TO fisc-dbn item 2, which is about View.Lede on the same template, and probably wants the same answer: either the per-year title travels in the year document (it is per-year prose, and the packager already builds every year's words in Go), or View.Title is refused on this template the way Lede will be.
close_reason: The per-year <title> is built in Go and read from year.title. sankeyTitle is the one place the literal lives; app.js no longer composes it, so a caller's own View.Title survives the opening showYear instead of being overwritten before the reader touches anything. Refusing Title on SankeyTemplate was the first design and was rejected on peer review: the View.Lede refusal fires because index.html.tmpl renders no {{.Lede}}, and it renders {{.Title}} at line 6, so nothing is dropped and there is nothing to refuse. It would also have stranded buildSite's v.Nav fallback for this view.

title: lifecycle.mjs's refuseOpening defaults to a no-op, so a check can pass with the rejection it is about never occurring
description:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26, mutation-verified.

tools/jscheck/lifecycle.mjs declares 'let refuseOpening = () => {}' and only replaces it inside plannedFetch's settle callback for data/sankey.json. If that fetch is never issued, the callback never runs, refuseOpening(new TypeError(...)) does nothing, and 'a superseded fetch rejection paints no banner over the year that drew' passes with the rejection it exists to test never having happened.

Verified: gating 'await showYear(years[0])' off in main() leaves this check PASS (and defect 1's hang check too). seam.mjs is what actually goes red, so the run is not silent -- but these two checks are, and each is a claim about a state it did not reach.

FIX SHAPE: assert fetch.asked contains the opening path before calling refuseOpening, or make the default throw. Same species as the clickYear guards added in 5e96603.
close_reason: Three checks in lifecycle.mjs now assert fetch.asked contains data/sankey.json before asserting anything that depends on the opening fetch having been issued. The bead named two; there were three -- defect 1's block pushes a second check (the Escape dispatch) off the same state. Assertions rather than a throwing default: run.mjs turns a throw out of checks() into one 'a whole check module threw' and discards every other check in the file. Mutation-verified by gating 'await showYear(years[0])' off in main(): all three go red BY NAME and all 27 checks still report.

title: The disabled-state hover rule outranks the checked pill, so the no-JS year toggle loses its selection under the cursor
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26. A CSS specificity accident in the state the
page ships in.

site/style.css: `.year-toggle:disabled label:hover { background: none }` has
specificity (0,3,1) and outranks
`.year-toggle input:checked + label { background: var(--wash) }` at (0,2,2).

The fieldset ships DISABLED -- index.html.tmpl renders it that way and app.js
removes the attribute as its enhancement -- so with JavaScript off, or during
the opening fetch before wireYears runs, hovering the currently-selected year
erases the fill that says it is selected. What survives is the box-shadow ring,
and the comment beside that rule says in as many words that it deliberately does
not rely on the ring alone.

So the reader hovers the pill telling them which year they are looking at and
the answer disappears under the cursor, in the no-JavaScript state this project
otherwise defends carefully.

The rule was aimed at cancelling `.year-toggle label:hover` (0,1,2) and
over-reaches by one class. Narrowing it -- `:disabled label:not(:has(...))`, or
simply raising the checked rule above it -- is a one-line fix; the case to add
is a rendered-markup assertion that the disabled toggle still marks its
selection, since this is exactly the kind of thing that comes back.
acceptance_criteria: with the fieldset disabled, the checked year keeps its fill under the cursor; the hover suppression still applies to the unchecked pills; the fix is a narrowing rather than a raise of !important
close_reason: Landed in 2a31fc0. Narrowed to '.year-toggle:disabled input:not(:checked) + label:hover' rather than raising the checked rule: the suppression was only ever aimed at cancelling '.year-toggle label:hover' and over-reached by one class, so raising the other rule would leave the over-reach for whatever comes next. Verified by cascade: with JS off the checked pill keeps var(--wash) under the cursor while unchecked pills still lose their hover fill -- both halves of the bead's criteria. The assertion is a string match over the embedded stylesheet, NOT the CSS specificity calculator the plan called for: peer review was right that computing specificity in Go is what tools/jscheck refuses one layer up, and that it models only one axis of the cascade, so it would prove the arithmetic rather than the outcome. Mutation-verified. Correction recorded in the commit: the contrast table at style.css:938-951 is NOT pinned by anything -- nothing in the tree reads it.

title: README says the detail schedules are not yet drawn, and revenue.html draws all 924 of them
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26.

README.md says the detail schedules are "not yet drawn" and never mentions
revenue.html. Since 92e657f the site publishes a second page rendering all 924
pp.127-140 facts across four columns, each figure linked to the extracted text
of the page it was read from.

The README's NUMERIC claims were checked in the same review and are all exact --
1,448 facts, 21 pages, and the per-schedule 240 / 924 / 196 / 88. It is only the
prose about what the site draws that has fallen behind, which is the more
misleading half: a reader trusts the numbers and concludes the coverage is
unpublished.

Small, and worth doing when the next site change lands rather than on its own.
acceptance_criteria: README describes the two pages the site actually publishes; its numeric claims are re-checked against facts.jsonl in the same edit rather than assumed to have stayed true
close_reason: Landed in 27b37e0. Three stale prose claims, not one. (a) 'not yet drawn' corrected WITHOUT overcorrecting: revenue.html draws pp.127-140's 924, and the other two schedules (196 and 88) are still undrawn and are named. (b) The architecture diagram said 'one projection per (fiscal_year, basis, scope)', which Options.Columns replaced and which cannot express a four-column trends document -- found by review, not in the bead. (c) 'nothing has been pushed to it, so CI has never run' was false (origin/main is an ancestor of HEAD, fisc-ze7 closed); replaced with the push rule that IS true here. Numeric claims re-counted in the same edit as the bead required -- 1,448 / 21 / 240 / 924 / 196 / 88, all exact, so none moved.

title: trends_test.go's 'the values check must stay QUIET' block asserts nothing and its premise is false
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26, and reproduced.

internal/check/trends_test.go, inside TestASeriesShortAColumnIsCaught. The
comment says the values check must stay QUIET "or this test proves nothing", and
then:

  - THE BODY IS t.Logf, so the `if` cannot fail the test in either direction.
  - THE PREMISE IS FALSE. Running the same mutation
    (series.Points = series.Points[:1]) makes trend-points-tie-to-facts return
    FAIL with "...no point publishes it", because the dropped point's fact is
    still in factsFor(s.Facts, p.Options).

So the test proves nothing about the division of labour it names, and the
comment misdescribes shipped behaviour. Both halves are wrong in the same
direction, which is what makes it worth an id rather than a silent edit: the
division of labour between the two trend checks needs re-stating against what
they actually do, and then asserting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, as far as the reproduction goes: dropping a point from a
published series reddens BOTH checks -- points-tie-to-facts because a fact in
the slice is published by no point, and series-are-complete because the series
is short a column. That is redundancy rather than a division of labour, and it
may well be the right answer; it is simply not the one written down.
acceptance_criteria: the block asserts rather than logs; the comment states what the two checks actually do on a dropped point, verified by running the mutation rather than by reasoning about it; if the two checks genuinely overlap here, that is written down as overlap instead of as a division of labour
close_reason: Landed in the packager/check commit. buildCells now reports what it PLACED and buildTrendsPage reconciles that against counts.points, plus len(series) against counts.series, naming both numbers; two points in one column is refused separately because the counts still reconcile in that case. The check gains a column-membership arm -- measured as invisible to both existing arms, since comparePoint compares a point to its own fact and the reverse sweep filters facts on the same columns. Evidence is a GENUINE appended FY2027 point, with trend-series-are-complete asserted green in the same run. fisc-ewt's QUIET block now asserts, and records the two checks as OVERLAPPING on a dropped point rather than dividing labour, reproduced by running the mutation.

title: Three comments in the export path describe behaviour the code does not have
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26. Three claims in the tree that a reader would
believe and that are false. Grouped because the repair is the same in each case:
make the code true or make the comment true, and say which was chosen.
docs/agents/conventions.md names this class -- "a claim whose baseline no longer
exists in the tree cannot be checked".

(1) THE CONTRA ROWS ARE NOT RENDERED AS THE CITY PRINTS THEM.
internal/export/page.go's cellRef.Negative says the flag exists "so the
stylesheet can show it as the document does rather than as a minus sign in a
table", and site/style.css says "Rendering it as the city does keeps the page
and the page it cites saying one thing". The stylesheet only sets
`color: var(--critical)`. The built site renders -$14,086,438 where the page it
cites prints (14,086,438). NINE such cells ship. This one is worth fixing rather
than re-wording: the comments are right about why it matters.

(2) View.Lede IS SET AND NEVER RENDERED on the Sankey path.
internal/export/export.go says "Title is the <title> and the page heading. Lede
is the sentence under it." chrome.Lede is populated from v.Lede, but
site/index.html.tmpl contains no {{.Lede}} -- only revenue.html.tmpl does -- and
its <h1> is hardcoded rather than {{.Title}}. Verified: a spine view with a
caller Title and Lede renders the title in <title> only and drops the lede.
Harmless today because views() sets neither for the spine, which makes it a trap
for the next caller rather than a bug. Note paintYearWords then overwrites
document.title on any year switch regardless, so a caller-supplied spine title
does not survive a click either.

(3) AN UNREACHABLE GUARD, AND A TEST THAT COVERS SOMETHING ELSE.
internal/export/export.go's `case fixedPaths[v.Path], strings.HasPrefix(v.Path,
DataDir+"/")` can never fire: every fixedPaths key (.fisc-export, app.js,
style.css, .nojekyll) is caught first by the .html suffix check, and any
data/x.html by the root check. All six probed. views_test.go's case named "a
path that shadows an asset" (Path: "app.js") asserts "not an .html file", so the
shadowing guard the branch is named for is covered by nothing. Either the guard
must run before the suffix check -- so a shadowing path gets the message written
for it -- or it goes, with the suffix check's coverage of it stated.
acceptance_criteria: a contra cell renders as the cited page prints it, or both comments stop claiming it does; index.html.tmpl renders Title and Lede or export.go stops promising they are rendered, and the paintYearWords title overwrite is stated either way; the shadowing guard is reachable and its test asserts the message written for it, or the branch is removed with the suffix check's coverage stated
close_reason: Landed in 27b37e0. (1) CONTRA CELLS: the COMMENT was made true, not the code, reversing the bead's recommendation on evidence the bead did not have -- screen readers do not announce parentheses at default settings, so (14,086,438) reads aloud as POSITIVE, and the minus sign is the only direction signal for a reader not seeing the colour. Both comments now say the flag drives .contra (cell colour) and .mark-bar.contra (the bar hanging below the baseline, where direction IS geometric). (2) View.Lede: both symmetric fixes fail -- the spine's lede wraps a live #lede-year span app.js rewrites per year, and its <h1> deliberately differs from its <title>, so rendering {{.Title}} there would freeze the heading at the opening year. View.validate now REFUSES a Lede on a template with no {{.Lede}}. (3) The unreachable guard was MOVED above the suffix check, and views_test.go's shadowing case now asserts the shadowing message instead of pinning the arm's unreachability; a new case keeps the suffix check covered.

title: Client-side what-if: the marking rule, or it does not ship
description:
The reader-facing slider fisc-nvw calls "a third thing": arithmetic in the
browser over published figures, computed and discarded, never stored.

It is not a scenario record and not a fact, so no check can reach it. That makes
the MARKING the whole of the safeguard, and the bar is correspondingly high. The
result must be unmistakably the reader's own arithmetic: never citable, never in
a CSV export, never blended into a chart that also shows published figures
without the distinction being visible in the mark itself -- the same grammar the
Sankey already uses for derived, which is dashed AND diamond-marked AND named in
the legend, not any one of the three.

IF THAT CANNOT BE MADE UNMISTAKABLE IN THE UI, IT DOES NOT SHIP. That is the
decision this bead carries, and it is the reason the bead exists before the
feature does.

title: internal/check/fixture_test.go: testDocs's doc comment now sits on inlinePageDoc
description:
inlinePageDoc was inserted immediately after testDocss doc comment
(internal/check/fixture_test.go:208), so that comment now documents the wrong
function and testDocs has none. Mechanical; found by /code-review 2026-08-24.
close_reason: landed in 1f8c107, 056d355, 1ae566f; each defect reproduced with a test before being fixed

title: A wrapped_labels fragment sharing the leading gap with column headers is neither declarable nor omittable
description:
internal/mapping/resolve.go:562, in checkGap's leading-gap branch: a declared
wrapped_labels fragment is admitted only when the TRIMMED GAP EQUALS THE
FRAGMENT EXACTLY.

The branch's own comment says the leading gap is where a part's column headers
live -- which is why that branch exists at all, and why it refuses digits rather
than refusing text. So a page that wraps a label INTO that gap, beside the
headers, produces a gap that is header text plus the fragment, matches neither
the exact-equality test nor OmittedRows (which is about rows the DOCUMENT does
not print, a different claim), and the part cannot be expressed.

NOT REACHED BY ANY COMMITTED PAGE, which is why this is P3 rather than a
blocker. pp.127-140's straddle tail parts anchor on "FY 2026-27\n" and their
leading gap is empty; pp.167-170's wrapped labels (fisc-0cs) land BETWEEN rows,
not before the first one, and that path is the one 664d638 covers.

Worth filing rather than discovering: the schedules still unmapped are the ones
most likely to hit it. CIP pp.29-40 wrap project names and the ACFR wraps
account descriptions, and a fragment that cannot be declared fails closed --
correct, but with an error message that tells the author to declare something
the parser will then refuse.

Found by /code-review of the fisc-5gk.1 lane, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: a wrapped fragment in the leading gap alongside column headers is either declarable or refused with an error that says it cannot be declared here and why; a test carries the page shape

title: beginning + change - ending == 0 is asserted by nothing
description:
Found and MEASURED while closing fisc-4er, 2026-08-24.

THE CLAIM: for every (fund group, fiscal year) the spine publishes,

    fund-balance/beginning + fund-balance/change == fund-balance/ending

VERIFIED over facts/facts.jsonl restricted to all-funds-gross: it holds at zero
in all twelve cells. Three published cells per year per group, 36 facts, and
the identity between them is asserted by nothing today.

WHY IT IS NOT fisc-4er, which was closed as already satisfied.
TestPublishedSpineBalancesPerFundGroup (internal/mapping/mappings_test.go:253)
covers the RESIDUAL identity -- revenue + transfers in - expenditure -
transfers out - reserve increase == change -- and pins both sides to the
printed TOTAL SOURCES / TOTAL USES. It says nothing about beginning and ending,
which are two more printed cells on the same rows of pp.66-67.

SIZE: small. Both sides are in the fact store; this is a check or a test, not a
mapping change. Deliberately kept out of fisc-4er's scope because folding a
second claim into one assertion makes a failure ambiguous about which claim
broke.

title: A rollup may cover rules of different kinds or scopes, and nothing compares them
description:
Found reviewing the fisc-7fe fix, 2026-08-24, and deliberately NOT fixed there
because unlike the basis case it is not obviously wrong.

WHAT IS NOW GUARDED. CheckRollup compares the covered rules' bearer-part
columns element by element, on the EFFECTIVE basis (fisc-7fe, plus the basis
half found in review). validateRollups compares Units and Parts[0].Columns.

WHAT IS NOT. Rule.Kind and Rule.Scope are compared by nothing. A rollup may
cover an expenditure rule and a revenue rule, or a rule at all-funds-gross and
one at expenditure-by-department, and the sum is reported as a clean tie if the
figures happen to add up.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUSLY A BUG, which is the reason this is its own bead rather
than a line in that fix. p140's "Total Sources" is literally revenue plus
transfers in -- a printed total over two kinds. It is declared unassertable
today (fisc-wev), so nothing exercises the case, but it is the document's own
evidence that a mixed-kind rollup can be a real printed line rather than an
author error. Refusing it outright would be choosing a rule the corpus has not
yet asked for.

SCOPE IS DIFFERENT FROM KIND and may deserve the opposite answer. A rollup
summing a detail-scope total into a spine-scope one is the fisc-u2v doubling
mechanism at the rollup level: the two are the same money, so a tie there means
the arithmetic worked and the claim is still wrong.

WHAT TO DECIDE: whether scope must match (probably yes, and refusable at parse
time -- it needs no pages), and whether kind must match or must merely be
DECLARED when it varies, so a mixed-kind rollup is a statement rather than an
accident.

title: A wrapped label before a part's first mapped row cannot be declared
description:
internal/mapping/resolve.go:519-539. WrappedLabels is consumed in two places inside labelledValues: checkGap admits a gap whose trimmed text is declared, and a trailing fragment after the last row is admitted the same way. Both mark the declaration USED, and an entry the page never used is refused (resolve.go:532) -- which is the right shape, because a stale declaration is a claim about the page that has stopped being true.

THE GAP THIS LEAVES. checkGap's i == 0 case admits the text before the FIRST mapped row without consulting WrappedLabels and without marking anything used. So a wrapped label landing there cannot be declared at all: declaring it fails with 'is declared but does not appear between this part's rows', and not declaring it is accepted silently. The one shape where a fragment is invisible either way.

NOT TRIGGERED BY pp.167-170 AS MAPPED. All four wrapping division labels there put their HEAD in the section anchor and their tail between two rows, so every tail is declarable. It is reachable by anchoring differently on the same page: section 'Innovation &' leaves 'Economic' in the i == 0 gap.

ALSO IN THE SAME FIELD, and this is fisc-ekj: WrappedLabels is read only by labelledValues, so a declaration on a labels_from part is neither used nor stale-checked. The two are one fix -- decide where the field is consulted and make every declaration on every part either used or refused.

FIX SHAPE: have the i == 0 gap consult WrappedLabels and mark it used, keeping the current permissiveness for undeclared leading whitespace-plus-text only if there is a reason for it. Note that tightening it may make an existing part fail; check the spine's parts before landing.

Found by /code-review of the fisc-5gk.2 landing, 2026-08-23.
close_reason: Landed in 664d638 as one fix, per fisc-2jk's own framing. ekj refused at parse time on a labels_from part, with the bead's recorded p67 measurement re-run against the fix; 2jk's i==0 gap now consults WrappedLabels and marks it used, keeping the column-header permissiveness for a stated reason. Both proven red first.

title: A dangling $ late in a block is reported against the block's FIRST row
description:
internal/mapping/resolve.go:497. labelledValues calls

    dropCurrencyMarks(tokens(blk.Text[after:], blk.Start+after))

on the WHOLE REMAINDER OF THE BLOCK, for every row, and only afterwards truncates with `toks = toks[:ncols]`.

dropCurrencyMarks scans everything it is given, so a detached '$' sitting on the LAST row of a block makes the FIRST row's call return the error, and the message names that first row:

    row "Wages & Benefits": "$" is a currency mark with no figure after it

The reader then goes and looks at a row that is perfectly fine. The check itself is right -- a bare '$' must never be silently dropped, which is what dde657b landed it for -- and only the attribution is wrong.

FIX: truncate before checking, or pass dropCurrencyMarks the row's own span. Careful: the truncation currently depends on the currency marks having been removed first (a '$' would otherwise occupy one of the ncols slots), so the two cannot simply be swapped -- the row's span has to be found some other way, e.g. by dropping marks lazily until ncols figures are in hand.

TEST: a block whose last row carries a detached '$' must name the LAST row. A test with a single row, or with the mark on the first row, passes either way.

Found by /code-review of the fisc-o15 landing, 2026-08-23, and verified against the source.

title: CheckRollup panics on a rollup with no covers instead of erroring
description:
internal/mapping/resolve.go:988 and :977 index `rules[0]` with no length check. `coveredRules` returns an empty slice for a Rollup whose `covers` is empty, so CheckRollup panics with index out of range rather than returning an error.

WHY IT IS UNREACHABLE TODAY, and why that is not the same as safe. Two things keep it so, and neither is CheckRollup's own: parse.go refuses a rollup that declares neither covers nor unassertable, and pkg/cmd/build/report.go:194-199 skips CheckRollup entirely for an unassertable one. CheckRollup is EXPORTED, so a second caller -- a verify-side structural sweep (fisc-1wr.5) is the obvious one -- reintroduces the panic by doing nothing wrong.

This is the same class as the panic fisc-3bl already fixed in this function (column width taken from Parts[0] where the totals came from a later part). That one was reachable; this one is one caller away.

FIX: return a ResolveError naming the rollup when len(rules) == 0, before either index.

Found by /code-review of the fisc-o15 landing, 2026-08-23, and verified against the source.
close_reason: Landed in a3adb0e. fisc-7fe fixed element-wise on the EFFECTIVE basis (the Column.Basis override half was found in review of the fix); fisc-7a6 fixed at both sites, its premise corrected on the bead first; fisc-t9h guarded before both rules[0] indexes. Each test proven red against the prior code. Kind/scope left uncompared and filed separately.

title: [bug] registry.Alias's doc comment carries two concatenated intros, and the stale half names the wrong field
description:
internal/registry/registry.go:92. The Alias doc comment has two intros joined from a bad merge. The surviving-but-stale half attributes the evidence role to Note -- which is unvalidated and read by nothing -- rather than to Rationale, which validateFundAlias actually enforces.

Not a behaviour bug: the code is right and the comment is wrong. It matters because the comment is the thing a rule author reads when deciding where to put the page citation for an alias, and it currently points them at the field that will not be checked. That is the same shape as a declaration that cannot fail.

Found by /code-review over the fisc-3bl work, 2026-08-23. Not fixed there because it is in a package that lane does not touch and bundling it would have hidden it.
close_reason: landed in 1f8c107, 056d355, 1ae566f; each defect reproduced with a test before being fixed

title: Spine rule merge: a kind filter on the total_row declaration, five rules to three
description:
This is the work fisc-uli was ORIGINALLY written for, separated from Row.Kind
because fisc-uli's own 2026-08-21 correction shows the two want opposite things
from CheckTotals.

THE SAVING. The p66-67 spine needs five rules where three would do, because Kind
is per-Rule and the transfers and fund-balance rows share a printed block with
the expenditure rows. Each rule re-declares the whole block with skip: true on
the rows it does not own -- correct and fail-closed, but verbose and easy to get
wrong in review. mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml carries five rules
over ten parts for this reason.

WHY IT IS NOT PART OF Row.Kind. Merging spine-revenues (total_row
"TOTAL REVENUES:") with spine-transfers-in gives a rule whose printed total
covers ONLY the revenue rows, so the merged rule needs CheckTotals to sum BY
KIND. But fisc-5gk.1's eleven mixed fund blocks on pp.131-140 print a total that
covers BOTH kinds, and there CheckTotals' existing kind-BLINDNESS is exactly
what is wanted. A globally kind-aware CheckTotals makes p131's Airport block
stop tying to Total Airport (which includes Transfers In 3,247,000) and fails
all eleven.

THE RESOLUTION fisc-uli records: the kind filter belongs on the total_row
DECLARATION, not on CheckTotals globally. A total row is the thing that knows
which rows it covers, and saying so is a claim the rule author makes and review
can check -- the same shape as Column.Basis overriding Rule.Basis on the COLUMN,
the thing that knows.

SO THIS BEAD IS: a kind filter on the total_row declaration, plus the spine rule
merge it enables. Row.Kind itself is fisc-uli and lands with CheckTotals
untouched.

NOT URGENT. Nothing is blocked on it -- the five-rule spine is correct today and
the eleven mixed blocks work with kind-blind CheckTotals. This is a readability
and review-surface saving, which is what fisc-uli was before the fisc-u2v design
pass promoted its other half.

THE PROOF IT IS SAFE, when done: facts.jsonl byte-identical. A rule merge that
moves a fact has changed a published claim, because rule_id is in fact.MakeID's
tuple -- so this cannot be done without re-anchoring, and that cost belongs in
the estimate.
acceptance_criteria: a total_row declaration may name the kinds it covers; the spine's five rules become three; the eleven mixed fund blocks on pp.131-140 still tie under kind-blind totals; the facts.jsonl diff is exactly the rule_id changes the merge forces and nothing else

title: Cross-part column_headers agreement will need relaxing for a page with two grids
description:
fisc-yqv.2's parser requires every part reading a page of a document to declare
the SAME column_headers, and requires them all to opt in or none to. It catches a
real failure: the published spine writes one page's header list out five times,
and a drifted copy would build a different grid for the same page in one rule
than in another, with both reads still tying against their own printed totals.

But a page that prints two schedules side by side with different grids is not a
defect, and the check refuses one. No page in this corpus does yet; the CIP is
the obvious candidate. When one appears, the grouping key has to become finer
than (doc_id, page) -- probably the header line itself -- without losing the
drifted-copy catch.

See checkColumnGrids in internal/mapping/parse.go.
acceptance_criteria: a page printing two schedules with different grids can be mapped; the drifted-copy failure the check exists for is still caught

title: column_headers_ordinal, when a page forces it
description:
fisc-yqv.2's design specified column_headers_ordinal, mirroring section_ordinal.
It was dropped, measured: the full ordered header sequence occurs exactly ONCE
page-wide on 66, 67, 127, 128-140, 167, 168, 169, 170, CIP 40 and CIP 29, with
zero unconsumed words right of the first match on every one.

An ordered multi-entry sequence is a far stronger anchor than the single
substrings section_ordinal exists for ("REVENUES:" genuinely occurs twice on p66).
Shipping five validation branches and a selection branch no fixture could reach,
inside the guard everything else now trusts, was the worse trade.

Today an ambiguous header line is a refusal that names the candidate lines and
hints that no ordinal exists. Add the key when a real page forces it, WITH that
page as the fixture.
acceptance_criteria: the page that forces it is named, is committed as a fixture, and the ordinal's selection and validation branches are exercised by it

title: data/sources.yaml has two readers; pkg/cmd/export keeps its own
description:
internal/registry.LoadSources (fisc-1wr.5, lane A4) is now the strict, schema-gated reader of the whole source registry: it declares every key, so a key added to the file without being declared is a load failure rather than a silently dropped claim. pkg/cmd/export/data.go still carries sourceRegistry, a narrow non-validating view of four fields (id, title, publisher, url) used to build the site's citation targets.

Consolidating means loadDocs calls registry.LoadSources and maps Source -> export.Doc, which deletes a yaml.Unmarshal and a struct. It was deliberately NOT done in A4 for one reason worth recording: LoadSources validates sha256 and bytes, so `fisc export` would start refusing to run over a registry entry that carries no hash -- a behaviour change to the publishing path, in a lane about verification. pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go's fakeRepo would also have to grow file/bytes/sha256 fields it does not read.

Do it as its own change, with a decision about whether export should require the integrity fields (probably yes: a source the site cites with no recorded hash is a citation nobody can check).

title: Permanent Funds are a seventh fund type with no spine column
description: data/funds.yaml has 7 type values; the pp.66-67 schedule prints 6 columns. type: permanent covers 2 funds (470 Doolan Canyon Preserve Endowment, 471 Doolan Canyon Open Space) and no column on the citywide spine accounts for them. Column totals tie regardless because the check is per-column, not a partition check over all 112 funds -- so nothing currently notices. Establish where those funds land in the citywide roll-up before any check claims the spine partitions the fund list.
notes:
2026-08-18 FIRST PUBLISHED MONEY for the seventh fund type: Budget Book p76 prints a 'Permanent Funds' DESTINATION section -- 'Transfer From Open Space to Doolan Canyon Preserve Endow', 19,533 in FY2023-24 and '-' in the other three columns. So the schedule that has no Permanent column on pp.66-67 does carry a Permanent row one page group over, and p76's grand total spans a fund group the spine does not print. It nets to zero for FY2026 and FY2027, which is why p76's budget columns still tie to the spine exactly; it would NOT tie if the historical columns were ever mapped. Found reconciling p76 (fisc-5gk.3).
2026-08-21 NOW EVIDENCED RATHER THAN SUSPECTED, from the fisc-u2v design pass.
Budget Book p134 prints the Permanent Funds section as `Doolan Canyon Preserve
Endow` (data/funds.yaml fund 470, name truncated on the page -- see fisc-8dz).
It is TRANSFERS-ONLY and ZERO in both budget years, FY2025-26 and FY2026-27.

That matters twice over.

FIRST, it is why fisc-u2v's revenue-detail-ties-to-spine can be an exact
identity. pp.127-140 reproduce the whole revenue side of pp.66-67 to the cent
for all six fund groups -- and Permanent Funds, which pp.66-67 have no column
for, is the one section that could have broken the tie. It does not, because it
is zero in exactly the years reconciled.

SECOND, it makes the seventh-fund-type problem DEFERRABLE ON EVIDENCE rather
than merely unaddressed: nothing is being dropped from a published figure today.
The condition under which that stops being true is stated and checkable -- the
section becoming non-zero in a budget column.

So the reconciliation check should assert permanent is zero in the reconciled
years AND non-zero in FY2024, the way transfers_p76_test.go pins the residual:
the check then reddens if the page stops evidencing this bead, instead of
silently absorbing the change. Do not write it as a blanket exclusion of the
permanent fund type.
